uttareṇa purī ramyā somasyoktā vibhāvarī .. 15 ..
1.7.d:
अनन्तरं शिवा नाम पुरी वायोः प्रकीर्तिता ॥
उत्तरेण पुरी रम्या सोमस्योक्ता विभावरी ॥ 15 ॥
1.7.m: Next, the city named Śivā is celebrated for Vāyu; / in the north, the delightful city named Vibhāvarī is declared for Soma.

1.7.s:
anantaraṃ śivasyoktā nagarī śaṅkarī śivā ...
merupṛṣṭhe yathā devāḥ saṃśritāstu yathādiśam .. 16 ..
1.7.d:
अनन्तरं शिवस्योक्ता नगरी शङ्करी शिवा ॥।
मेरुपृष्ठे यथा देवाः संश्रितास्तु यथादिशम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.7.m: Next, the auspicious city Śaṅkarī is declared for Śiva. / In this manner the gods reside on the summit of Meru, according to their directions.

1.7.s:
vijñeyāste tu dikpālāstasyāṃtasyāṃ tathā diśi ..
devaḥ svāṃ nagarī nityaṃ mānasottaramūrdhani .. 17 ..
1.7.d:
विज्ञेयास्ते तु दिक्पालास्तस्यांतस्यां तथा दिशि ॥
देवः स्वां नगरी नित्यं मानसोत्तरमूर्धनि ॥ 17 ॥
1.7.m: They should be known as the guardians of the directions in each respective direction. / The lord constantly [views] his own city on the summit of Mānasottara;

1.7.s:
meruntu paśyati vibhustatstho merugatāṃ purīm ..
udakśṛṅgavato'rdhe tu yāmyena kurusaṃjñitam .. 18 ..
1.7.d:
मेरुन्तु पश्यति विभुस्तत्स्थो मेरुगतां पुरीम् ॥
उदक्शृङ्गवतोऽर्धे तु याम्येन कुरुसंज्ञितम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.7.m: situated there, the ruler looks upon Meru and the city situated on Meru. / North of the Śṛṅgavān half and to the south is the region named Kuru,

1.7.s:
varṣantu kathitaṃ divyaṃ sarvopadravavarjitam ..
śṛṅgavacchvetayormadhye varṣaṃ jñeyaṃ hiraṇyabham .. 19 ..
1.7.d:
वर्षन्तु कथितं दिव्यं सर्वोपद्रववर्जितम् ॥
शृङ्गवच्छ्वेतयोर्मध्ये वर्षं ज्ञेयं हिरण्यभम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.7.m: declared to be a divine realm, free from all afflictions. / Between Śṛṅgavān and Śveta, the realm should be known as shining like gold.

1.7.s:
ramyantu varṣaṃ vijñeyaṃ madhyataḥ śvetanīlayoḥ ..
madhye niṣadhanīlābhyāṃ paścārdhe gandhamādanaḥ .. 1.7.20 ..
1.7.d:
रम्यन्तु वर्षं विज्ञेयं मध्यतः श्वेतनीलयोः ॥
मध्ये निषधनीलाभ्यां पश्चार्धे गन्धमादनः ॥ 1.7.20 ॥
1.7.m: The delightful realm should be known to lie between Śveta and Nīla. / Between Niṣadha and Nīla, in the western half, is Gandhamādana.

1.7.s:
ketumālaḥ smṛto varṣastvatīva sumanoharaḥ ..
madhye niṣadhanīlābhyāṃ pūrve mālyavato gireḥ .. 21..
1.7.d:
केतुमालः स्मृतो वर्षस्त्वतीव सुमनोहरः ॥
मध्ये निषधनीलाभ्यां पूर्वे माल्यवतो गिरेः ॥ 21॥
1.7.m: The realm is known as Ketumāla, exceedingly charming. / Between Niṣadha and Nīla, east of Mount Mālyavān,

1.7.s:
varṣo rudramukho nāma nityaṃ mudita mānavaḥ ..
meroścaturdiśaṃ nāmnā varṣo rājannilāvṛtaḥ .. 22 ..
1.7.d:
वर्षो रुद्रमुखो नाम नित्यं मुदित मानवः ॥
मेरोश्चतुर्दिशं नाम्ना वर्षो राजन्निलावृतः ॥ 22 ॥
1.7.m: is the realm named Rudramukha, where men are ever joyful. / Around Meru on all four sides, O king, is the realm named Ilāvṛta.

1.7.s:
tasyāpi bhedāścatvāro nāmatastānnibodha me ..
bhadrāśvo jambumālaśca ketumānkuravastathā .. 23 ..
1.7.d:
तस्यापि भेदाश्चत्वारो नामतस्तान्निबोध मे ॥
भद्राश्वो जम्बुमालश्च केतुमान्कुरवस्तथा ॥ 23 ॥
1.7.m: It also has four divisions; learn them from me by name: / Bhadrāśva, Jambūmāla, Ketumān, and also the Kurus.

1.7.s:
jambūvṛkṣastu vikhyāto jambumāle tu yādava! ..
yojanānāṃ sahasraṃ tu tatpūrvaṃ tasya kīrtitam .. 24 ..
1.7.d:
जम्बूवृक्षस्तु विख्यातो जम्बुमाले तु यादव! ॥
योजनानां सहस्रं तु तत्पूर्वं तस्य कीर्तितम् ॥ 24 ॥
1.7.m: The rose-apple tree is renowned in Jambūmāla, O Yādava; / its measure was previously declared to be a thousand yojanas.

1.7.s:
tatphalebhyaḥ prabhavati ramyā jāṃbūnadī śubhā ..
meroḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā svamūle sā ca naśyati .. 25 ..
1.7.d:
तत्फलेभ्यः प्रभवति रम्या जांबूनदी शुभा ॥
मेरोः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा स्वमूले सा च नश्यति ॥ 25 ॥
1.7.m: From its fruits flows the delightful, auspicious river Jāmbūnadī; / having circumambulated Meru, it disappears at its own base.

1.7.s:
vṛkṣarājena tenedaṃ jambūdvīpaṃ pracakṣate ..
ilāvṛtastu prabhayā mero nityaṃ prakāśate .. 26 ..
1.7.d:
वृक्षराजेन तेनेदं जम्बूद्वीपं प्रचक्षते ॥
इलावृतस्तु प्रभया मेरो नित्यं प्रकाशते ॥ 26 ॥
1.7.m: From that king of trees this [realm] is called Jambūdvīpa. / Ilāvṛta constantly shines with the radiance of Meru.

1.7.s:
na tatra bhrājate sūryo na candro na ca tārakāḥ ..
meroḥ śarāvasaṃsthatvānnityameva tirohitaḥ .. 27 ..
1.7.d:
न तत्र भ्राजते सूर्यो न चन्द्रो न च तारकाः ॥
मेरोः शरावसंस्थत्वान्नित्यमेव तिरोहितः ॥ 27 ॥
1.7.m: Neither sun nor moon nor stars shine there; / because it stands in the basin of Meru, it is always concealed.

1.7.s:
hemakūṭāduttarato harivarṣaṃ pracakṣate ..
hemakūṭāddakṣiṇatastathā kiṃpuruṣaṃ smṛtam .. 28 ..
1.7.d:
हेमकूटादुत्तरतो हरिवर्षं प्रचक्षते ॥
हेमकूटाद्दक्षिणतस्तथा किंपुरुषं स्मृतम् ॥ 28 ॥
1.7.m: North of Hemakūṭa, they declare Harivarṣa; / south of Hemakūṭa is known Kiṃpuruṣa.

1.7.s:
himācalāddakṣiṇato varṣaṃ yādava bhāratam ..
karmabhūmirmahīpāla yatra vartāmahe vayam .. 29 ..
1.7.d:
हिमाचलाद्दक्षिणतो वर्षं यादव भारतम् ॥
कर्मभूमिर्महीपाल यत्र वर्तामहे वयम् ॥ 29 ॥
1.7.m: South of the Snowy Mountain, O Yādava, is the realm Bhārata, / the land of action, O protector of the earth, in which we dwell.

1.7.s:
bhārate'sminyugāvasthā keśavena vinirmitā ..
varṣe dve cātha saṃsthāne vijñeye dakṣiṇottare .. 1.7.30 ..
1.7.d:
भारतेऽस्मिन्युगावस्था केशवेन विनिर्मिता ॥
वर्षे द्वे चाथ संस्थाने विज्ञेये दक्षिणोत्तरे ॥ 1.7.30 ॥
1.7.m: In this Bhārata, the order of the ages was established by Keśava. / Two realms are to be known situated in the south and north.

1.7.s:
varṣatrayaṃ tu vijñeyaṃ caturasraṃ tu madhyamam ..
dīrghaṃ tathaiva vijñeyaṃ varṣāṇāṃ ca catuṣṭayam .. 31 ..
1.7.d:
वर्षत्रयं तु विज्ञेयं चतुरस्रं तु मध्यमम् ॥
दीर्घं तथैव विज्ञेयं वर्षाणां च चतुष्टयम् ॥ 31 ॥
1.7.m: Three middle realms are to be known as quadrangular, / and likewise four realms are to be known as oblong.

1.7.s:
varṣāṇāṃ navasāhasro viṣkambhaḥ kathito nṛpa ..
yojanānāṃ pramāṇena kathitastattvadarśibhiḥ .. 32 ..
1.7.d:
वर्षाणां नवसाहस्रो विष्कम्भः कथितो नृप ॥
योजनानां प्रमाणेन कथितस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥ 32 ॥
1.7.m: The width of the realms is declared to be nine thousand, O king, / in the measure of yojanas, as spoken by the seers of truth.

1.7.s:
viṣkambhaḥ parvatānāṃ tu sahasradvitayaṃ smṛtam ..
meroryojanasāhasro viṣkambhaḥ kathitastathā .. 33 ..
1.7.d:
विष्कम्भः पर्वतानां तु सहस्रद्वितयं स्मृतम् ॥
मेरोर्योजनसाहस्रो विष्कम्भः कथितस्तथा ॥ 33 ॥
1.7.m: The width of the mountains is known to be two thousand [yojanas]; / and the width of Meru is declared to be a thousand yojanas.

1.7.s:
yojanānāṃ tu niyutaṃ jambūdvīpaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
yāmyottareṇa tasyedaṃ pramāṇaṃ te mayeritam .. 34 ..
1.7.d:
योजनानां तु नियुतं जम्बूद्वीपः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
याम्योत्तरेण तस्येदं प्रमाणं ते मयेरितम् ॥ 34 ॥
1.7.m: Jambūdvīpa is proclaimed to be one hundred thousand yojanas. / This extent from south to north has been told to you by me.

1.7.s:
pūrvāpareṇa tasyāpi pramāṇaṃ śṛṇu pārthiva ..
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi dvātriṃśacca śatāni ca .. 35 ..
1.7.d:
पूर्वापरेण तस्यापि प्रमाणं शृणु पार्थिव ॥
योजनानां सहस्राणि द्वात्रिंशच्च शतानि च ॥ 35 ॥
1.7.m: Hear also its measure from east to west, O ruler of the earth: / thirty-two thousand and one hundred yojanas

1.7.s:
bhadrāśvaketumālau dvau pratyekaṃ pārthivottama ..
yojanānāṃ sahasreṇa śatasāhasrakāni ca .. 36 ..
1.7.d:
भद्राश्वकेतुमालौ द्वौ प्रत्येकं पार्थिवोत्तम ॥
योजनानां सहस्रेण शतसाहस्रकानि च ॥ 36 ॥
1.7.m: for Bhadrāśva and Ketumāla each, O best of rulers of the earth; / and with a thousand yojanas, a hundred thousand [in all].

1.7.s:
navamerustathā prokto gandhamādanamānataḥ ..
merornavasahasrāṇi mālyavāṃśca nigadyate .. 37 ..
1.7.d:
नवमेरुस्तथा प्रोक्तो गन्धमादनमानतः ॥
मेरोर्नवसहस्राणि माल्यवांश्च निगद्यते ॥ 37 ॥
1.7.m: Nine [thousand yojanas] from Meru is declared according to the measurement of Gandhamādana; / and Mālyavān is said to be nine thousand from Meru.

1.7.s:
meroryojanasāhasro viṣkambhaḥ kathitastathā ..
evamapyeṣa niyutaṃ jambūdvīpaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 38 ..
1.7.d:
मेरोर्योजनसाहस्रो विष्कम्भः कथितस्तथा ॥
एवमप्येष नियुतं जम्बूद्वीपः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 38 ॥
1.7.m: And the width of Meru is declared to be a thousand yojanas. / Thus too this Jambūdvīpa is proclaimed to be one hundred thousand [yojanas].

1.7.s:
himācale yakṣavarā niviṣṭā daityapradhānāḥ khalu hemakūṭe ..
gandharvamukhyā niṣadhe ca śaile nāgā niviṣṭāśca tathaiva nīle .. 39 ..
1.7.d:
हिमाचले यक्षवरा निविष्टा दैत्यप्रधानाः खलु हेमकूटे ॥
गन्धर्वमुख्या निषधे च शैले नागा निविष्टाश्च तथैव नीले ॥ 39 ॥
1.7.m: The foremost Yakṣas are settled on the Snowy Mountain; on Hemakūṭa indeed are the chief Daityas; / the foremost Gandharvas dwell on Mount Niṣadha, and Nāgas are settled likewise on Nīla;

1.7.s:
śvete pitṝṇāṃ ca gatirniviṣṭā siddhāstathā śṛṅgavataśca pṛṣṭhe ..
sendrāstathā devagaṇāśca merau krīḍāvihāreṇa sadā vasanti .. 1.7.40 ..
iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare prathamakhaṇḍe mārkaṇḍeyavajrasaṃvāde jambūdvīpavarṇano nāma saptamodhyāyaḥ .. 7 .. ..
1.7.d:
श्वेते पितॄणां च गतिर्निविष्टा सिद्धास्तथा शृङ्गवतश्च पृष्ठे ॥
सेन्द्रास्तथा देवगणाश्च मेरौ क्रीडाविहारेण सदा वसन्ति ॥ 1.7.40 ॥
इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे प्रथमखण्डे मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे जम्बूद्वीपवर्णनो नाम सप्तमोध्यायः ॥ 7 ॥ ॥
1.7.m:
on Śveta the realm of the ancestors is established; likewise the Siddhas dwell on the ridge of Śṛṅgavān; / and the multitudes of gods headed by Indra constantly dwell on Meru in sportive enjoyment.
Thus ends the seventh chapter, named 'Description of Jambūdvīpa', in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the first book of the holy Viṣṇudharmottara.

1.8.s:
.. vajra uvāca ..
bhagavanbhārataṃ varṣaṃ śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ ..
karmabhūmiṣu martyānāṃ varṣaṃ bhārgava bhāratam .. 1 ..
1.8.d:
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥
भगवन्भारतं वर्षं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ॥
कर्मभूमिषु मर्त्यानां वर्षं भार्गव भारतम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.8.m: Vajra said: / O venerable one, I wish to hear about the realm Bhārata in truth, / Bhārata, the realm among the lands of action for mortals, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

1.8.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
bhāratasyāsya varṣasya nava bhedāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..
aṣṭabhirgiribhiśchannā yetvagamyāḥ parasparam .. 2 ..
1.8.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
भारतस्यास्य वर्षस्य नव भेदाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
अष्टभिर्गिरिभिश्छन्ना येत्वगम्याः परस्परम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.8.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Nine divisions of this realm of Bhārata have been proclaimed,
which are covered by eight mountains and are mutually inaccessible.

1.8.s:
himācalādāsamudraṃ girayaste vyavasthitāḥ ..
yāmyottareṇa rājendra nāmatastānnibodha me .. 3 ..
1.8.d:
हिमाचलादासमुद्रं गिरयस्ते व्यवस्थिताः ॥
याम्योत्तरेण राजेन्द्र नामतस्तान्निबोध मे ॥ 3 ॥
1.8.m:
Those mountains extend from the Himalayas to the ocean,
running south to north, O king of kings. Learn them by name from me:

1.8.s:
svamālī hemamālī ca śambhuḥ kārtasvarākaraḥ ..
vaiḍūryaparvataścaiva rājato maṇimānbhavaḥ .. 4 ..
1.8.d:
स्वमाली हेममाली च शम्भुः कार्तस्वराकरः ॥
वैडूर्यपर्वतश्चैव राजतो मणिमान्भवः ॥ 4 ॥
1.8.m:
Svamālin, Hemamālin, Śambhu, the source of gold,
the Vaiḍūrya mountain, and Rājata, Maṇimat, and Bhava;

1.8.s:
indradyumnaḥ kadetaśca tāmravarṇo gabhastimān ..
rāgadveṣastathaivānyo gāndharvastvatha vāruṇaḥ .. 5 ..
1.8.d:
इन्द्रद्युम्नः कदेतश्च ताम्रवर्णो गभस्तिमान् ॥
रागद्वेषस्तथैवान्यो गान्धर्वस्त्वथ वारुणः ॥ 5 ॥
1.8.m:
Indradyumna, Kadeta, Tāmravarṇa, Gabhastimat,
Rāgadveṣa, and another, Gāndharva, and then Vāruṇa.

1.8.s:
teṣāṃ tu navamo madhye dvīpo nāmnā tu madhyamaḥ ..
asminmanvantare kṣiptaḥ sāgaraiśca caturdiśam .. 6 ..
1.8.d:
तेषां तु नवमो मध्ये द्वीपो नाम्ना तु मध्यमः ॥
अस्मिन्मन्वन्तरे क्षिप्तः सागरैश्च चतुर्दिशम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.8.m:
The ninth island situated among them is named Madhyama;
in this manvantara it is surrounded by oceans on all four sides.

1.8.s:
vaiḍūryaparvataḥ pūrvamuttareṇa himācalāt ..
paścārdhe kāñcanagirerudageva ca lāvaṇāt .. 9 ..
1.8.d:
वैडूर्यपर्वतः पूर्वमुत्तरेण हिमाचलात् ॥
पश्चार्धे काञ्चनगिरेरुदगेव च लावणात् ॥ 9 ॥
1.8.m:
The Vaiḍūrya mountain is to the east, north of the Himalayas,
and in the western half of the golden mountain, just north of the salt ocean.

1.8.s:
veṣṭitaḥ sāgaraḥ sarvo nānāsattvāśrayo nṛpa . ..
himālayaḥ sāgaraistu kṛto deśadvayastathā .. 8 ..
1.8.d:
वेष्टितः सागरः सर्वो नानासत्त्वाश्रयो नृप ॥।
हिमालयः सागरैस्तु कृतो देशद्वयस्तथा ॥ 8 ॥
1.8.m:
The entire ocean is encircled, serving as a refuge for various living beings, O king;
thus the Himalaya is made into two regions by the oceans.

1.8.s:
lavaṇasyottare pārśve sāgarasya ca dakṣiṇe ..
purī laṃkā sanniviṣṭā yasyāṃ vai rāvaṇo hataḥ .. 9 ..
1.8.d:
लवणस्योत्तरे पार्श्वे सागरस्य च दक्षिणे ॥
पुरी लंका सन्निविष्टा यस्यां वै रावणो हतः ॥ 9 ॥
1.8.m:
On the northern shore of the salt ocean and to the south of [the other] sea,
stands the city of Laṅkā, in which Rāvaṇa was indeed slain.

1.8.s:
lavaṇena ca saṃpṛktaḥ samudro lavaṇo yataḥ ..
himācalasya yo bhāgo varṣe'sminnṛpa bhārate ..1.8.1 0..
1.8.d:
लवणेन च संपृक्तः समुद्रो लवणो यतः ॥
हिमाचलस्य यो भागो वर्षेऽस्मिन्नृप भारते ॥1.8.1 0॥
1.8.m:
Because it is joined with salt, the ocean is called salty.
That part of the Himalayas which lies in this realm of Bhārata, O king,

1.8.s:
tatrāsti śailapravaro dvitīyo gandhamādanaḥ ..
śvetaśca parvataśreṣṭho mandaraśca mahāgiriḥ .. 11 ..
1.8.d:
तत्रास्ति शैलप्रवरो द्वितीयो गन्धमादनः ॥
श्वेतश्च पर्वतश्रेष्ठो मन्दरश्च महागिरिः ॥ 11 ॥
1.8.m:
there stands that foremost of mountains, the second Gandhamādana,
and the best of mountains Śveta, and the great mountain Mandara.

1.8.s:
ete śailavarā dṛṣṭā pāṇḍavaiśca mahātmabhiḥ ..
himācalasya madhye tu kailāso nāma parvataḥ..12..
1.8.d:
एते शैलवरा दृष्टा पाण्डवैश्च महात्मभिः ॥
हिमाचलस्य मध्ये तु कैलासो नाम पर्वतः॥12॥
1.8.m:
These excellent mountains were seen by the great-souled Pāṇḍavas.
In the middle of the Himalayas is the mountain named Kailāsa.

1.8.s:
himavatyeva vikhyāto naranārāyaṇāśramaḥ..
yatra sā badarī ramyā nānāśakunisevitā ..13..
1.8.d:
हिमवत्येव विख्यातो नरनारायणाश्रमः॥
यत्र सा बदरी रम्या नानाशकुनिसेविता ॥13॥
1.8.m:
Right on the snowy range is renowned the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa,
where that charming Badarī tree stands, frequented by various birds.

1.8.s:
uṣṇatoyavahā gaṅgā śvetatoyavahā parā ..
suvarṇasikatā rājaṃstāpasairupaśobhitā .. 14 ..
1.8.d:
उष्णतोयवहा गङ्गा श्वेततोयवहा परा ॥
सुवर्णसिकता राजंस्तापसैरुपशोभिता ॥ 14 ॥
1.8.m:
There the Gaṅgā carries warm water, while another carries white water;
with golden sands, O king, it is graced by ascetics.

1.8.s:
ityete kathitā dvīpāḥ prādhānyena tavānagha ..
eteṣāmaṃtare dvīpāḥ śataśotha sahasraśaḥ ..15..
1.8.d:
इत्येते कथिता द्वीपाः प्राधान्येन तवानघ ॥
एतेषामंतरे द्वीपाः शतशोथ सहस्रशः ॥15॥
1.8.m:
Thus these islands have been described in main to you, O sinless one.
Between these lie islands by the hundreds and thousands.

1.8.s:
na te varṇayituṃ śakyā varṣāṇāṃ tu śatairapi ..
vivarjayitvā bharatasya varṣaṃ varṣeṣu sarveṣu nareṃdrasiṃha ..
nirāmayā vītabhayā manuṣyā varṣeṣu sarveṣu tathaiva coktāḥ .. 16 ..
1.8.d:
न ते वर्णयितुं शक्या वर्षाणां तु शतैरपि ॥
विवर्जयित्वा भरतस्य वर्षं वर्षेषु सर्वेषु नरेंद्रसिंह ॥
निरामया वीतभया मनुष्या वर्षेषु सर्वेषु तथैव चोक्ताः ॥ 16 ॥
1.8.m:
They cannot be described even in hundreds of years.
With the exception of the realm of Bharata, in all the [other] realms, O lion among kings,
men are free from disease and fear; so it is proclaimed for all those realms.

1.8.s:
āyuḥpramāṇaṃ labhate hi rājandvīpeṣu sarveṣu naro mayoktam ..
kṛtvā śubhaṃ karma tu bhārate'smindvīpeṣu sarveṣu narāḥ prayānti .. ... 17 ..
1.8.d:
आयुःप्रमाणं लभते हि राजन्द्वीपेषु सर्वेषु नरो मयोक्तम् ॥
कृत्वा शुभं कर्म तु भारतेऽस्मिन्द्वीपेषु सर्वेषु नराः प्रयान्ति ॥ ॥। 17 ॥
1.8.m:
A man obtains the full span of life in all the islands that I have spoken of, O king;
having performed auspicious actions in this realm of Bhārata, men proceed to all those islands.

1.8.s:
vṛkṣeṣu teṣāṃ prabhavanti kāmāḥ striyaśca teṣāmapi rūpavatyaḥ ..
daṇḍaśca teṣāṃ ca na dāṇḍiko'sti sanmārgagāste'pi tathā ca rājan ..18..
1.8.d:
वृक्षेषु तेषां प्रभवन्ति कामाः स्त्रियश्च तेषामपि रूपवत्यः ॥
दण्डश्च तेषां च न दाण्डिकोऽस्ति सन्मार्गगास्तेऽपि तथा च राजन् ॥18॥
1.8.m:
Their desires arise from trees, and their women are beautiful;
they have no punishment and no punisher, and they walk upon the path of virtue, O king.

1.9.s:
.. vajra uvāca ..
śrotuṃ janānihecchāmi sāgaradvīpavāsinaḥ ..
prādhānyena bhṛguśreṣṭha vistarādvistaro yataḥ .. 1 ..
1.9.d:
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥
श्रोतुं जनानिहेच्छामि सागरद्वीपवासिनः ॥
प्राधान्येन भृगुश्रेष्ठ विस्तराद्विस्तरो यतः ॥ 1 ॥
1.9.m:
Vajra said:
I wish to hear here of the peoples dwelling on the islands of the ocean
principally, O best of the Bhṛgus, since an exhaustive account would be too extensive.

1.9.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
pāñcālāḥ kuravo matsyā yaudheyāḥ savaṭaścarāḥ ..
kuntayaḥ śūrasenāśca madhyadeśajanāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 2 ..
1.9.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
पाञ्चालाः कुरवो मत्स्या यौधेयाः सवटश्चराः ॥
कुन्तयः शूरसेनाश्च मध्यदेशजनाः स्मृताः ॥ 2 ॥
1.9.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
The Pāñcālas, Kurus, Matsyas, Yaudheyas along with the Paṭaccaras,
the Kuntis, and the Śūrasenas are considered peoples of the Middle Country.

1.9.s:
vṛṣadhvajāṃjanāḥ pannāḥ suhmā māgadhacedayaḥ ..
kāśayaśca videhāśca pūrvasyāṃ kośalāstathā .. 3 ..
1.9.d:
वृषध्वजांजनाः पन्नाः सुह्मा मागधचेदयः ॥
काशयश्च विदेहाश्च पूर्वस्यां कोशलास्तथा ॥ 3 ॥
1.9.m:
The Vṛṣadhvajas, Aṅjanas, Pannas, Suhmas, Māgadhas, and Cedis,
the Kāśis, Videhas, and likewise the Kośalas are in the east.

1.9.s:
kaliṅgavaṅgapuṇḍrāṅgavaidarbhā mūlakāstathā..
vindhyāntanilayāḥ proktāḥ pūrvadakṣiṇataḥ smṛtāḥ .. 4 ..
1.9.d:
कलिङ्गवङ्गपुण्ड्राङ्गवैदर्भा मूलकास्तथा॥
विन्ध्यान्तनिलयाः प्रोक्ताः पूर्वदक्षिणतः स्मृताः ॥ 4 ॥
1.9.m:
The Kaliṅgas, Vaṅgas, Puṇḍras, Aṅgas, Vaidarbhas, and Mūlakas,
said to dwell at the borders of the Vindhyas, are remembered in the southeast.

The Pulindas, Aśmakas, Jīmūtas, the dwellers of Nararāṣṭra,
the Karṇāṭakas, and the Bhojakaṭas are dwellers of the southern path.

1.9.s:
ambaṣṭhā draviḍā nāgāḥ kāmbojāḥ strīmukhāḥ śakāḥ ..
ānantavāsinaścaiva jñeyā dakṣiṇapaścime .. 6 ..
1.9.d:
अम्बष्ठा द्रविडा नागाः काम्बोजाः स्त्रीमुखाः शकाः ॥
आनन्तवासिनश्चैव ज्ञेया दक्षिणपश्चिमे ॥ 6 ॥
1.9.m:
The Ambaṣṭhas, Draviḍas, Nāgas, Kāmbojas, Strīmukhas, Śakas,
and the inhabitants of Ānanta are to be known in the southwest.

1.9.s:
strīrājyaṃ saindhavā mlecchā nāstikyā yavanāstathā ..
paścimena ca vijñeyāḥ paṭumānauṣadhaiḥ saha .. 7..
1.9.d:
स्त्रीराज्यं सैन्धवा म्लेच्छा नास्तिक्या यवनास्तथा ॥
पश्चिमेन च विज्ञेयाः पटुमानौषधैः सह ॥ 7॥
1.9.m:
The Kingdom of Women, the Saindhavas, Mlecchas, Nāstikyas, and Yavanas,
together with the Paṭumats and the Auṣadhas, are to be known in the west.

1.9.s:
māṇḍavyāśca tuṣārāśca mūlikāśca mukhāḥ khaśāḥ ..
mahākeśā mahānāsā deśāstūrattarapaścime .. 8 ..
1.9.d:
माण्डव्याश्च तुषाराश्च मूलिकाश्च मुखाः खशाः ॥
महाकेशा महानासा देशास्तूरत्तरपश्चिमे ॥ 8 ॥
1.9.m:
The Māṇḍavyas, Tuṣāras, Mūlikas, Mukhas, Khaśas,
the Mahākeśas, and the Mahānāsas are regions in the northwest.

1.9.s:
lampagāstālanāgāśca marugāndhārajāhutāḥ ..
himavannilayā mlecchā hyudīcīṃ diśamāśritāḥ .. 9 ..
1.9.d:
लम्पगास्तालनागाश्च मरुगान्धारजाहुताः ॥
हिमवन्निलया म्लेच्छा ह्युदीचीं दिशमाश्रिताः ॥ 9 ॥
1.9.m:
The Lampagas, Tālanāgas, Marus, Gāndhāras, and Jāhutas,
Mlecchas dwelling in the Himalayas, occupy the northern quarter.

The Trigartas, Mīnas, Kaulūtas, Brahmaputras, Satīgaṇas,
Abhisāras, and Kāśmīras are proclaimed in the northeast.

1.9.s:
rājendrasāgaradvīpā pradhānā vasudhādhipāḥ ..
bhavate'haṃ pravakṣyāmi digdeśena nibodha tat.. 11..
1.9.d:
राजेन्द्रसागरद्वीपा प्रधाना वसुधाधिपाः ॥
भवतेऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि दिग्देशेन निबोध तत्॥ 11॥
1.9.m:
The principal rulers of the earth among the ocean islands, O king of kings,
I shall declare to you; learn them according to the direction and region:

1.9.s:
pañcālanātho magadhādhipaśca kaliṅgarāḍ bhojakaṭeśvaraśca ..
anantakaḥ saindhavakastuṣāro madreśvaraścātha kulūtanāthaḥ .. 12 ..
1.9.d:
पञ्चालनाथो मगधाधिपश्च कलिङ्गराड् भोजकटेश्वरश्च ॥
अनन्तकः सैन्धवकस्तुषारो मद्रेश्वरश्चाथ कुलूतनाथः ॥ 12 ॥
1.9.m:
The lord of Pāñcāla, the sovereign of Magadha, the king of Kaliṅga, the lord of Bhojakaṭa,
the ruler of Ananta, the lord of Sindh, the Tuṣāra, the king of Madra, and then the lord of Kulūta.

1.10.s:
vajra uvāca ..
niviṣṭānsāgare dvīpe saptāhaṃ kulaparvatān ..
nāmataḥ śrotumicchāmi tatprasūtāśca nimnagāḥ .. 1 ..
1.10.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
निविष्टान्सागरे द्वीपे सप्ताहं कुलपर्वतान् ॥
नामतः श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्प्रसूताश्च निम्नगाः ॥ 1 ॥
1.10.m:
Vajra said:
I wish to hear by name of the seven family mountain ranges
situated in the island in the ocean, and of the rivers that issue from them.

1.10.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
mahendro malayaḥ sahyaḥ śuktimānṛkṣaparvataḥ ..
vindhyaśca pāriyātraśca saptāsminkulaparvatāḥ .. 2 ..
1.10.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
महेन्द्रो मलयः सह्यः शुक्तिमानृक्षपर्वतः ॥
विन्ध्यश्च पारियात्रश्च सप्तास्मिन्कुलपर्वताः ॥ 2 ॥
1.10.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Śuktimat, the Ṛkṣa mountain,
Vindhya, and Pāriyātra are the seven family mountain ranges here.

1.10.s:
trisāmā ṛṣikulyāśca ikṣugā tridivālayā ..
lāṃgūlinī vaṃśadharā nadyastvetā mahendrajāḥ ..3 ..
1.10.d:
त्रिसामा ऋषिकुल्याश्च इक्षुगा त्रिदिवालया ॥
लांगूलिनी वंशधरा नद्यस्त्वेता महेन्द्रजाः ॥3 ॥
1.10.m:
Trisāmā, Ṛṣikulyā, Ikṣugā, Tridivālayā,
Lāṅgūlinī, and Vaṃśadharā are rivers born of Mahendra.

1.10.s:
kṛtamālā tāmraparṇī puṣpajā cotpalāvatī ..
śītodakā girivahā nadyo malayasambhavāḥ ..4..
1.10.d:
कृतमाला ताम्रपर्णी पुष्पजा चोत्पलावती ॥
शीतोदका गिरिवहा नद्यो मलयसम्भवाः ॥4॥
1.10.m:
Kṛtamālā, Tāmraparṇī, Puṣpajā, Utpalāvatī,
Śītodakā, and Girivahā are the rivers arising from Malaya.

1.10.s:
tuṅgabhadrā suprakārā vāhyā kāverikā tathā ..
dakṣiṇāpathamadhyasthā sahyapādavinissṛtāḥ .. 5 ..
1.10.d:
तुङ्गभद्रा सुप्रकारा वाह्या कावेरिका तथा ॥
दक्षिणापथमध्यस्था सह्यपादविनिस्सृताः ॥ 5 ॥
1.10.m:
Tuṅgabhadrā, Suprakārā, Vāhyā, and Kāverikā,
situated in the middle of the southern path, have issued from the foot of Sahya.

1.10.s:
ṛṣikā sukumārī ca mandagā mandavāsinī ..
nṛpamālā śirī caiva śuktimatpādanissṛtāḥ .. 6 ..
1.10.d:
ऋषिका सुकुमारी च मन्दगा मन्दवासिनी ॥
नृपमाला शिरी चैव शुक्तिमत्पादनिस्सृताः ॥ 6 ॥
1.10.m:
Ṛṣikā, Sukumārī, Mandagā, Mandavāsinī,
Nṛpamālā, and Śirī have issued from the foot of Śuktimat.

1.10.s:
mandākinī daśārṇā ca śoṇo devī ca narmadā ..
tamasā pippalā ceti ṛkṣavatpādaniḥsṛtāḥ ..7..
1.10.d:
मन्दाकिनी दशार्णा च शोणो देवी च नर्मदा ॥
तमसा पिप्पला चेति ऋक्षवत्पादनिःसृताः ॥7॥
1.10.m:
Mandākinī, Daśārṇā, Śoṇa, the goddess Narmadā,
Tamasā, and Pippalā have issued from the foot of Ṛkṣavat.

1.10.s:
veṇā vaitaraṇī caiva narmadā ca kumudvatī ..
toyā setuśilā caiva vindhyapādavinissṛtāḥ ..8..
1.10.d:
वेणा वैतरणी चैव नर्मदा च कुमुद्वती ॥
तोया सेतुशिला चैव विन्ध्यपादविनिस्सृताः ॥8॥
1.10.m:
Veṇā, Vaitaraṇī, Narmadā, Kumudvatī,
Toyā, and Setuśilā have issued from the foot of Vindhya.

1.10.s:
pārā carmaṇvatī pādā vidiśā veṇuvatyapi ..
siprā hyavantī kuntī ca pāriyātraviniḥsṛtāḥ .. 9..
1.10.d:
पारा चर्मण्वती पादा विदिशा वेणुवत्यपि ॥
सिप्रा ह्यवन्ती कुन्ती च पारियात्रविनिःसृताः ॥ 9॥
1.10.m:
Pārā, Carmaṇvatī, Pādā, Vidiśā, Veṇuvatī,
Siprā, Avantī, and Kuntī have issued from Pāriyātra.

1.10.s:
nadyaḥ pradhānāḥ kathitāstavaitāḥ puṇyāḥ pavitrā ṛṣisevitāśca ..
santīha nadyaśca sahasraśo'nyā vaktuṃ na śakyā yaduvṛndanātha . .. 1.10.10 ..
1.10.d:
नद्यः प्रधानाः कथितास्तवैताः पुण्याः पवित्रा ऋषिसेविताश्च ॥
सन्तीह नद्यश्च सहस्रशोऽन्या वक्तुं न शक्या यदुवृन्दनाथ ॥। 1.10.10 ॥
1.10.m:
These principal rivers have been declared to you, sacred, purifying, and frequented by sages;
and there are thousands of other rivers here that cannot be recounted, O lord of the Yadu host.

1.11.s:
vajra uvāca ..
himavatpādasambhūtāḥ puṇyā brahmanviśeṣataḥ ..
prādhānyena samācakṣva nadyaḥ pāpabhayāpahāḥ ..1..
1.11.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
हिमवत्पादसम्भूताः पुण्या ब्रह्मन्विशेषतः ॥
प्राधान्येन समाचक्ष्व नद्यः पापभयापहाः ॥1॥
1.11.m:
Vajra said:
O brahmin, tell me chiefly of the holy rivers
that arise from the slopes of the Himavat, which remove fear and sin.

1.11.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
kauśeyavarṇasalilā kuśeśayavimiśritā ..
kauśikasya priyā nityaṃ kauśikī nimnagottamā .. 2 ..
1.11.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
कौशेयवर्णसलिला कुशेशयविमिश्रिता ॥
कौशिकस्य प्रिया नित्यं कौशिकी निम्नगोत्तमा ॥ 2 ॥
1.11.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Its waters the colour of tussar silk, mingled with lotuses,
ever dear to Kauśika, the Kauśikī is the foremost of streams.

1.11.s:
nimajjatpāpasaṃghaughanirmalīkaraṇe śubhā ..
niścarā nimnagā śreṣṭhā nityaṃ munijanapriyā ..3..
1.11.d:
निमज्जत्पापसंघौघनिर्मलीकरणे शुभा ॥
निश्चरा निम्नगा श्रेष्ठा नित्यं मुनिजनप्रिया ॥3॥
1.11.m:
Auspicious in cleansing the mass of sins of those who bathe in it,
the Niścarā is an excellent stream, ever dear to sages.

1.11.s:
gajendrabhinnakūlā tu gaṅgātulyā ca puṇyataḥ ..
gandharvagaṇagītā ca gaṇḍakī gokulākulā .. 4 ..
1.11.d:
गजेन्द्रभिन्नकूला तु गङ्गातुल्या च पुण्यतः ॥
गन्धर्वगणगीता च गण्डकी गोकुलाकुला ॥ 4 ॥
1.11.m:
Its banks broken by great elephants, equal to the Gaṅgā in holiness,
sung by hosts of gandharvas, the Gaṇḍakī is crowded with herds of cattle.

1.11.s:
lokānāṃ pāvanāyālaṃ lokanāthena nirmitā ..
lokadṛṣṭimanohārī lohityaśca mahānadaḥ ..5..
1.11.d:
लोकानां पावनायालं लोकनाथेन निर्मिता ॥
लोकदृष्टिमनोहारी लोहित्यश्च महानदः ॥5॥
1.11.m:
Created by the Lord of the World to purify the worlds,
captivating to the eyes of men, is the great river Lohitya.

1.11.s:
divaḥ sevyā sadā viprairdivi devagaṇairyathā..
dṛṣadvatī samākīrṇā darśanīyodakā tathā .. 6 ..
1.11.d:
दिवः सेव्या सदा विप्रैर्दिवि देवगणैर्यथा॥
दृषद्वती समाकीर्णा दर्शनीयोदका तथा ॥ 6 ॥
1.11.m:
Ever to be frequented by brahmins just as heaven is by gods in the sky,
thus the Dṛṣadvatī is crowded [with pilgrims], its waters fair to behold.

1.11.s:
bahudā bahusattvā'tha menā ca pralayakṣamā ..
anavacchinnavāhā tu likhitasya ca bāhudā ..7..
1.11.d:
बहुदा बहुसत्त्वाऽथ मेना च प्रलयक्षमा ॥
अनवच्छिन्नवाहा तु लिखितस्य च बाहुदा ॥7॥
1.11.m:
Then the Bahudā of many creatures, and the Menā capable of dissolution;
and the Bāhudā of Likhita, of uninterrupted course.

1.11.s:
dharmapradā sevakānāṃ dhūtapāpā mahānadī..
gomatī gokulākīrṇā gajendragaṇagāhitā .. 8 ..
1.11.d:
धर्मप्रदा सेवकानां धूतपापा महानदी॥
गोमती गोकुलाकीर्णा गजेन्द्रगणगाहिता ॥ 8 ॥
1.11.m:
Granting dharma to her servants, the great river cleanses sin:
the Gomatī, crowded with herds of cattle, plunged into by herds of great elephants,

1.11.s:
gandharvagītagaṃbhīrā gaṇayakṣagaṇairyutā ..
kuhūkadambakādambakekāravavināditā .. 9 ..
1.11.d:
गन्धर्वगीतगंभीरा गणयक्षगणैर्युता ॥
कुहूकदम्बकादम्बकेकारवविनादिता ॥ 9 ॥
1.11.m:
deep with songs of gandharvas, accompanied by troops of gaṇas and yakṣas,
resounding with the calls of cuckoos, kadamba geese, and the screams of peacocks,

1.11.s:
kumudotpala kahlārakusumairākulodakā ..
devadevasya yā devī dayitā śaṅkarasya ca .. 1.11.10 ..
1.11.d:
कुमुदोत्पल कह्लारकुसुमैराकुलोदका ॥
देवदेवस्य या देवी दयिता शङ्करस्य च ॥ 1.11.10 ॥
1.11.m:
its waters filled with night-blooming water lilies, blue lotuses, and white water lilies,
which goddess is beloved of the god of gods, Śaṅkara—

1.11.s:
devikā sā purā rājandevalokagatipradā ..
vistāritamahākūlā viṣamadvīpa vījitā .. 11 ..
1.11.d:
देविका सा पुरा राजन्देवलोकगतिप्रदा ॥
विस्तारितमहाकूला विषमद्वीप वीजिता ॥ 11 ॥
1.11.m:
she is the ancient Devikā, O king, which grants access to the world of the gods;
her great banks broad, fanned by rugged islands;

1.11.s:
viṣṇulokapradā devī vitastāghavināśinī ..
candrabhāgā ca candrāṃśucāruśītajalāvilā .. 12 ..
1.11.d:
विष्णुलोकप्रदा देवी वितस्ताघविनाशिनी ॥
चन्द्रभागा च चन्द्रांशुचारुशीतजलाविला ॥ 12 ॥
1.11.m:
the goddess Vitastā, granting the world of Viṣṇu, destroying sin;
and the Candrabhāgā, its turbid waters lovely and cool like moonbeams,

1.11.s:
candralokapradā snāne cāmaratvapradāyinī ..
sarojākulatīrthā ca sarayūḥ saritāṃ varā ..13 ..
1.11.d:
चन्द्रलोकप्रदा स्नाने चामरत्वप्रदायिनी ॥
सरोजाकुलतीर्था च सरयूः सरितां वरा ॥13 ॥
1.11.m:
granting the world of the moon by bathing, conferring the state of an immortal;
and the Sarayū, best of rivers, its bathing places crowded with lotuses,

1.11.s:
satataṃ sevitā sadbhiḥ somalokamabhīpsubhiḥ ..
indrebhasevitataṭā indraloka pradāyinī .. 14 ..
1.11.d:
सततं सेविता सद्भिः सोमलोकमभीप्सुभिः ॥
इन्द्रेभसेविततटा इन्द्रलोक प्रदायिनी ॥ 14 ॥
1.11.m:
constantly frequented by the virtuous seeking the world of Soma;
its banks visited by Indra's elephant, granting Indra's world,

1.11.s:
indīvarākulajalā tathā devī irāvatī ..
viśiṣṭapāśavicchede vipāśā kuśalā tathā .. 15 ..
1.11.d:
इन्दीवराकुलजला तथा देवी इरावती ॥
विशिष्टपाशविच्छेदे विपाशा कुशला तथा ॥ 15 ॥
1.11.m:
its waters filled with blue lotuses: likewise the goddess Irāvatī;
and the Vipāśā, skilled in severing prominent bonds,

1.11.s:
tathaiva sarvapāpānāṃ vipākakāriṇī nṛṇām ..
vaśiṣṭhavidrutā devī śatadrurdrutagāminī .. 16 ..
1.11.d:
तथैव सर्वपापानां विपाककारिणी नृणाम् ॥
वशिष्ठविद्रुता देवी शतद्रुर्द्रुतगामिनी ॥ 16 ॥
1.11.m:
and likewise bringing about the ripening of all sins for men;
the swift-flowing goddess Śatadru, by whom Vasiṣṭha fled;

1.11.s:
raudrāṇāmapi sattvānāṃ rudralokapradā śivā ..
kṛṣṇena kṛṣṇatoyā ca bālye pītapayodharā .. 17 ..
1.11.d:
रौद्राणामपि सत्त्वानां रुद्रलोकप्रदा शिवा ॥
कृष्णेन कृष्णतोया च बाल्ये पीतपयोधरा ॥ 17 ॥
1.11.m:
the auspicious river granting the world of Rudra even to fierce creatures;
and the river whose dark waters were drunk like breasts in childhood by Kṛṣṇa,

1.11.s:
yamasvasā ca yamunā yāmyaduḥkhavināśinī ..
saptaprakārā ca nadī tathā devī sarasvatī ..18 ..
1.11.d:
यमस्वसा च यमुना याम्यदुःखविनाशिनी ॥
सप्तप्रकारा च नदी तथा देवी सरस्वती ॥18 ॥
1.11.m:
Yama's sister, the Yamunā, who destroys the sufferings of Yama's realm;
and the sevenfold river, the divine Sarasvatī.

1.11.s:
tasyāḥ saptasu bhāgeṣu nāmāni śṛṇu me nṛpa ..
suprabhā kātarākṣī ca viśālā mānasahradā .. 19 ..
1.11.d:
तस्याः सप्तसु भागेषु नामानि शृणु मे नृप ॥
सुप्रभा कातराक्षी च विशाला मानसह्रदा ॥ 19 ॥
1.11.m:
Hear from me, O king, its names in its seven regions:
Suprabhā, Kātarākṣī, Viśālā, Mānasahradā,

1.11.s:
sarasvatyoghanādā ca suveṇurvimalodakā ..
puṣkare naimiṣe caiva gayāyāṃ kośaleṣu ca .. 1.11.20 ..
1.11.d:
सरस्वत्योघनादा च सुवेणुर्विमलोदका ॥
पुष्करे नैमिषे चैव गयायां कोशलेषु च ॥ 1.11.20 ॥
1.11.m:
Sarasvatī, Oghanādā, and Suveṇu of clear waters:
at Puṣkara, at Naimiṣa, at Gayā, and among the Kośalas,

1.11.s:
kurukṣetre kramājjñeyā gaṅgādvāre himācale ..
nadyastathaitā himavatprasūtāḥ pradhānabhūtāḥ kathitā nṛvīra! ..
uktāśca nadyaśca sahasraśo'nyāḥ sarvāḥ pavitrā ṛṣivaryajuṣṭāḥ .. 21 ..
1.11.d:
कुरुक्षेत्रे क्रमाज्ज्ञेया गङ्गाद्वारे हिमाचले ॥
नद्यस्तथैता हिमवत्प्रसूताः प्रधानभूताः कथिता नृवीर! ॥
उक्ताश्च नद्यश्च सहस्रशोऽन्याः सर्वाः पवित्रा ऋषिवर्यजुष्टाः ॥ 21 ॥
1.11.m:
at Kurukṣetra, at Gaṅgādvāra, and on the Himācala, they should be known in order.
Thus these rivers born of the Himavat, being the principal ones, have been told, O hero among men!
And thousands of other rivers have been mentioned, all sacred and frequented by the best of sages.

1.11.s:
varṣasya tasyāpi tathāntare'sminsaptaprakārā ca trimārgagāpi ..
dvīpaṃ praviṣṭā bharatasya rājan bhagīrathārādhitapadmajoktā .. 22 ..
1.11.d:
वर्षस्य तस्यापि तथान्तरेऽस्मिन्सप्तप्रकारा च त्रिमार्गगापि ॥
द्वीपं प्रविष्टा भरतस्य राजन् भगीरथाराधितपद्मजोक्ता ॥ 22 ॥
1.11.m:
And within this realm, the three-pathed river too, divided into seven forms,
entered the continent of Bharata, O king, as spoken of by the lotus-born [Brahmā] when propitiated by Bhagīratha.

1.12.s:
..vajra uvāca ..
bhāratasyāsya varṣasya bhede'sminnavame prabho ..
kimarthaṃ sāgaraḥ khātaḥ sa kṛtaḥ sagaraistathā..1..
1.12.d:
॥वज्र उवाच ॥
भारतस्यास्य वर्षस्य भेदेऽस्मिन्नवमे प्रभो ॥
किमर्थं सागरः खातः स कृतः सगरैस्तथा॥1॥
1.12.m:
Vajra said:
In this ninth division of this realm of Bharata, O lord,
why was the ocean dug, and how was it made by the sons of Sagara?

1.12.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
bhāratasyāsya varṣasya bhede'sminnavame nṛpa! ..
navame ca diśāṃ bhāge pūrvasyāṃ diśi yādava ..2 ..
1.12.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
भारतस्यास्य वर्षस्य भेदेऽस्मिन्नवमे नृप! ॥
नवमे च दिशां भागे पूर्वस्यां दिशि यादव ॥2 ॥
1.12.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
In this ninth division of this realm of Bharata, O king,
and in the ninth part of the directions, in the eastern quarter, O Yādava,

1.12.s:
kośalo nāma viṣayaḥ prabhūtadhanadhānyavān ..
sphītagrāmaguṇāḍhyo'sti nityaṃ mudita mānavaḥ .. 3 ..
1.12.d:
कोशलो नाम विषयः प्रभूतधनधान्यवान् ॥
स्फीतग्रामगुणाढ्योऽस्ति नित्यं मुदित मानवः ॥ 3 ॥
1.12.m:
there is a territory named Kośala, possessed of abundant wealth and grain,
endowed with the virtues of prosperous villages, where people are ever joyful,

1.12.s:
payasvinyaḥ payasvinyo yatra sasyadharā dharā ..
mano'bhirāmā rāmāśca puruṣāḥ pauruṣāgragāḥ .. 4 ..
1.12.d:
पयस्विन्यः पयस्विन्यो यत्र सस्यधरा धरा ॥
मनोऽभिरामा रामाश्च पुरुषाः पौरुषाग्रगाः ॥ 4 ॥
1.12.m:
where rivers flow with milk, where the earth yields grain,
where women are delightful to the mind, and men are foremost in manly virtue;

1.12.s:
vidagdhajanabhūyiṣṭhā sarvapuṇya samākulā ..
nagarairna viśiṣyante yatra grāmā manoharāḥ .. 5 ..
1.12.d:
विदग्धजनभूयिष्ठा सर्वपुण्य समाकुला ॥
नगरैर्न विशिष्यन्ते यत्र ग्रामा मनोहराः ॥ 5 ॥
1.12.m:
abounding in clever people, filled with every merit,
where charming villages are not surpassed by cities;

1.12.s:
gavāṃ praveśe sāyāhne yatra grāmeṣu bhāskaraḥ ..
dhūlipuñjaparikṣiptaḥ vanasānuvirājitaḥ .. 6 ..
1.12.d:
गवां प्रवेशे सायाह्ने यत्र ग्रामेषु भास्करः ॥
धूलिपुञ्जपरिक्षिप्तः वनसानुविराजितः ॥ 6 ॥
1.12.m:
where the sun at evening, as the cows return to the villages,
is veiled in clouds of dust, yet shines bright over the forest slopes;

1.12.s:
paścime prathame caiva yatra yāme virājitaḥ ..
rātrau brahmadhvanistatra tiṣṭhatīva nabhastalam .. 7 ..
1.12.d:
पश्चिमे प्रथमे चैव यत्र यामे विराजितः ॥
रात्रौ ब्रह्मध्वनिस्तत्र तिष्ठतीव नभस्तलम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.12.m:
where, during the last and the first watch of the night,
the sound of Vedic recitation shines forth, seeming to pervade the vault of heaven;

1.12.s:
phalāvanataśākhāḍhyāśchāyādrumasamā kulāḥ ..
prapākūpataḍāgāḍhyā panthāno yatra yādava .. 8 ..
1.12.d:
फलावनतशाखाढ्याश्छायाद्रुमसमा कुलाः ॥
प्रपाकूपतडागाढ्या पन्थानो यत्र यादव ॥ 8 ॥
1.12.m:
where the roads are filled with shade trees, rich with branches bent down with fruit,
endowed with water-stations, wells, and ponds, O Yādava;

1.12.s:
vyādhitaskaradurbhikṣapararāṣṭrabhayāni ca ..
janā yatra na jānanti nākālamaraṇaṃ tathā .. 9 ..
1.12.d:
व्याधितस्करदुर्भिक्षपरराष्ट्रभयानि च ॥
जना यत्र न जानन्ति नाकालमरणं तथा ॥ 9 ॥
1.12.m:
where the people know no fear of disease, thieves, famine, or hostile realms,
nor any untimely death;

where the earth is marked by sacrificial posts, adorned with temples of the gods,
and beautified by excellent step-wells crowded with blue lotuses;

1.12.s:
udyāneṣu sadā yatra veṇugāndharvaniḥsvanam ..
śilīmukharavairmiśraṃ yātyasaṃbādhatāṃ guṇaiḥ .. 11 ..
1.12.d:
उद्यानेषु सदा यत्र वेणुगान्धर्वनिःस्वनम् ॥
शिलीमुखरवैर्मिश्रं यात्यसंबाधतां गुणैः ॥ 11 ॥
1.12.m:
where in the gardens the continuous sound of flutes and gandharva-song,
mingled with the humming of bees, is harmonious through its qualities;

1.12.s:
yasminna kaściccyavate svadharmāddīno jano yatra na cāsti kaścit ..
na netrahīno vikalendriyo vā vasundharā yatra yathārthanāmā .. 12 ..
1.12.d:
यस्मिन्न कश्चिच्च्यवते स्वधर्माद्दीनो जनो यत्र न चास्ति कश्चित् ॥
न नेत्रहीनो विकलेन्द्रियो वा वसुन्धरा यत्र यथार्थनामा ॥ 12 ॥
1.12.m:
wherein no one falls away from their own duty, and where no person is wretched,
nor blind or of impaired senses, and where the earth bears its name according to truth.

1.13.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
kosalāviṣaye sphīte tasminmanujapuṅgava ..
devānāmapyayodhyāsti tvayodhyānāmataḥ purī .. 1 ..
1.13.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
कोसलाविषये स्फीते तस्मिन्मनुजपुङ्गव ॥
देवानामप्ययोध्यास्ति त्वयोध्यानामतः पुरी ॥ 1 ॥
1.13.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
In that prosperous territory of Kosala, O bull among men,
there is a city named Ayodhyā, which is unconquerable even to the gods,

provided with ramparts and moats, beautified by the banks of the Sarayū,
gleaming with splendid palaces, with its high roads well divided;

resplendent with hundreds of elephants that are ever gentle, resembling mountains of collyrium,
born of the lineage of divine elephants;

filled with horses swift as thought, with lean faces and fine ears,
with long necks and eyebrow arches, and large thighs and hips;

1.13.s:
padmagarbhasavarṇāṅgyaḥ pūrṇacandranibhānanāḥ ..
saṃlāpollāsakuśalā yatra veśyāḥ sahasraśaḥ .. 5 ..
1.13.d:
पद्मगर्भसवर्णाङ्ग्यः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाः ॥
संलापोल्लासकुशला यत्र वेश्याः सहस्रशः ॥ 5 ॥
1.13.m:
where courtesans by the thousands have limbs the colour of a lotus interior,
faces resembling the full moon, skilled in playful banter;

1.13.s:
na tatpuṇyaṃ na sā vidyā na tacchilpaṃ na sā kriyā ..
ayodhyāṃ prāpya yasyārthī nirāśaḥ pratigacchati .. .. 6 ..
1.13.d:
न तत्पुण्यं न सा विद्या न तच्छिल्पं न सा क्रिया ॥
अयोध्यां प्राप्य यस्यार्थी निराशः प्रतिगच्छति ॥ ॥ 6 ॥
1.13.m:
there is no merit, no learning, no craft, no sacred rite,
seeking which a supplicant turns away disappointed after reaching Ayodhyā;

crowded with hundreds of gardens, abounding in assemblies and festivities,
its men heroic and free from disease, devoid of all dispute,

1.13.s:
vīṇāveṇumṛdaṅgānāṃ śabdaiḥ satatanāditā ..
sadā prahṛṣṭamanujā bahuratnopaśobhitā .. 8 ..
1.13.d:
वीणावेणुमृदङ्गानां शब्दैः सततनादिता ॥
सदा प्रहृष्टमनुजा बहुरत्नोपशोभिता ॥ 8 ॥
1.13.m:
continually echoing with the sounds of lutes, flutes, and mṛdaṅgas,
its people ever rejoicing, adorned with many gems.
resounding loudly with the chanting of the Veda, adorned by crowds of twice-born, / with sins destroyed by the wind filled with rising smoke of clarified butter;
having its breezes made fragrant by scattering sweet-scented incense, / always crowded with sweet-smelling people in the market streets;

1.13.s:
yatra dīno jano nāsti malinaḥ kṛśito'pi vā ..
vedanindāparaḥ kṣudro bhinnaseturna nāstikaḥ .. 11 ..
1.13.d:
यत्र दीनो जनो नास्ति मलिनः कृशितोऽपि वा ॥
वेदनिन्दापरः क्षुद्रो भिन्नसेतुर्न नास्तिकः ॥ 11 ॥
1.13.m: where there was no wretched person, nor one dirty or emaciated, / no one intent on reviling the Vedas, no base person, no breaker of social bounds, and no atheist.

1.13.s:
vistīrṇā daśa madhye ca yojanānāṃ mahāpurī ..
sarayūtīramāśritya yojanatrayamāyatā ..12..
1.13.d:
विस्तीर्णा दश मध्ये च योजनानां महापुरी ॥
सरयूतीरमाश्रित्य योजनत्रयमायता ॥12॥
1.13.m: The great city was ten yojanas wide across the middle, / and extended three yojanas along the bank of the Sarayū.

1.13.s:
manvantare'sminpunareva rājñā vinirmitā sā manunā nṛvīra! ..
manvantaraṃ yena jagatsamagraṃ pālyaṃ yathāvadyaduvṛndanātha! .. 13 ..
1.13.d:
मन्वन्तरेऽस्मिन्पुनरेव राज्ञा विनिर्मिता सा मनुना नृवीर! ॥
मन्वन्तरं येन जगत्समग्रं पाल्यं यथावद्यदुवृन्दनाथ! ॥ 13 ॥
1.13.m: In this Manu-period, O heroic king, leader of the Yadu hosts, it was built again by King Manu, / by whom the entire universe is to be properly protected throughout the Manu-period.

1.14.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
vaivasvatena manunā yena sā nirmitā purī ..
sa tu kṛtvā ciraṃ rājyamikṣvākumabhiṣicya ca .. 1 ..
1.14.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
वैवस्वतेन मनुना येन सा निर्मिता पुरी ॥
स तु कृत्वा चिरं राज्यमिक्ष्वाकुमभिषिच्य च ॥ 1 ॥
1.14.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / By Manu, son of Vivasvat, by whom that city was built, / after ruling for a long time and consecrating Ikṣvāku,

1.14.s:
puttre bhāraṃ samāveśya saśarīro divaṃ gataḥ ..
tatrasthaḥ pālayannāste trailokyaṃ sacarācaram .. 2 ..
1.14.d:
पुत्त्रे भारं समावेश्य सशरीरो दिवं गतः ॥
तत्रस्थः पालयन्नास्ते त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.14.m: and placing the burden [of kingship] upon his son, he went to heaven in his bodily form. / Abiding there, he remains protecting the three worlds with the moving and unmoving beings.

1.14.s:
tena manvantaraṃ sarvaṃ pālanīyamidaṃ jagat ..
ikṣvākustasya tanayaḥ pālayāmāsa medinīm ..3..
1.14.d:
तेन मन्वन्तरं सर्वं पालनीयमिदं जगत् ॥
इक्ष्वाकुस्तस्य तनयः पालयामास मेदिनीम् ॥3॥
1.14.m: This entire universe is to be protected by him for the whole Manu-period. / His son Ikṣvāku protected the earth.

1.14.s:
dharmajñaśca kṛtajñaśca satyavādī jitendriyaḥ ..
sudarśaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ nayāpanayakovidaḥ .. 4 ..
1.14.d:
धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च सत्यवादी जितेन्द्रियः ॥
सुदर्शः सर्वभूतानां नयापनयकोविदः ॥ 4 ॥
1.14.m: He knew dharma and was grateful, spoke truth and had conquered his senses; / he was pleasing to behold for all beings, skilled in policy and impolicy,

1.14.s:
brahmaṇyaśca śaraṇyaśca dīnānāthānukampakaḥ ..
daivamantraprabhūtsāha śaktibhiśca samanvitaḥ ..5 ..
1.14.d:
ब्रह्मण्यश्च शरण्यश्च दीनानाथानुकम्पकः ॥
दैवमन्त्रप्रभूत्साह शक्तिभिश्च समन्वितः ॥5 ॥
1.14.m: devoted to brahmins, a refuge, compassionate toward the wretched and helpless, / endowed with the powers of fate, counsel, majesty, and energy;

1.14.s:
ṣāḍguṇyavinmahotsāhaḥ smitapūrvābhibhāṣaṇaḥ ..
yuktadaṃḍo na nirdaṃḍo na ca daṇḍaratistathā ..6..
1.14.d:
षाड्गुण्यविन्महोत्साहः स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषणः ॥
युक्तदंडो न निर्दंडो न च दण्डरतिस्तथा ॥6॥
1.14.m: knowing the sixfold statecraft, possessing great zeal, speaking with a smile first, / applying punishment justly, neither devoid of punishment nor delighting in it;

1.14.s:
vedavedāṅgatattvajño yajñayājī taporatiḥ ..
akṣudralīlo'bhimataḥ sarvasattvo na hiṃsakaḥ .. 7 ..
1.14.d:
वेदवेदाङ्गतत्त्वज्ञो यज्ञयाजी तपोरतिः ॥
अक्षुद्रलीलोऽभिमतः सर्वसत्त्वो न हिंसकः ॥ 7 ॥
1.14.m: knowing the truth of the Vedas and auxiliary sciences, an offerer of sacrifices, delighting in ascetic practice, / noble in demeanor, highly regarded, friendly to all beings, and not causing harm;

1.14.s:
mānyo mānayatāṃ śakyaḥ sukhaḥ pūjyaprapūjakaḥ ..
kāmaḥ krodho mado māno lobho harṣastathaiva ca .. 8 ..
1.14.d:
मान्यो मानयतां शक्यः सुखः पूज्यप्रपूजकः ॥
कामः क्रोधो मदो मानो लोभो हर्षस्तथैव च ॥ 8 ॥
1.14.m: honorable, accessible to those who honor him, delightful, venerating those who are worthy of veneration. / Desire, anger, intoxication, pride, greed, and arrogance:

1.14.s:
nityaṃ śarīraprabhavā ripavastena ṣaḍ jitāḥ ..
sarvatra vidhinā dṛśyaḥ subhagaḥ priyadarśanaḥ .. 9 ..
1.14.d:
नित्यं शरीरप्रभवा रिपवस्तेन षड् जिताः ॥
सर्वत्र विधिना दृश्यः सुभगः प्रियदर्शनः ॥ 9 ॥
1.14.m: these six enemies arising from the body were constantly conquered by him. / Fit to be seen everywhere according to rule, fortunate, pleasing of sight,

1.14.s:
bahudhānyo bahudhano bahunāgāśvapūruṣaḥ ..
ayodhyānilayo nityaṃ devārigaṇadarpahā ..1.14.1 0..
1.14.d:
बहुधान्यो बहुधनो बहुनागाश्वपूरुषः ॥
अयोध्यानिलयो नित्यं देवारिगणदर्पहा ॥1.14.1 0॥
1.14.m: rich in grain and wealth, having many elephants, horses, and men, / ever dwelling in Ayodhyā, destroying the arrogance of the hosts of the gods' enemies.

1.14.s:
sa tadā pālayāmāsa putravatsakalāḥ prajāḥ ..
nādharmaḥ kaścidapyāsīttasminrājani mānavaḥ .. 11 ..
1.14.d:
स तदा पालयामास पुत्रवत्सकलाः प्रजाः ॥
नाधर्मः कश्चिदप्यासीत्तस्मिन्राजनि मानवः ॥ 11 ॥
1.14.m: He then protected all the subjects like his own children; / while he was king, not a single human being engaged in adharma.

1.14.s:
dīno vā vyādhito vāpi svalpāyurvā ca duḥkhitaḥ ..
mūrkho vā mandarūpo vā durbhago vā nirākṛtiḥ ..12..
1.14.d:
दीनो वा व्याधितो वापि स्वल्पायुर्वा च दुःखितः ॥
मूर्खो वा मन्दरूपो वा दुर्भगो वा निराकृतिः ॥12॥
1.14.m: [There was no one] miserable, diseased, short-lived, or suffering, / nor foolish, unsightly, unfortunate, or deformed.

1.14.s:
ekatra dehe sakalaṃ guṇaughaṃ draṣṭāhamityeva viśiṣṭabuddhiḥ ..
sasarja yaṃ rājavaraṃ mahātmā prajāpatiḥ sarvajagatpradhānaḥ ..13..
1.14.d:
एकत्र देहे सकलं गुणौघं द्रष्टाहमित्येव विशिष्टबुद्धिः ॥
ससर्ज यं राजवरं महात्मा प्रजापतिः सर्वजगत्प्रधानः ॥13॥
1.14.m: Thinking 'I will see the whole mass of virtues in one single body', with exceptional intellect, / the great-souled Prajāpati, foremost of all the universe, created this best of kings.

1.14.s: iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare prathamakhaṇḍe mārkaṇḍeyavajrasaṃvāde ikṣvākukulavarṇanaṃnāma caturdaśo'dhyāyaḥ.. ...14..
1.14.d: इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे प्रथमखण्डे मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे इक्ष्वाकुकुलवर्णनंनाम चतुर्दशोऽध्यायः॥ ॥.14॥
1.14.m: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Lineage of Ikṣvāku', in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the First Book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.

1.15.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ikṣvākorabhavatputro vikukṣirnnāma dhārmikaḥ ..
kakutsthastanayastasya cānenāstasya cātmajaḥ ..1..
1.15.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
इक्ष्वाकोरभवत्पुत्रो विकुक्षिर्न्नाम धार्मिकः ॥
ककुत्स्थस्तनयस्तस्य चानेनास्तस्य चात्मजः ॥1॥
1.15.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Ikṣvāku had a righteous son named Vikukṣi; / his son was Kakutstha, and his son was Anenas.

1.15.s:
tasya putraḥ pṛthuḥ śrīmān viśvadāsastadātmajaḥ ..
tasya śrāvastako nāma śrāvastī yena nirmitā..2..
1.15.d:
तस्य पुत्रः पृथुः श्रीमान् विश्वदासस्तदात्मजः ॥
तस्य श्रावस्तको नाम श्रावस्ती येन निर्मिता॥2॥
1.15.m: His son was glorious Pṛthu, whose son was Viśvadāsa; / his [son] was named Śrāvastaka, by whom Śrāvastī was founded.

1.15.s:
bṛhadaśvaḥ sutastasya kuvalāśvastadātmajaḥ ..
kuvalāśvo mahātejā dhundhumāratvamāgataḥ ..
dhuṃdhuṃ hatvā mahākāyamudake jalarākṣasam .. 3 ..
1.15.d:
बृहदश्वः सुतस्तस्य कुवलाश्वस्तदात्मजः ॥
कुवलाश्वो महातेजा धुन्धुमारत्वमागतः ॥
धुंधुं हत्वा महाकायमुदके जलराक्षसम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.15.m: His son was Bṛhadaśva, and his son was Kuvalāśva. / Kuvalāśva of great splendor attained the name Dhundhumāra / having slain Dhundhu, the gigantic water-demon, in the waters.

1.15.s:
vajra uvāca ..
kathaṃ dhuṃdhurmahātejāḥ kuvalāśvena ghātitaḥ ..
kaścāyaṃ dhuṃdhurityeṣa viśruto jalarākṣasaḥ .. 4..
1.15.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
कथं धुंधुर्महातेजाः कुवलाश्वेन घातितः ॥
कश्चायं धुंधुरित्येष विश्रुतो जलराक्षसः ॥ 4॥
1.15.m: Vajra said: / How was Dhundhu of great splendor slain by Kuvalāśva? / And who was this water-demon renowned as Dhundhu?

1.15.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ekārṇave purā loke naṣṭasthāvarajaṅgame .. 5 ..
1.15.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एकार्णवे पुरा लोके नष्टस्थावरजङ्गमे ॥ 5 ॥
1.15.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Formerly, when the world had become a single cosmic ocean and moving and unmoving things were destroyed,

1.15.s:
naṣṭacandrārkapavane vinaṣṭagrahatārake ..
śeṣaparyaṅkamāsādya supto devo janārdanaḥ .. 6 ..
1.15.d:
नष्टचन्द्रार्कपवने विनष्टग्रहतारके ॥
शेषपर्यङ्कमासाद्य सुप्तो देवो जनार्दनः ॥ 6 ॥
1.15.m: when the moon, sun, and wind were vanished, and the planets and stars were destroyed, / the god Janārdana slept, resting on the bed of Śeṣa.

1.15.s:
nābhau tasya samutpannaṃ devasya kamalaṃ śubham ..
tatra jajñe svayaṃ brahmā devaḥ śubhacaturmukhaḥ..7..
1.15.d:
नाभौ तस्य समुत्पन्नं देवस्य कमलं शुभम् ॥
तत्र जज्ञे स्वयं ब्रह्मा देवः शुभचतुर्मुखः॥7॥
1.15.m: An auspicious lotus arose from the navel of the god. / There the four-faced auspicious god Brahmā was himself born.

1.15.s:
tatrāste so'bhyasanvedānsupte deve janārdane ..
upāsāṃcakrire tasya vedā dehabhṛtastathā .. 8 ..
1.15.d:
तत्रास्ते सोऽभ्यसन्वेदान्सुप्ते देवे जनार्दने ॥
उपासांचक्रिरे तस्य वेदा देहभृतस्तथा ॥ 8 ॥
1.15.m: He sat there studying the Vedas while the god Janārdana was asleep; / and the Vedas, assuming bodily forms, waited upon him.

1.15.s:
vedābhyāsarate tatra svedabindurajāyata ..
sapadmapatramāsādya dvidhābhūtobhavannṛpa .. 9 ..
1.15.d:
वेदाभ्यासरते तत्र स्वेदबिन्दुरजायत ॥
सपद्मपत्रमासाद्य द्विधाभूतोभवन्नृप ॥ 9 ॥
1.15.m: While he was occupied in the study of the Vedas, a drop of sweat arose there; / falling upon a lotus petal, O king, it split into two.

1.15.s:
rajastamomayau tasmājjātau daityau balotkaṭau ..
madhukaiṭabhanāmānau mahābalaparākramau .. 1.15.10 ..
1.15.d:
रजस्तमोमयौ तस्माज्जातौ दैत्यौ बलोत्कटौ ॥
मधुकैटभनामानौ महाबलपराक्रमौ ॥ 1.15.10 ॥
1.15.m: From that arose two daityas, composed of rajas and tamas, formidable in strength, / named Madhu and Kaiṭabha, possessing great power and valor.

1.15.s:
tatastau jahraturvedānbrahmaṇaḥ pāpaniścayau ..
saśarīreṣu vedeṣu hateṣvatha pitāmahaḥ .. 11..
1.15.d:
ततस्तौ जह्रतुर्वेदान्ब्रह्मणः पापनिश्चयौ ॥
सशरीरेषु वेदेषु हतेष्वथ पितामहः ॥ 11॥
1.15.m: Then the two, determined on evil, snatched away the Vedas from Brahmā. / When the embodied Vedas were thus carried away, the Grandfather

1.15.s:
bodhayāmāsa deveśaṃ padmanābhaṃ sa cānaghaḥ ..
sa vibuddhastadā devaḥ kṛtvā hayaśirodharam .. 12 ..
1.15.d:
बोधयामास देवेशं पद्मनाभं स चानघः ॥
स विबुद्धस्तदा देवः कृत्वा हयशिरोधरम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.15.m: awakened the lord of gods, the lotus-navelled, sinless one. / That god, then awakened, assumed a horse's head,

1.15.s:
śaśāṅkaśatasaṃkāśaṃ nānābharaṇaśobhitam ..
dvitīyena śarīreṇa rasātalatalaṃ gataḥ .. 13..
1.15.d:
शशाङ्कशतसंकाशं नानाभरणशोभितम् ॥
द्वितीयेन शरीरेण रसातलतलं गतः ॥ 13॥
1.15.m: resembling a hundred moons and adorned with various ornaments; / with that second body, he went to the depths of the netherworld.

1.15.s:
tenāśvaśirasā gatvā vedānādāya śāśvatān ..
pitāmahāya pradadau bhūya eva jagadguruḥ ..14..
1.15.d:
तेनाश्वशिरसा गत्वा वेदानादाय शाश्वतान् ॥
पितामहाय प्रददौ भूय एव जगद्गुरुः ॥14॥
1.15.m: Going with that horse's head and recovering the eternal Vedas, / the Guru of the universe gave them back again to the Grandfather.

1.15.s:
tato hayaśirodhārī gatontardhānamīśvaraḥ ..
ājagmatustato deśaṃ dānavau madhukaiṭabhau ..15..
1.15.d:
ततो हयशिरोधारी गतोन्तर्धानमीश्वरः ॥
आजग्मतुस्ततो देशं दानवौ मधुकैटभौ ॥15॥
1.15.m: Then the Lord who possessed the horse's head vanished; / thereupon the two dānavas, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, arrived at that place.

1.15.s:
viṣṇuścakāra dehau dvau viṣṇurjiṣṇu riti smṛtau ..
madhunā yuyudhe jiṣṇurviṣṇurvai kaiṭabhena ca .. 16 ..
1.15.d:
विष्णुश्चकार देहौ द्वौ विष्णुर्जिष्णु रिति स्मृतौ ॥
मधुना युयुधे जिष्णुर्विष्णुर्वै कैटभेन च ॥ 16 ॥
1.15.m: Viṣṇu assumed two bodies, known as Viṣṇu and Jiṣṇu; / Jiṣṇu fought with Madhu, and Viṣṇu indeed with Kaiṭabha.

1.15.s:
tatastayoḥ suyuddhena tuṣṭo devo janārdanaḥ ..
uvāca tau mahākāyau dānavau madhu kaiṭabhau .. 17 ..
1.15.d:
ततस्तयोः सुयुद्धेन तुष्टो देवो जनार्दनः ॥
उवाच तौ महाकायौ दानवौ मधु कैटभौ ॥ 17 ॥
1.15.m: Then, pleased with their great fight, the god Janārdana / spoke to the two gigantic dānavas, Madhu and Kaiṭabha:

1.15.s:
varaṃ varayatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhavantāvaparājitau ..
tāvabrūtāṃ tato devaṃ viṣṇuṃ kamalalocanam .. 18 ..
1.15.d:
वरं वरयतां श्रेष्ठं भवन्तावपराजितौ ॥
तावब्रूतां ततो देवं विष्णुं कमललोचनम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.15.m: 'Choose a supreme boon, since you two are undefeated.' / Thereupon the two spoke to the lotus-eyed god Viṣṇu:

1.15.s:
putro'smākaṃ bhaveddeva mahābalaparākramaḥ ..
putre jāte tu yau tau dvau viṣṇunā jiṣṇunā purā .. 19 ..
1.15.d:
पुत्रोऽस्माकं भवेद्देव महाबलपराक्रमः ॥
पुत्रे जाते तु यौ तौ द्वौ विष्णुना जिष्णुना पुरा ॥ 19 ॥
1.15.m: 'O god, may a son of great strength and valor be born to us.' / After that son was born, those two heroes who were formerly

1.15.s:
nihatau ca tadā vīrau hyudakaṃ ca samāśritau ..
medo mumucatustatra vyāptā yenābhavanmahī .. .. 1.15.20 ..
1.15.d:
निहतौ च तदा वीरौ ह्युदकं च समाश्रितौ ॥
मेदो मुमुचतुस्तत्र व्याप्ता येनाभवन्मही ॥ ॥ 1.15.20 ॥
1.15.m: slain by Viṣṇu and Jiṣṇu, resting in the water, / released fat there, by which the earth was permeated.

1.15.s:
medinīti tataḥ khyātā loke'smiṃstattvacintakaiḥ ..
varāharūpeṇa tadā coddhṛtā vasudhā tataḥ .. 21 ..
1.15.d:
मेदिनीति ततः ख्याता लोकेऽस्मिंस्तत्त्वचिन्तकैः ॥
वराहरूपेण तदा चोद्धृता वसुधा ततः ॥ 21 ॥
1.15.m: Therefore it was named Medinī in this world by those who contemplate the truth. / Then the earth was lifted up in the form of a boar;

1.15.s:
tenaiva devadevena pūrvasthāne nive śitā ..
sargaṃ cakre tato brahmā devadevasya śāsanāt .. 22 ..
1.15.d:
तेनैव देवदेवेन पूर्वस्थाने निवे शिता ॥
सर्गं चक्रे ततो ब्रह्मा देवदेवस्य शासनात् ॥ 22 ॥
1.15.m: by that very god of gods it was established in its former place. / Then Brahmā carried out creation by command of the god of gods.

1.15.s:
evaṃ tadā devavarasya yuddhe nipātitau tau madhukaiṭabhākhyau ..
devasya viṣṇoḥ sadanaṃ prayātau kṣīrārṇave tasya samīpagau ca .. 23..
1.15.d:
एवं तदा देववरस्य युद्धे निपातितौ तौ मधुकैटभाख्यौ ॥
देवस्य विष्णोः सदनं प्रयातौ क्षीरार्णवे तस्य समीपगौ च ॥ 23॥
1.15.m: Thus the two named Madhu and Kaiṭabha, struck down in battle by the foremost of the gods, / went to the abode of the god Viṣṇu and approached near him in the Ocean of Milk.

1.16.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
bhāratasyāsya varṣasya bhāge'sminnavame nṛpa! ..
samudro vālukāpūrṇa ujjānaka iti śrutiḥ .. 1 ..
1.16.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
भारतस्यास्य वर्षस्य भागेऽस्मिन्नवमे नृप! ॥
समुद्रो वालुकापूर्ण उज्जानक इति श्रुतिः ॥ 1 ॥
1.16.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
In this ninth region of the land of Bhārata, O king, / is an ocean filled with sand, renowned as Ujjānaka.

1.16.s:
tasya madhye samudrasya dhundhuprasthapateḥ sadā ..
saṃvatsarasya sonte tu mahocchvāsaṃ pramuñcati ..2..
1.16.d:
तस्य मध्ये समुद्रस्य धुन्धुप्रस्थपतेः सदा ॥
संवत्सरस्य सोन्ते तु महोच्छ्वासं प्रमुञ्चति ॥2॥
1.16.m: In the middle of that ocean, the lord of Dhundhuprastha always / releases a great exhalation at the end of the year.

1.16.s:
yadā tadā bhūḥ skhalati saśailavanakānanā.
prāṇino ye'lpasattvāśca te yānti yamasādanam .. 3 ..
1.16.d:
यदा तदा भूः स्खलति सशैलवनकानना।
प्राणिनो येऽल्पसत्त्वाश्च ते यान्ति यमसादनम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.16.m: When [he does] then, the earth stumbles, together with its mountains, forests, and groves; / and living beings that have little strength go to the abode of Yama.

1.16.s:
yadā vibuddho bhavati kiñciccheṣā mahī tadā ..
āhārārthaṃ karotyugraḥ pāpātmā jalarākṣasaḥ .. 4 ..
1.16.d:
यदा विबुद्धो भवति किञ्चिच्छेषा मही तदा ॥
आहारार्थं करोत्युग्रः पापात्मा जलराक्षसः ॥ 4 ॥
1.16.m: When he is awakened, with just a little of the earth remaining [undisturbed], / the fierce, evil-minded water-rākṣasa then acts for the sake of food.

1.16.s:
etasminneva kāle tu cottaṅkastapyate tapaḥ ..
tapasonte mahātmānaṃ dadarśa madhusūdanam .. 5 ..
1.16.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु चोत्तङ्कस्तप्यते तपः ॥
तपसोन्ते महात्मानं ददर्श मधुसूदनम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.16.m: At that very time, however, Uttaṅka was performing austerities. / At the end of his austerities, he beheld the high-souled Madhusūdana.

1.16.s:
tamuvāca harirdevo varaṃ varaya bhārgava . ..
uttaṃkaḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā tuṣṭāva madhusūdanam .. 6 ..
1.16.d:
तमुवाच हरिर्देवो वरं वरय भार्गव ॥।
उत्तंकः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा तुष्टाव मधुसूदनम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.16.m: Lord Hari said to him, 'Choose a boon, O descendant of Bhṛgu!' / Uttaṅka, folding his hands, praised Madhusūdana.

1.16.s:
uvāca varadaṃ devameṣa eva varo mama ..
yadahaṃ devadevasya dṛṣṭavāṃścaraṇāmbujau .. 7 ..
1.16.d:
उवाच वरदं देवमेष एव वरो मम ॥
यदहं देवदेवस्य दृष्टवांश्चरणाम्बुजौ ॥ 7 ॥
1.16.m: He said to the boon-granting god, 'This indeed is my boon: / that I have seen the lotus-like feet of the God of gods.'

1.16.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca ..
avaśyaṃ te varo deyo mayā bhṛgukulodvaha ..
ajaraścāmaraścaiva matprasādādbhaviṣyasi .. 8 ..
1.16.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ॥
अवश्यं ते वरो देयो मया भृगुकुलोद्वह ॥
अजरश्चामरश्चैव मत्प्रसादाद्भविष्यसि ॥ 8 ॥
1.16.m:
The Holy One said:
'A boon must surely be given to you by me, O perpetuator of the Bhṛgu lineage: / by my grace you shall become free from old age and immortal.

1.16.s:
yatrecchasi jalaṃ tatra bhaviṣyati tathā tava ..
devatānāṃ mahatkāryaṃ tathaiva ca kariṣyasi .. 9 ..
1.16.d:
यत्रेच्छसि जलं तत्र भविष्यति तथा तव ॥
देवतानां महत्कार्यं तथैव च करिष्यसि ॥ 9 ॥
1.16.m: Wherever you desire water, there it shall be for you as well; / and likewise, you shall accomplish a great task for the deities.

1.16.s:
āśramasyāsya te bādhāṃ yaḥ karoti sadānagha ..
kuvalāśvena taṃ gatvā dhuṃdhu ghātaya mā ciram .. 1.16.10 ..
1.16.d:
आश्रमस्यास्य ते बाधां यः करोति सदानघ ॥
कुवलाश्वेन तं गत्वा धुंधु घातय मा चिरम् ॥ 1.16.10 ॥
1.16.m: He who continually causes affliction to this hermitage of yours, O sinless one— / go, have that Dhundhu slain by Kuvalāśva without delay!

1.16.s:
ahaṃ cāsya pravekṣyāmi kuvalāśvasya vigraham ..
tejasā sa madīyena dhuṃdhumājau haniṣyati .. 11 ..
1.16.d:
अहं चास्य प्रवेक्ष्यामि कुवलाश्वस्य विग्रहम् ॥
तेजसा स मदीयेन धुंधुमाजौ हनिष्यति ॥ 11 ॥
1.16.m: And I shall enter the body of this Kuvalāśva; / by my splendour he will slay Dhundhu in battle.

1.16.s:
na hyalpatejasā hantuṃ dhuṃdhuḥ śakyo bhṛgūttama ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
etāvaduktvā bhagavān gato'ntardhānamīśvaraḥ .. 12 ..
1.16.d:
न ह्यल्पतेजसा हन्तुं धुंधुः शक्यो भृगूत्तम ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एतावदुक्त्वा भगवान् गतोऽन्तर्धानमीश्वरः ॥ 12 ॥
1.16.m:
For Dhundhu cannot be slain by one of small splendour, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.' / Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having spoken thus much, the Lord, the Sovereign, vanished.

1.16.s:
jagāma ca tathāyodhyāmuttaṃko'pi mahātapāḥ ..
pūjito bṛhadaśvena bṛhadaśvamabhāṣata .. 13 ..
1.16.d:
जगाम च तथायोध्यामुत्तंकोऽपि महातपाः ॥
पूजितो बृहदश्वेन बृहदश्वमभाषत ॥ 13 ॥
1.16.m: And Uttaṅka, of great austerity, likewise went to Ayodhyā. / Honoured by Bṛhadaśva, he addressed Bṛhadaśva:

1.16.s:
utaṅka uvāca ..
kathaṃ nidrāsi rājendra sukhaṃ paryaṅkamāsthitaḥ ..
dhundhoścaritamālokya baddhakakṣo bhavādhunā .. 14 ..
1.16.d:
उतङ्क उवाच ॥
कथं निद्रासि राजेन्द्र सुखं पर्यङ्कमास्थितः ॥
धुन्धोश्चरितमालोक्य बद्धकक्षो भवाधुना ॥ 14 ॥
1.16.m:
Uttaṅka said:
'How can you sleep comfortably reclining on your couch, O best of kings? / Having observed the conduct of Dhundhu, gird your loins right now!

1.16.s:
vacanānmama rājendra dhuṃdhuṃ hantuṃ tavāsti bhoḥ ..
śaktiḥ kimudyamādrājñāṃ duṣkaraṃ te punaḥ katham .. 15 ..
1.16.d:
वचनान्मम राजेन्द्र धुंधुं हन्तुं तवास्ति भोः ॥
शक्तिः किमुद्यमाद्राज्ञां दुष्करं ते पुनः कथम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.16.m: At my word, O best of kings, you have the power to slay Dhundhu. / What is difficult for kings through exertion, and how [could it be so] for you?

1.16.s:
jahi dhuṃdhuṃ mahākāyaṃ nṛpate dvijabādhakam ..
śrutvā munivaco rājā kuvalāśvamabhāṣata .. 16 ..
1.16.d:
जहि धुंधुं महाकायं नृपते द्विजबाधकम् ॥
श्रुत्वा मुनिवचो राजा कुवलाश्वमभाषत ॥ 16 ॥
1.16.m: Slay Dhundhu of immense body, O king, who afflicts the twice-born!' / Having heard the sage's words, the king spoke to Kuvalāśva:

1.16.s:
ahaṃ vanapravṛttastu tyaktadaṇḍastathaiva ca ..
jahi taṃ dānavaśreṣṭhaṃ tvamuttaṅkena pālitaḥ .. 17 ..
1.16.d:
अहं वनप्रवृत्तस्तु त्यक्तदण्डस्तथैव च ॥
जहि तं दानवश्रेष्ठं त्वमुत्तङ्केन पालितः ॥ 17 ॥
1.16.m: 'I have set out for the forest and have also laid down the rod of punishment. / Protected by Uttaṅka, slay that foremost of the dānavas!'

1.16.s:
evamuktaḥ pariṣvaktaḥ pitrā prakṛtivatsalaḥ ..
uttaṅkasahito gatvā yuddhāyodakarākṣasam .. 18 ..
1.16.d:
एवमुक्तः परिष्वक्तः पित्रा प्रकृतिवत्सलः ॥
उत्तङ्कसहितो गत्वा युद्धायोदकराक्षसम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.16.m: Thus addressed and embraced by his father, he who was affectionate to his subjects, / having gone together with Uttaṅka to fight the water-rākṣasa,

1.16.s:
yuyudhe taṃ ca dharmātmā dhuṃdhuṃ tenaiva keśavaḥ ..
utaṅkānumate paścādbrahmāstreṇa jaghāna tam .. 19 ..
1.16.d:
युयुधे तं च धर्मात्मा धुंधुं तेनैव केशवः ॥
उतङ्कानुमते पश्चाद्ब्रह्मास्त्रेण जघान तम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.16.m: and the righteous-minded one fought with him, with Dhundhu, [and] through him Keśava [fought]. / Then, with Uttaṅka's permission, he slew him with the Brahmā weapon.

1.16.s:
hatvā taṃ rākṣasaṃ lebhe tridaśebhyastadā varān ..
kṛṣṇe bhaktiṃ sthitiṃ dharme vāsaṃ svarge tathākṣayam .. 1.16.20 ..
1.16.d:
हत्वा तं राक्षसं लेभे त्रिदशेभ्यस्तदा वरान् ॥
कृष्णे भक्तिं स्थितिं धर्मे वासं स्वर्गे तथाक्षयम् ॥ 1.16.20 ॥
1.16.m: Having slain that rākṣasa, he then received boons from the gods: / devotion to Kṛṣṇa, steadfastness in dharma, and imperishable residence in heaven.

1.16.s:
madhukaiṭabhayoḥ putraṃ ghātayitvā narādhipa ..
dhundhumāratvamagamadaśobhata tathā purīm .. 21 ..
1.16.d:
मधुकैटभयोः पुत्रं घातयित्वा नराधिप ॥
धुन्धुमारत्वमगमदशोभत तथा पुरीम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.16.m: Having caused the son of Madhu and Kaiṭabha to be slain, O lord of men, / he attained the title of Dhundhumāra and graced the city.

1.16.s:
tasminhate daityavare prasannā diśo babhūvurmuditāśca devāḥ ..
vinaṣṭavighnaṃ ca jagattadāsa rājā ca kīrtiṃ paramāmavāpa .. 22 ..
1.16.d:
तस्मिन्हते दैत्यवरे प्रसन्ना दिशो बभूवुर्मुदिताश्च देवाः ॥
विनष्टविघ्नं च जगत्तदास राजा च कीर्तिं परमामवाप ॥ 22 ॥
1.16.m: When that foremost of daityas was slain, the directions became clear, and the gods rejoiced; / the world then became free from obstacles, and the king attained supreme renown.

1.17.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
dhuṃdhumārāddṛḍhāśvastu haryaśvastasya cātmajaḥ ..
nikuṃbhastasya tanayaḥ suhitaśca tadātmajaḥ......
bhṛśāśvastanayastasya māndhātā tasya cātmajaḥ..
daivena vidhinā rājā jātastasyaiva codarāt .. 2 ..
1.17.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
धुंधुमाराद्दृढाश्वस्तु हर्यश्वस्तस्य चात्मजः ॥
निकुंभस्तस्य तनयः सुहितश्च तदात्मजः॥॥॥
भृशाश्वस्तनयस्तस्य मान्धाता तस्य चात्मजः॥
दैवेन विधिना राजा जातस्तस्यैव चोदरात् ॥ 2 ॥
1.17.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
From Dhundhumāra [was born] Dṛḍhāśva, and Haryaśva was his son. / Nikuṃbha was his son, and Suhita was his son. / […] / Bhṛśāśva was his son, and Māndhātṛ was his son; / by divine decree, the king was born indeed from his belly.

1.17.s:
purukutsaḥ sutastasya trasaddasyustadātmajaḥ ..
śambhustasyātmajaḥ śrīmānanaraṇyeti viśrutaḥ ..3..
1.17.d:
पुरुकुत्सः सुतस्तस्य त्रसद्दस्युस्तदात्मजः ॥
शम्भुस्तस्यात्मजः श्रीमाननरण्येति विश्रुतः ॥3॥
1.17.m: Purukutsa was his son, and Trasaddasyu was his son; / his son was the glorious Sambhu, renowned as Anaraṇya,

1.17.s:
rāvaṇena hato yo'sau trilokavijayī purā ..
dṛśadaśvaḥ sutastasya tasmādvasumanā nṛpaḥ .. 4 ..
1.17.d:
रावणेन हतो योऽसौ त्रिलोकविजयी पुरा ॥
दृशदश्वः सुतस्तस्य तस्माद्वसुमना नृपः ॥ 4 ॥
1.17.m: who was slain in ancient times by Rāvaṇa, the conqueror of the three worlds. / Dṛśadaśva was his son, and from him [was born] King Vasumanas.

1.17.s:
tasya putrastridhanvākhyaḥ tasmāttryyāraṇiḥ smṛtaḥ ..
tasya satyavrataḥ putraḥ triśaṅkuṃ yaṃ pracakṣate .. 5 ..
1.17.d:
तस्य पुत्रस्त्रिधन्वाख्यः तस्मात्त्र्य्यारणिः स्मृतः ॥
तस्य सत्यव्रतः पुत्रः त्रिशङ्कुं यं प्रचक्षते ॥ 5 ॥
1.17.m: His son was named Tridhanvan; from him Tryyāruṇa is remembered. / His son was Satyavrata, whom they call Triśaṅku.

1.17.s:
hariścandraḥ sutastasya rohitāśvastadātmajaḥ ..
haritastatsuto rājā cañcurhārita ucyate .. 6 ..
1.17.d:
हरिश्चन्द्रः सुतस्तस्य रोहिताश्वस्तदात्मजः ॥
हरितस्तत्सुतो राजा चञ्चुर्हारित उच्यते ॥ 6 ॥
1.17.m: Hariścandra was his son, and Rohitāśva was his son. / Harita was his son, and King Cañcu is called Hārita.

1.17.s:
vijayastasya tanayaścālarkastasya cātmajaḥ ..
alarkasya vṛkaḥ putrastasmādbāhustu jajñivān ..7..
1.17.d:
विजयस्तस्य तनयश्चालर्कस्तस्य चात्मजः ॥
अलर्कस्य वृकः पुत्रस्तस्माद्बाहुस्तु जज्ञिवान् ॥7॥
1.17.m: Vijaya was his son, and Alarka was his son; / Alarka's son was Vṛka, and from him Bāhu was born.

1.17.s:
pānastrīmṛgayākṣeṣu sa bahuvyasanānvitaḥ ..
vyasane tasya saktasya narendrasyāribhistadā .. 8 ..
1.17.d:
पानस्त्रीमृगयाक्षेषु स बहुव्यसनान्वितः ॥
व्यसने तस्य सक्तस्य नरेन्द्रस्यारिभिस्तदा ॥ 8 ॥
1.17.m: He was addicted to many vices: drinking, women, hunting, and gambling. / While that king was devoted to vice, then by enemies—

1.17.s:
haihayaistālajaṅghaiśca sarvamlecchagaṇāvṛtaiḥ ..
chalenāpahṛtaṃ rājyaṃ hṛtarājyo vanaṃ gataḥ .. 9 ..
1.17.d:
हैहयैस्तालजङ्घैश्च सर्वम्लेच्छगणावृतैः ॥
छलेनापहृतं राज्यं हृतराज्यो वनं गतः ॥ 9 ॥
1.17.m: by the Haihayas and the Tālajaṅghas, surrounded by hosts of all [manner of] mlecchas— / his kingdom was seized through deceit. Having lost his kingdom, he went to the forest.

1.17.s:
padbhyāmanuyayau tasya vanaṃ bhāryā guṇānvitā ..
gurviṇī prāgdadau yasyāḥ sapatnī tu garaṃ kila ..1.17.1 0..
1.17.d:
पद्भ्यामनुययौ तस्य वनं भार्या गुणान्विता ॥
गुर्विणी प्राग्ददौ यस्याः सपत्नी तु गरं किल ॥1.17.1 0॥
1.17.m: His virtuous wife followed him on foot to the forest; / pregnant, she had previously been given poison by her co-wife.

1.17.s:
tatassā sagaraṃ putraṃ suṣāva vanagā śubhā ..
jātaputro narapatiḥ saṃyuktaḥ kālakarmaṇā ..11..
1.17.d:
ततस्सा सगरं पुत्रं सुषाव वनगा शुभा ॥
जातपुत्रो नरपतिः संयुक्तः कालकर्मणा ॥11॥
1.17.m: Then, dwelling in the forest, that auspicious woman gave birth to a son, Sagara (with poison). / When the son was born, the lord of men was overtaken by the working of time.

1.17.s:
anvāruroha taṃ rājñī yādavī dharmavatsalā..
saṃskṛtaḥ sarvasaṃskāraiḥ sagaraścyavanena ca ..12..
1.17.d:
अन्वारुरोह तं राज्ञी यादवी धर्मवत्सला॥
संस्कृतः सर्वसंस्कारैः सगरश्च्यवनेन च ॥12॥
1.17.m: The queen, a Yādava princess devoted to dharma, mounted [the funeral pyre] after him. / Sagara was initiated with all the sacraments by Cyavana,

1.17.s:
śāstragrāme dhanurvede nītaḥ pāraṃ tathā param..
sa yauvanamanuprāpya eka eva narādhipaḥ..13..
1.17.d:
शास्त्रग्रामे धनुर्वेदे नीतः पारं तथा परम्॥
स यौवनमनुप्राप्य एक एव नराधिपः॥13॥
1.17.m: and was led to the supreme limit in the collection of sciences and in the science of archery. / Having attained youth, that sole lord of men,

1.17.s:
padātirbaddhanistriṃśaścyavanasya prasādataḥ ..
haihayāṃstālajaṅghāṃśca nijaghāna parantapaḥ..14..
1.17.d:
पदातिर्बद्धनिस्त्रिंशश्च्यवनस्य प्रसादतः ॥
हैहयांस्तालजङ्घांश्च निजघान परन्तपः॥14॥
1.17.m: on foot and wearing a sword, by the grace of Cyavana, / that scorcher of foes struck down the Haihayas and Tālajaṅghas.

1.17.s:
tatastvayodhyāṃ saṃprāpya lebhe rājyamakaṃṭakam..
sagaro rājyamāsādya balena caturaṅgiṇā ..15..
1.17.d:
ततस्त्वयोध्यां संप्राप्य लेभे राज्यमकंटकम्॥
सगरो राज्यमासाद्य बलेन चतुरङ्गिणा ॥15॥
1.17.m: Then, having reached Ayodhyā, he obtained a kingdom free of thorns. / Having attained the kingdom, Sagara, with a fourfold army,

1.17.s:
vijitya sakalānmlecchānvaśaṃ cakre ca pārthivān ..
vijitya pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ prāpya rājyamakaṇṭakam .. 16 ..
1.17.d:
विजित्य सकलान्म्लेच्छान्वशं चक्रे च पार्थिवान् ॥
विजित्य पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां प्राप्य राज्यमकण्टकम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.17.m: conquered all the mlecchas and brought the kings under his sway. / Having conquered the entire earth and gained an unhindered kingdom,

1.17.s:
cyavanaṃ pūjayāmāsa satkāreṇa punaḥpunaḥ ..
cyavanenābhyanujñātaḥ sa cakre dārasaṃgraham .. 17 ..
1.17.d:
च्यवनं पूजयामास सत्कारेण पुनःपुनः ॥
च्यवनेनाभ्यनुज्ञातः स चक्रे दारसंग्रहम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.17.m: he honoured Cyavana repeatedly with hospitable reverence. / Permitted by Cyavana, he took wives.

1.17.s:
āsīdbhāryādvayaṃ tasya sagarasya mahātmanaḥ ..
sa tābhyāṃ sahito rājā putrārthaṃ taptavāṃstapaḥ ..18..
1.17.d:
आसीद्भार्याद्वयं तस्य सगरस्य महात्मनः ॥
स ताभ्यां सहितो राजा पुत्रार्थं तप्तवांस्तपः ॥18॥
1.17.m: That high-souled Sagara had two wives. / Together with both of them, the king performed austerities for the sake of sons.

1.17.s:
tapasonte haraḥ prāha rājānaṃ tapasā kṛśam ..
ekaṃ vaṃśakaraṃ putramekā te janayiṣyati ..19..
1.17.d:
तपसोन्ते हरः प्राह राजानं तपसा कृशम् ॥
एकं वंशकरं पुत्रमेका ते जनयिष्यति ॥19॥
1.17.m: At the end of his austerities, Hara said to the king emaciated by ascetic toil: / 'One [wife] will give birth to one lineage-bearing son for you.

1.17.s:
ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇi dvitīyā janayiṣyati ..
evaṃ labdhavaro rājā sabhāryaḥ svapuraṃ gataḥ .. 1.17.20 ..
1.17.d:
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि द्वितीया जनयिष्यति ॥
एवं लब्धवरो राजा सभार्यः स्वपुरं गतः ॥ 1.17.20 ॥
1.17.m:
"The second will give birth to sixty thousand sons."
Having thus obtained the boon, the king returned to his city accompanied by his wives.

1.17.s:
putraṃ putrāṃśca dharmāpmā janayāmāsa vīryavān ..
karmaṇā caiva nāmnā ca rājaputro'samañjasaḥ..21..
1.17.d:
पुत्रं पुत्रांश्च धर्माप्मा जनयामास वीर्यवान् ॥
कर्मणा चैव नाम्ना च राजपुत्रोऽसमञ्जसः॥21॥
1.17.m:
The righteous, mighty [king] begot a son and [many] sons.
The prince [born as one], by both deeds and name, was Asamañjasa.

1.17.s:
pitrā vivāsito rājyātpaurāṇāmahite rataḥ..
tasya putroṃśumānnāma sarvaiḥ samudito guṇaiḥ ..
toṣayāmāsa pitaraṃ pituḥ pṛthvīpatiṃ ca saḥ .. 22 ..
1.17.d:
पित्रा विवासितो राज्यात्पौराणामहिते रतः॥
तस्य पुत्रोंशुमान्नाम सर्वैः समुदितो गुणैः ॥
तोषयामास पितरं पितुः पृथ्वीपतिं च सः ॥ 22 ॥

1.17.s:
pautreṇa tenānaghaḥ sevyamānaḥ putrairmahāvīryaparākramaiśca ..
sa rañjayanrājavaro jitāriḥ śaśāsa pṛthvīṃ sakalāṃ mahātmā .. 23 ..
1.17.d:
पौत्रेण तेनानघः सेव्यमानः पुत्रैर्महावीर्यपराक्रमैश्च ॥
स रञ्जयन्राजवरो जितारिः शशास पृथ्वीं सकलां महात्मा ॥ 23 ॥
1.17.m:
Served by that faultless grandson and by his sons of great valour and strength,
that best of kings, having conquered his foes, delighting [his subjects], ruled the whole earth, magnanimous.

1.18.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
sagarasya tu te putrāssaṃhatā vīryasaṃyutāḥ ..
saṃjātā daivayogena devabrāhmaṇakaṃṭakāḥ .. 1 ..
1.18.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
सगरस्य तु ते पुत्रास्संहता वीर्यसंयुताः ॥
संजाता दैवयोगेन देवब्राह्मणकंटकाः ॥ 1 ॥
1.18.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Those sons of Sagara, banded together and endowed with valour,
became, by the working of fate, thorns to gods and brahmins.

1.18.s:
teṣāṃ tu karmaṇodvignā devāḥ sarve pitāmaham ..
abruvansāgaraiḥ sarvairdeva bādhyāma saṃhataiḥ ..2..
1.18.d:
तेषां तु कर्मणोद्विग्ना देवाः सर्वे पितामहम् ॥
अब्रुवन्सागरैः सर्वैर्देव बाध्याम संहतैः ॥2॥
1.18.m:
Agitated by their actions, all the gods said to the Grandfather:
"O god, we are harassed by all the united sons of Sagara!"

1.18.s:
evamuktastadā brahmā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ ..
uvāca devānsakalānsāgaraiḥ pratyamarṣitān .. 3 ..
1.18.d:
एवमुक्तस्तदा ब्रह्मा सर्वलोकपितामहः ॥
उवाच देवान्सकलान्सागरैः प्रत्यमर्षितान् ॥ 3 ॥
1.18.m:
Addressed thus at that time, Brahmā, the Grandfather of all the worlds,
said to all the gods who were angered against the sons of Sagara:

1.18.s:
yastvasya jagato nāthaḥ paramātmā sanātanaḥ ..
vāsudevaḥ sa kapilaḥ surāstān ghātayiṣyati .. 4 ..
1.18.d:
यस्त्वस्य जगतो नाथः परमात्मा सनातनः ॥
वासुदेवः स कपिलः सुरास्तान् घातयिष्यति ॥ 4 ॥
1.18.m:
"He who is the lord of this universe, the eternal Supreme Self,
Vāsudeva, as Kapila, O gods, will slay them."

1.18.s:
evamuktāḥ surā stena yayuḥ sarve triviṣṭapam ..
etasminneva kāle tu sagaraḥ sa mahīpatiḥ .. 5 ..
1.18.d:
एवमुक्ताः सुरा स्तेन ययुः सर्वे त्रिविष्टपम् ॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु सगरः स महीपतिः ॥ 5 ॥
1.18.m:
Addressed thus by him, all the gods went to heaven.
At that very time, King Sagara

1.18.s:
dīkṣito vājimedhāya vidhivadvedapāragaiḥ ..
turaṅgaṃ cārayāmāsuryajñiyaṃ tanayā mahīm .. 6 ..
1.18.d:
दीक्षितो वाजिमेधाय विधिवद्वेदपारगैः ॥
तुरङ्गं चारयामासुर्यज्ञियं तनया महीम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.18.m:
was consecrated for the horse sacrifice according to rule by those who had crossed to the end of the Vedas.
His sons roamed the earth with the sacrificial horse.

1.18.s:
teṣāṃ cārayatāṃ so'śvaḥ kapilena tathā hṛtaḥ ..
kapilena hṛtaṃ nāśvaṃ te jānanti vimohitāḥ .. 7 ..
1.18.d:
तेषां चारयतां सोऽश्वः कपिलेन तथा हृतः ॥
कपिलेन हृतं नाश्वं ते जानन्ति विमोहिताः ॥ 7 ॥
1.18.m:
As they were roaming, that horse was taken away by Kapila.
Deluded, they did not know the horse to have been taken by Kapila.

1.18.s:
anveṣanto'pi yatnena nāpuste turagaṃ yataḥ ..
pitre nivedya te sarve nicakhnuḥ pṛthivītalam .. 8 ..
1.18.d:
अन्वेषन्तोऽपि यत्नेन नापुस्ते तुरगं यतः ॥
पित्रे निवेद्य ते सर्वे निचख्नुः पृथिवीतलम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.18.m:
Searching with effort, since they did not find the horse,
they reported to their father, and all of them dug into the surface of the earth.

1.18.s:
bhāratasyāsya varṣasya bhede'sminnavame nṛpa! ..
samantatastataścakruḥ khātakarmabalānvitāḥ .. 9 ..
1.18.d:
भारतस्यास्य वर्षस्य भेदेऽस्मिन्नवमे नृप! ॥
समन्ततस्ततश्चक्रुः खातकर्मबलान्विताः ॥ 9 ॥
1.18.m:
In this ninth division of this Bhārata realm, O king,
endowed with strength, they then carried out the work of excavation all around,

1.18.s:
vistarādyojanaśataṃ pātālatalagāminam ..
vaiḍūryapavartātpūrvamuttareṇa himācalāt .. 1.18.10 ..
1.18.d:
विस्तराद्योजनशतं पातालतलगामिनम् ॥
वैडूर्यपवर्तात्पूर्वमुत्तरेण हिमाचलात् ॥ 1.18.10 ॥
1.18.m:
a hundred yojanas in width, reaching down to the underworld,
east of the Vaiḍūrya mountain and north of the Himālaya,

1.18.s:
paścārdhe kāñcanagirerudageva ca lāvaṇāt ..
himācalaśca tairvīraḥ rājandeśadvaye kṣataḥ .. 11 ..
1.18.d:
पश्चार्धे काञ्चनगिरेरुदगेव च लावणात् ॥
हिमाचलश्च तैर्वीरः राजन्देशद्वये क्षतः ॥ 11 ॥
1.18.m:
in the western half of the Golden Mountain and north of the Salt [Ocean].
And the Himālaya, O hero, O king, was breached by them in two regions,

1.18.s:
himācalasya khaṇḍaśca khātasyāntaḥ praveśitaḥ ..
uttaraḥ sāgarastasmāddhima śailena durgamaḥ .. 12 ..
1.18.d:
हिमाचलस्य खण्डश्च खातस्यान्तः प्रवेशितः ॥
उत्तरः सागरस्तस्माद्धिम शैलेन दुर्गमः ॥ 12 ॥
1.18.m:
and a portion of the Himālaya was hurled into the excavation.
From that, the northern ocean is difficult of access because of the snow-mountain.

1.18.s:
evaṃvidhena khātena te praviśya pṛthakpṛthak ..
ekīkṛtā daivayogātkapilo yatra vai sthitaḥ .. 13 ..
1.18.d:
एवंविधेन खातेन ते प्रविश्य पृथक्पृथक् ॥
एकीकृता दैवयोगात्कपिलो यत्र वै स्थितः ॥ 13 ॥
1.18.m:
Entering separately through such an excavation,
they were brought together by the power of fate right where Kapila stood.

1.18.s:
kapilasya samīpasthaṃ dadṛśuste turaṅgamam ..
turaṅgasahitaṃ dṛṣṭvā kapilaṃ te tvamarṣitāḥ .. 14 ..
1.18.d:
कपिलस्य समीपस्थं ददृशुस्ते तुरङ्गमम् ॥
तुरङ्गसहितं दृष्ट्वा कपिलं ते त्वमर्षिताः ॥ 14 ॥
1.18.m:
They saw the horse standing near Kapila.
Seeing Kapila together with the horse, enraged,

1.18.s:
kuddālalepikāhastāstasya jagmurvadhepsayā ..
tānbādhamānāndurbuddhīnsa dadarśa tadā ṛṣiḥ .. 15 ..
1.18.d:
कुद्दाललेपिकाहस्तास्तस्य जग्मुर्वधेप्सया ॥
तान्बाधमानान्दुर्बुद्धीन्स ददर्श तदा ऋषिः ॥ 15 ॥
1.18.m:
with spades and trowels in hand, they advanced with the desire to kill him.
The sage then saw those evil-minded ones assailing him.

1.18.s:
cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭamātrāste bhasmībhūtāstu sāgarāḥ ..
narakaṃ ca gatāḥ sarve devabrāhmaṇakaṇṭakāḥ .. 16 ..
1.18.d:
चक्षुषा दृष्टमात्रास्ते भस्मीभूतास्तु सागराः ॥
नरकं च गताः सर्वे देवब्राह्मणकण्टकाः ॥ 16 ॥
1.18.m:
As soon as they were seen with his eye, those sons of Sagara were reduced to ashes,
and all those thorns to gods and brahmins went to hell.

1.18.s:
vijñāya tanayānnaṣṭānnāradātsagaro nṛpaḥ ..
preṣayāmāsa satatamaṃśumantaṃ sa dhārmikam ..17 ..
1.18.d:
विज्ञाय तनयान्नष्टान्नारदात्सगरो नृपः ॥
प्रेषयामास सततमंशुमन्तं स धार्मिकम् ॥17 ॥
1.18.m:
Learning from Nārada that his sons had perished, King Sagara
always sent the righteous Aṃśumat.

1.18.s:
aṃśumānapi saṃprāpya kapilaṃ munisattamam..
abhivādya mahātejāstuṣṭāva yadunandanaḥ .. 18 ..
1.18.d:
अंशुमानपि संप्राप्य कपिलं मुनिसत्तमम्॥
अभिवाद्य महातेजास्तुष्टाव यदुनन्दनः ॥ 18 ॥
1.18.m:
Having reached Kapila, the best of sages,
Aṃśumat also, the joy of the Yadus, endowed with great splendour, saluted and praised him.

1.18.s:
tasya tuṣṭo'tha turagaṃ dattavānkapilo muniḥ ..
aṃśumantaṃ tadovāca pitṝṇāṃ salilārthinām .. 19 ..
1.18.d:
तस्य तुष्टोऽथ तुरगं दत्तवान्कपिलो मुनिः ॥
अंशुमन्तं तदोवाच पितॄणां सलिलार्थिनाम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.18.m:
Pleased with him, the sage Kapila then gave him the horse,
and he then said to Aṃśumat regarding his ancestors who sought [funerary] water:

1.18.s:
pautraste bhavitā rājaṃstapasā tasya toṣitā ..
āgamiṣyati sā devī gaṅgā gaganamekhalā .. 1.18.20 ..
1.18.d:
पौत्रस्ते भविता राजंस्तपसा तस्य तोषिता ॥
आगमिष्यति सा देवी गङ्गा गगनमेखला ॥ 1.18.20 ॥
1.18.m:
"You will have a grandson, O king; pleased by his austerity,
that goddess Gaṅgā, whose girdle is the sky, will arrive.

1.18.s: tayā klinnamidaṃ bhasma sāgarāṇāṃ durātmanām .. 21 ..
1.18.d: तया क्लिन्नमिदं भस्म सागराणां दुरात्मनाम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.18.m: When these ashes of the wicked sons of Sagara

1.18.s:
yadā bhaviṣyati tadā sāgarāḥ svargagāminaḥ ..
anyasyāpi yadā tvasthi gaṅgātoye patiṣyati .. 22 ..
1.18.d:
यदा भविष्यति तदा सागराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥
अन्यस्यापि यदा त्वस्थि गङ्गातोये पतिष्यति ॥ 22 ॥
1.18.m:
are wetted by her, then the sons of Sagara will go to heaven.
Moreover, whenever the bone of anyone else falls into the water of the Gaṅgā,

1.18.s:
tasyāpi svarlokagatirbhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ..
evamuktoṃśumāñśīghraṃ cābhivādya jagadgurum .. 23 ..
1.18.d:
तस्यापि स्वर्लोकगतिर्भविष्यति न संशयः ॥
एवमुक्तोंशुमाञ्शीघ्रं चाभिवाद्य जगद्गुरुम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.18.m:
he too will attain the heavenly world, without a doubt."
Having been addressed thus, Aṃśumat quickly saluted the teacher of the universe,

1.18.s:
āgamya yojayāmāsa turageṇa pitāmaham ..
yajñaṃ samāpayāmāsa sagaro'pi mahīpatiḥ .. 24 ..
1.18.d:
आगम्य योजयामास तुरगेण पितामहम् ॥
यज्ञं समापयामास सगरोऽपि महीपतिः ॥ 24 ॥
1.18.m:
and returning, united his grandfather with the horse.
King Sagara also completed the sacrifice.

1.18.s:
evaṃ hi sāgarairmattaiḥ khātako nṛpasattama ..
yena klṛptamidaṃ dvīpaṃ sāgaraṃ nṛpa kathyate.. .. 25 ..
1.18.d:
एवं हि सागरैर्मत्तैः खातको नृपसत्तम ॥
येन क्लृप्तमिदं द्वीपं सागरं नृप कथ्यते॥ ॥ 25 ॥
1.18.m:
Thus, indeed, the trench [was dug] by the frenzied sons of Sagara, O best of kings,
by which this continent was formed, and is called Sāgara, O king.

1.18.s:
lavaṇodātsamudrācca toyena nṛpa sāgaraḥ..
yadā pūrṇastadā jāto lavaṇodo narādhipa! .. 26 ..
1.18.d:
लवणोदात्समुद्राच्च तोयेन नृप सागरः॥
यदा पूर्णस्तदा जातो लवणोदो नराधिप! ॥ 26 ॥
1.18.m:
When the ocean was filled with water from the Salt Ocean, O king,
then, O ruler of men, the Salt Ocean arose.

1.18.s:
kṛtsnaṃ ya evaṃ jayati sa samrāḍiti kīrtyate ..
tato gataḥ sa dharmātmā kālena mahatā divam .. 27 ..
1.18.d:
कृत्स्नं य एवं जयति स सम्राडिति कीर्त्यते ॥
ततो गतः स धर्मात्मा कालेन महता दिवम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.18.m:
He who conquers the whole [earth] thus is proclaimed an emperor.
Then, after a long time, that righteous [king] went to heaven.

1.18.s:
dilīpe bhāramāsajya jagāma tanaye svake ..
dilīpo'pi samādāya rājyaṃ putraṃ bhagīratham .. 28 ..
1.18.d:
दिलीपे भारमासज्य जगाम तनये स्वके ॥
दिलीपोऽपि समादाय राज्यं पुत्रं भगीरथम् ॥ 28 ॥
1.18.m:
Entrusting the burden [of kingship] to his son Dilīpa, he departed.
Dilīpa also, having assumed the kingdom, [later gave it to] his son Bhagīratha,

1.18.s:
jagāma tridivaṃ rājā vane taptvā mahattapaḥ ..
āsādya rājyaṃ sa bhagīratho'pi ānīya gaṅgāṃ tapasā ca bhūmim .. 29 ..
1.18.d:
जगाम त्रिदिवं राजा वने तप्त्वा महत्तपः ॥
आसाद्य राज्यं स भगीरथोऽपि आनीय गङ्गां तपसा च भूमिम् ॥ 29 ॥
1.18.m:
and the king went to heaven after performing great austerities in the forest.
Bhagīratha too, having obtained the kingship and brought the Gaṅgā to earth through austerity,

1.18.s: saṃplāvayāmāsa jalena bhasma tatsāgarāṇāṃ yaduvṛndanātha! .. 1.18.30 ..
1.18.d: संप्लावयामास जलेन भस्म तत्सागराणां यदुवृन्दनाथ! ॥ 1.18.30 ॥
1.18.m: inundated with water those ashes of the sons of Sagara, O lord of the host of Yadus!

1.18.s:
saṃplāvite bhasmani rājaputrā gaṅgājalaughena divaṃ prayātāḥ ..
svarlokamāsādya tathā'kṣayaṃ te vasanti hṛṣṭāstridaśaiḥ sametāḥ ..31..
1.18.d:
संप्लाविते भस्मनि राजपुत्रा गङ्गाजलौघेन दिवं प्रयाताः ॥
स्वर्लोकमासाद्य तथाऽक्षयं ते वसन्ति हृष्टास्त्रिदशैः समेताः ॥31॥
1.18.m:
When the ashes were flooded by the torrent of Gaṅgā's water, the princes went to heaven;
and reaching that imperishable heavenly world, they dwell delighted, united with the thirty [gods].

1.19.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
rājyaṃ prāpya mahātejā dilīpatanayo nṛpaḥ ..
narakasthān pitṝñśrutvā rājyaṃ nyasyāśu vṛddhaye ..1..
1.19.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
राज्यं प्राप्य महातेजा दिलीपतनयो नृपः ॥
नरकस्थान् पितॄञ्श्रुत्वा राज्यं न्यस्याशु वृद्धये ॥1॥
1.19.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having obtained the kingship, the highly splendid king, the son of Dilīpa,
hearing that his ancestors were in hell, quickly entrusted the kingdom to an elder,

1.19.s:
gaṅgāmārādhayāmāsa tapasā mahatā tadā ..
yamaiśca niyamai rājannaparṇāśanakaistathā .. 2..
1.19.d:
गङ्गामाराधयामास तपसा महता तदा ॥
यमैश्च नियमै राजन्नपर्णाशनकैस्तथा ॥ 2॥
1.19.m:
and then worshipped Gaṅgā with great austerity,
with restraints, O king, and observances, and by subsisting on non-fallen leaves.

1.19.s:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi tapastepe bhṛśaṃ nṛpaḥ ..
atha gaṃgā mahādevī prasannābhūdgataklamā .. 3 ..
1.19.d:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि तपस्तेपे भृशं नृपः ॥
अथ गंगा महादेवी प्रसन्नाभूद्गतक्लमा ॥ 3 ॥
1.19.m:
For ten thousand years the king performed severe austerity.
Then the great goddess Gaṅgā was pleased, her fatigue departed.

1.19.s:
bhagīratho'pi dharmātmā varaṃ lebhe kutūhalī ..
tato lekhanadī devī prāvocattaṃ bhagīratham .. 4 ..
1.19.d:
भगीरथोऽपि धर्मात्मा वरं लेभे कुतूहली ॥
ततो लेखनदी देवी प्रावोचत्तं भगीरथम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.19.m:
The righteous Bhagīratha, filled with wonder, received a boon.
Then the divine river of the gods spoke to that Bhagīratha:

1.19.s: patantyā gaganātsoḍhuṃ mama vegaṃ vasundharā .. 5 ..
1.19.d: पतन्त्या गगनात्सोढुं मम वेगं वसुन्धरा ॥ 5 ॥
1.19.m: "As I fall from the sky, to bear my momentum the earth

1.19.s:
na samarthā yadā tasmāttoṣayasvāśu śaṃkaram ..
sa hi śaktaḥ pataṃtyā me vegaṃ soḍhuṃ nareśvara..6..
1.19.d:
न समर्था यदा तस्मात्तोषयस्वाशु शंकरम् ॥
स हि शक्तः पतंत्या मे वेगं सोढुं नरेश्वर॥6॥
1.19.m:
is not able; therefore quickly propitiate Śaṅkara.
