For he is capable of bearing my momentum as I fall, O ruler of men."

1.19.s:
evamuktvā yayau devī tadāntardhānamīśvarī..
bhagīratho'pi dharmātmā tapastepe sudāruṇam..7..
1.19.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ययौ देवी तदान्तर्धानमीश्वरी॥
भगीरथोऽपि धर्मात्मा तपस्तेपे सुदारुणम्॥7॥
1.19.m:
Having spoken thus, the sovereign goddess then vanished.
And the righteous Bhagīratha performed very severe austerity

1.19.s:
ārādhanārthaṃ devasya śaṅkarasya mahātmanaḥ..
tapaso'nte mahātejā dṛṣṭavāñjagadīśvaram..8..
1.19.d:
आराधनार्थं देवस्य शङ्करस्य महात्मनः॥
तपसोऽन्ते महातेजा दृष्टवाञ्जगदीश्वरम्॥8॥
1.19.m:
to propitiate the god, the magnanimous Śaṅkara.
At the end of his austerity, the greatly splendid one saw the Lord of the Universe.

1.19.s:
devadeva uvāca..
tapasogreṇa te rājan prasanno'smi yathepsitam..
dadāmi te yato bhaktiṃ pitṝṇāṃ cākṣayaṃ yaśaḥ ..9..
1.19.d:
देवदेव उवाच॥
तपसोग्रेण ते राजन् प्रसन्नोऽस्मि यथेप्सितम्॥
ददामि ते यतो भक्तिं पितॄणां चाक्षयं यशः ॥9॥
1.19.m:
The god of gods said:
O king, by your fierce asceticism I am pleased; as you desire,
I grant you [your wish], on account of which you have devotion and imperishable renown for your ancestors.

1.19.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
evamuktastu devena pūjayitvā maheśvaram ..
jagāma gaṅgāṃ manasā rājā pūrṇamanorathaḥ ..1.19.10..
1.19.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
एवमुक्तस्तु देवेन पूजयित्वा महेश्वरम् ॥
जगाम गङ्गां मनसा राजा पूर्णमनोरथः ॥1.19.10॥
1.19.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Thus addressed by the god, the king, having worshipped Maheśvara,
his wish fulfilled, turned his mind toward Gaṅgā.

1.19.s:
śaṅkarādhiṣṭhitaṃ jñātvā nṛpateśca cikīrṣitam ..
papāta gananādgaṃgā tadā rājīvalocana! ..11..
1.19.d:
शङ्कराधिष्ठितं ज्ञात्वा नृपतेश्च चिकीर्षितम् ॥
पपात गननाद्गंगा तदा राजीवलोचन! ॥11॥
1.19.m:
Knowing that Śaṅkara had taken his stand and [knowing] the king's intention,
Gaṅgā then fell from the sky, O lotus-eyed one!

1.19.s:
gaṃgāyāḥ patanaṃ jñātvā brahmā taṃ deśamāgataḥ ..
yamendravaruṇāndevānpuraskṛtyāmitaujasaḥ .. 12 ..
1.19.d:
गंगायाः पतनं ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मा तं देशमागतः ॥
यमेन्द्रवरुणान्देवान्पुरस्कृत्यामितौजसः ॥ 12 ॥
1.19.m:
Knowing of Gaṅgā's descent, Brahmā came to that region,
placing the gods of immeasurable power at the head, with Yama, Indra, and Varuṇa.

1.19.s:
ṛṣayo nāgagandharvavidyādharamahoragāḥ ..
suparṇakinnaragaṇāstathaivāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ .. 13 ..
1.19.d:
ऋषयो नागगन्धर्वविद्याधरमहोरगाः ॥
सुपर्णकिन्नरगणास्तथैवाप्सरसां गणाः ॥ 13 ॥
1.19.m:
Sages, nāgas, gandharvas, vidyādharas, and great serpents,
troops of suparṇas and kinnaras, and likewise troops of apsarases [arrived].

1.19.s:
vimānaśatasaṃbādhaṃ tadbabhūva nabhastalam ..
prakīryamāṇaṃ kusumairdevanāgavirājitam ..
suraprabhādurnirīkṣyaṃ tadābharaṇabhāsuram ..14..
1.19.d:
विमानशतसंबाधं तद्बभूव नभस्तलम् ॥
प्रकीर्यमाणं कुसुमैर्देवनागविराजितम् ॥
सुरप्रभादुर्निरीक्ष्यं तदाभरणभासुरम् ॥14॥
1.19.m:
The vault of heaven then became crowded with hundreds of aerial chariots,
strewn with blossoms, graced by gods and nāgas,
dazzling to behold with the radiance of the gods, luminous with their ornaments,

1.19.s:
sugandhi cāru pavanaṃ suratūryanināditam ..
nabhasastasya madhyena papāta gaganānnadī ..15..
1.19.d:
सुगन्धि चारु पवनं सुरतूर्यनिनादितम् ॥
नभसस्तस्य मध्येन पपात गगनान्नदी ॥15॥
1.19.m:
fragrant and pleasant with breezes, resounding with divine musical instruments.
Through the midst of that sky the river fell from the heavens.

1.19.s:
viśāmi bhittvā pātālaṃ srotasā gṛhya śaṅkaram ..
ityevaṃ duṣṭabhāvā sā papāta haramūrdhani ..16..
1.19.d:
विशामि भित्त्वा पातालं स्रोतसा गृह्य शङ्करम् ॥
इत्येवं दुष्टभावा सा पपात हरमूर्धनि ॥16॥
1.19.m:
"I will cleave Pātāla and enter, sweeping Śaṅkara along with my current."
With such malicious intent she fell upon Hara's head.

1.19.s:
jñātvā krūramabhiprāyaṃ devyā devaḥ pinākabhṛt..
jaṭākalāpe tāṃ devīṃ tiraścakre caturmukhaḥ ..17..
1.19.d:
ज्ञात्वा क्रूरमभिप्रायं देव्या देवः पिनाकभृत्॥
जटाकलापे तां देवीं तिरश्चक्रे चतुर्मुखः ॥17॥
1.19.m:
Knowing the cruel intention of the goddess, the god who bears the Pināka,
the four-faced one, caused that goddess to vanish within the mass of his matted hair.

1.19.s:
babhrāma sā tiro bhūtvā tatraiva tvaciraṃ nadī ..
tasyāḥ pataṃtyā ye kecidbiṃdavaḥ kṣitimāgatāḥ..16..
1.19.d:
बभ्राम सा तिरो भूत्वा तत्रैव त्वचिरं नदी ॥
तस्याः पतंत्या ये केचिद्बिंदवः क्षितिमागताः॥16॥
1.19.m:
Having vanished, that river wandered right there for a short time.
Whatever drops of hers fell to the earth,

1.19.s:
taiḥ kṛtaṃ pṛthivīpāla tadā vindusaraḥ śubham..
devopi dṛṣṭvā rājānaṃ kṣudhayā vyākulendriyam .. 19 ..
1.19.d:
तैः कृतं पृथिवीपाल तदा विन्दुसरः शुभम्॥
देवोपि दृष्ट्वा राजानं क्षुधया व्याकुलेन्द्रियम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.19.m:
by them was formed, O protector of the earth, the auspicious Bindusaras lake.
Then the god, seeing the king agitated in his senses from hunger,

1.19.s: tatyāja tāṃ tadā śīghraṃ jaṭāgreṇa maheśvaraḥ ..1.19.20..
1.19.d: तत्याज तां तदा शीघ्रं जटाग्रेण महेश्वरः ॥1.19.20॥
1.19.m: Maheśvara then quickly released her from the tip of a matted lock.

1.19.s:
dhṛtagaṃgo jagāmātha tato'ntardhānamīśvaraḥ ..
maheśvaraśirobhraṣṭā praviṣṭā ca saraḥ śubham .. 21 ..
1.19.d:
धृतगंगो जगामाथ ततोऽन्तर्धानमीश्वरः ॥
महेश्वरशिरोभ्रष्टा प्रविष्टा च सरः शुभम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.19.m:
Having sustained Gaṅgā, the Lord then vanished from there.
And fallen from Maheśvara's head, she entered the auspicious lake.

1.19.s:
tasmādviniḥsṛtā bhūyaḥ saptadhā devanimnagā ..
hlādinī hrādinī caiva plāvinī ceti prācyagāḥ ..22..
1.19.d:
तस्माद्विनिःसृता भूयः सप्तधा देवनिम्नगा ॥
ह्लादिनी ह्रादिनी चैव प्लाविनी चेति प्राच्यगाः ॥22॥
1.19.m:
Issuing forth from it, the celestial river again [divided] into seven streams:
Hlādinī, Hrādinī, and Plāvinī, going to the east;

1.19.s:
sītāvaktraśca sindhuśca pratīcyabhimukhā gatāḥ ..
dakṣiṇena tathā gaṃgā bhagīrathapathānugā ..
kvacidvegena mahatā kvacinmandavisarpiṇī .. 23 ..
1.19.d:
सीतावक्त्रश्च सिन्धुश्च प्रतीच्यभिमुखा गताः ॥
दक्षिणेन तथा गंगा भगीरथपथानुगा ॥
क्वचिद्वेगेन महता क्वचिन्मन्दविसर्पिणी ॥ 23 ॥

1.19.s:
kvacitphenākulajalā kvacidāvartamālinī ..
kvacidgambhīraśabdaughā niḥśabdā ca tathā kvacit .. 24 ..
1.19.d:
क्वचित्फेनाकुलजला क्वचिदावर्तमालिनी ॥
क्वचिद्गम्भीरशब्दौघा निःशब्दा च तथा क्वचित् ॥ 24 ॥
1.19.m:
here with waters churning with foam, there garlanded with whirlpools,
here with a deep flood of sound, and likewise here soundless,

1.19.s:
kvaciddhaṃsaravoddāmā cakravākayugā kvacita ..
ūrmimālākulajalā kusumotkaramaṇḍitā..25..
1.19.d:
क्वचिद्धंसरवोद्दामा चक्रवाकयुगा क्वचित ॥
ऊर्मिमालाकुलजला कुसुमोत्करमण्डिता॥25॥
1.19.m:
here resounding unrestrained with the cries of wild geese, here with pairs of shelducks,
her waters agitated by rows of waves, adorned with heaps of blossoms,

1.19.s:
jalasattvaśatākīrṇā surasiddhasukhapradā ..
amṛtasvādusalilā harasaṃsarganirmalā .. 26 ..
1.19.d:
जलसत्त्वशताकीर्णा सुरसिद्धसुखप्रदा ॥
अमृतस्वादुसलिला हरसंसर्गनिर्मला ॥ 26 ॥
1.19.m:
teeming with hundreds of aquatic creatures, granting happiness to gods and siddhas,
her water having the taste of nectar, stainless through contact with Hara,

1.19.s:
viṣṇupādaprahārotthā sarvapāta kanāśinī ..
evaṃ saṃprāpya sā viṃdhyaṃ praviṣṭā pūrvasāgaram .. 27 ..
1.19.d:
विष्णुपादप्रहारोत्था सर्वपात कनाशिनी ॥
एवं संप्राप्य सा विंध्यं प्रविष्टा पूर्वसागरम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.19.m:
arisen from the stroke of Viṣṇu's foot, destroying all sins.
Reaching the Vindhya in this manner, she entered the eastern ocean.

1.19.s:
sāgareṇa samāsādya pātālaṃ bhīmadarśanam ..
plāvayāmāsa tadbhasma sāgarāṇāṃ mahātmanām..28..
1.19.d:
सागरेण समासाद्य पातालं भीमदर्शनम् ॥
प्लावयामास तद्भस्म सागराणां महात्मनाम्॥28॥
1.19.m:
Arriving at the terrifying Pātāla by means of the ocean,
she flooded the ashes of the high-souled sons of Sagara.

1.19.s: bhasmani plāvite sarve gatāste sāgarā divam ..29..
1.19.d: भस्मनि प्लाविते सर्वे गतास्ते सागरा दिवम् ॥29॥
1.19.m: When their ashes were submerged, all those sons of Sagara went to heaven.

1.19.s:
evaṃ dharāṃ devanadī prayātā supuṇyatoyā ṛṣivaryajuṣṭā ..
mahānubhāvā nṛpa jahnukanyā niśreṇibhūtā tridivaprayāṇe ..1.19.30..
1.19.d:
एवं धरां देवनदी प्रयाता सुपुण्यतोया ऋषिवर्यजुष्टा ॥
महानुभावा नृप जह्नुकन्या निश्रेणिभूता त्रिदिवप्रयाणे ॥1.19.30॥
1.19.m:
Thus the celestial river came to earth, possessing most sacred waters, resorted to by the foremost sages,
the daughter of Jahnu of great majesty, O king, becoming a stairway for the journey to heaven.

1.20.s:
vajra uvāca ..
bhāgīrathītvaṃ gaṅgātvaṃ devanadyā mayā śrutam ..
kirmarthaṃ jāhnavī loke kathyate sāgaraṅgamā .. 1 ..
1.20.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
भागीरथीत्वं गङ्गात्वं देवनद्या मया श्रुतम् ॥
किर्मर्थं जाह्नवी लोके कथ्यते सागरङ्गमा ॥ 1 ॥
1.20.m:
Vajra said:
I have heard of the celestial river's nature as Bhāgīrathī and as Gaṅgā.
Why is she who flows to the ocean called Jāhnavī in the world?

1.20.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
pañcālākhyo'sti viṣayo madhyadeśe mahīpate .
svadharmakarmaniratairyuto varṇāśramaiḥ sadā .. 2 ..
1.20.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
पञ्चालाख्योऽस्ति विषयो मध्यदेशे महीपते ।
स्वधर्मकर्मनिरतैर्युतो वर्णाश्रमैः सदा ॥ 2 ॥
1.20.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
There is a realm named Pañcāla in the middle country, O protector of the earth,
always filled with the social classes and life-stages engaged in the duties of their own dharma.

1.20.s:
mahodayaṃ puraṃ tatra kuśastambhena nirmitam ..
sarvaratnasamākīrṇaṃ kānyakubjeti viśrutam .. 3 ..
1.20.d:
महोदयं पुरं तत्र कुशस्तम्भेन निर्मितम् ॥
सर्वरत्नसमाकीर्णं कान्यकुब्जेति विश्रुतम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.20.m:
There is a city named Mahodaya, built by Kuśastambha,
filled with all jewels, renowned as Kānyakubjā.

1.20.s:
tasminbabhūva bhūpālo jahnuḥ paramadhārmikaḥ ..
yasya kīrtimataḥ kīrtirbrahmāṇḍaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhati .. 4 ..
1.20.d:
तस्मिन्बभूव भूपालो जह्नुः परमधार्मिकः ॥
यस्य कीर्तिमतः कीर्तिर्ब्रह्माण्डं व्याप्य तिष्ठति ॥ 4 ॥
1.20.m:
In it there lived a supremely righteous ruler of the earth, Jahnu,
whose fame, renowned as he was, stands pervading the cosmic egg.

1.20.s:
sa kadācinmahīpālo hayamedhamupāharat ..
dīkṣitasya narendrasya yajñavāṭaṃ tu nimragā .. 5 ..
plāvayāmāsa vegena jalaughairyadusattam .. 1..
1.20.d:
स कदाचिन्महीपालो हयमेधमुपाहरत् ॥
दीक्षितस्य नरेन्द्रस्य यज्ञवाटं तु निम्रगा ॥ 5 ॥
प्लावयामास वेगेन जलौघैर्यदुसत्तम् ॥ 1॥
1.20.m:
Once that ruler of the earth performed a horse sacrifice.
As the lord of men was consecrated for the rite, the river
flooded the sacrificial enclosure with speed and torrents of water, O best of the Yadus.

1.20.s: plāvite yajñavāṭe tu rājā gaṅgāṃ tadābravīt .. 6..
1.20.d: प्लाविते यज्ञवाटे तु राजा गङ्गां तदाब्रवीत् ॥ 6॥
1.20.m: When the sacrificial enclosure was flooded, the king then said to Gaṅgā:

1.20.s:
asya gaṅgai'valepasya sadyaḥ phalamavāpnuhi ..
pibāmi sakalaṃ toyaṃ tava sāgaravallabhe .. 7 ..
1.20.d:
अस्य गङ्गैऽवलेपस्य सद्यः फलमवाप्नुहि ॥
पिबामि सकलं तोयं तव सागरवल्लभे ॥ 7 ॥
1.20.m:
"Reap at once the fruit of this insolence, O Gaṅgā!
I shall drink all your water, O beloved of the ocean!"

1.20.s:
evamuktvā papau rājā sarvaṃ bhāgīrathījalam ..
tapasā mahatā rājaṃstathā yogabalena ca .. 8 ..
1.20.d:
एवमुक्त्वा पपौ राजा सर्वं भागीरथीजलम् ॥
तपसा महता राजंस्तथा योगबलेन च ॥ 8 ॥
1.20.m:
Having spoken thus, the king drank all the water of Bhāgīrathī
through his great asceticism, O king, and through the power of yoga.

1.20.s:
dṛṣṭvaiva gaṅgāṃ nistoyāṃ dīnairmunijanaistataḥ ..
prasāditastu gaṅgārthe tatyāja śravaṇena tām .. 9 ..
1.20.d:
दृष्ट्वैव गङ्गां निस्तोयां दीनैर्मुनिजनैस्ततः ॥
प्रसादितस्तु गङ्गार्थे तत्याज श्रवणेन ताम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.20.m:
Seeing Gaṅgā completely waterless, the miserable ascetics then
propitiated [him] on Gaṅgā's behalf, and he released her through his ear.

1.20.s:
duhitṛtve ca jagrāha rājā bhāgīrathīṃ tadā ..
tena sā kathitā loke jāhnavī yadunandana .. 1.20.10 ..
1.20.d:
दुहितृत्वे च जग्राह राजा भागीरथीं तदा ॥
तेन सा कथिता लोके जाह्नवी यदुनन्दन ॥ 1.20.10 ॥
1.20.m:
And the king then accepted Bhāgīrathī as his daughter;
therefore she is spoken of as Jāhnavī in the world, O delighter of the Yadus.

1.20.s:
atīva darpito rājā gaṅgāyāḥ sa yadā nṛpa ..
yaśo'rthaṃ plāvayāmāsa yajñavāṭaṃ tadānagha ..11..
1.20.d:
अतीव दर्पितो राजा गङ्गायाः स यदा नृप ॥
यशोऽर्थं प्लावयामास यज्ञवाटं तदानघ ॥11॥
1.20.m:
When that king became exceedingly proud, O king,
she flooded the sacrificial enclosure for the sake of [his] renown, O sinless one.

1.20.s:
evaṃ triloke nṛpa jahnukanyā proktā budhairviṣṇupadī pavitrā ..
himācalasyādripatestanūjā samudrapatnī varadā viśokā .. 12 ..
1.20.d:
एवं त्रिलोके नृप जह्नुकन्या प्रोक्ता बुधैर्विष्णुपदी पवित्रा ॥
हिमाचलस्याद्रिपतेस्तनूजा समुद्रपत्नी वरदा विशोका ॥ 12 ॥
1.20.m:
Thus, O king, the daughter of Jahnu, pure, having her source at Viṣṇu's foot, is declared by the wise in the three worlds,
the daughter of the Himālaya, the lord of mountains, the wife of the ocean, the granter of boons, sorrowless.

1.21.s:
vajra uvāca ..
gaṅgā viṣṇupadī loke kimarthaṃ kathitā budhaiḥ ..
tanmamācakṣva tattvena bhṛguvaṃśavivardhana! .. 1 ..
1.21.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
गङ्गा विष्णुपदी लोके किमर्थं कथिता बुधैः ॥
तन्ममाचक्ष्व तत्त्वेन भृगुवंशविवर्धन! ॥ 1 ॥
1.21.m:
Vajra said:
Why is Gaṅgā spoken of by the wise in the world as Viṣṇupadī?
Explain that to me in truth, O enhancer of the Bhṛgu lineage!

1.21.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
svāyambhuventare pūrvaṃ catvāro devatāgaṇāḥ ..
jayākhyāścājitākhyāśca śukrākhyāśca prakīrtitāḥ .. 2 ..
1.21.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
स्वायम्भुवेन्तरे पूर्वं चत्वारो देवतागणाः ॥
जयाख्याश्चाजिताख्याश्च शुक्राख्याश्च प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 2 ॥
1.21.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Formerly, in the Svāyambhuva interval, there were four groups of deities,
proclaimed as the Jayas, the Ajitas, and the Śukras.

1.21.s:
teṣāṃ babhūva devendro viśvabhuglokapūjitaḥ ..
āsaṃstasyā surā ghorāstadā dāyādabāndhavāḥ .. 3 ..
1.21.d:
तेषां बभूव देवेन्द्रो विश्वभुग्लोकपूजितः ॥
आसंस्तस्या सुरा घोरास्तदा दायादबान्धवाः ॥ 3 ॥
1.21.m:
Their lord of gods was Viśvabhuj, worshipped by the world.
At that time, his cousins, the fierce asuras, existed.

1.21.s:
babhūva rājā teṣāṃ ca bāṣkalirnnāma nāmataḥ ..
yena vikramya śakrasya hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ tadā balāt .. 4 ..
1.21.d:
बभूव राजा तेषां च बाष्कलिर्न्नाम नामतः ॥
येन विक्रम्य शक्रस्य हृतं राज्यं तदा बलात् ॥ 4 ॥
1.21.m:
And they had a king named Bāṣkali by name,
by whom, having assailed [him], the kingdom of Śakra was seized then by force.

1.21.s:
hṛtarājyastu devendro brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ..
brahmāpi śakramādāya jagāma śaraṇaṃ harim .. 5 ..
1.21.d:
हृतराज्यस्तु देवेन्द्रो ब्रह्माणं शरणं गतः ॥
ब्रह्मापि शक्रमादाय जगाम शरणं हरिम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.21.m:
Deprived of his kingdom, the lord of gods took refuge with Brahmā;
and Brahmā too, taking Śakra along, went for refuge to Hari.

1.21.s:
nivedayāmāsa tadā devadevāya śārṅgiṇe ..
bāṣkalervijayaṃ sarvaṃ brahmā śubhacaturmukhaḥ .. 6 ..
1.21.d:
निवेदयामास तदा देवदेवाय शार्ङ्गिणे ॥
बाष्कलेर्विजयं सर्वं ब्रह्मा शुभचतुर्मुखः ॥ 6 ॥
1.21.m:
Then the auspicious four-faced Brahmā reported to the god of gods,
the wielder of the bow Śārṅga, all of Bāṣkali's conquest.

1.21.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca ..
brahmanpratyāhariṣyāmi rājyamasya śatakratoḥ..
divi deveṣu dharmātmannivṛtto bhava mā ciram ..7..
1.21.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ॥
ब्रह्मन्प्रत्याहरिष्यामि राज्यमस्य शतक्रतोः॥
दिवि देवेषु धर्मात्मन्निवृत्तो भव मा चिरम् ॥7॥
1.21.m:
The Holy One said:
O Brahmā, I shall restore the kingdom of this performer of a hundred sacrifices.
Return to the gods in heaven without delay, O righteous one.

1.21.s:
ahaṃ vāmanarūpeṇa prayāsye bāṣkaliṃ nṛpam ..
māṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitaṃ tantu gatvā yācatu devarāṭ .. 8 ..
1.21.d:
अहं वामनरूपेण प्रयास्ये बाष्कलिं नृपम् ॥
मां दृष्ट्वा विस्मितं तन्तु गत्वा याचतु देवराट् ॥ 8 ॥
1.21.m:
In the form of a dwarf I shall approach King Bāṣkali;
seeing him astonished upon seeing me, let the king of gods go and ask [for the kingdom].

1.21.s:
lokatrayaṃ mama hṛtaṃ tvayā vikramya bāṣkale ..
tatrāgniśaraṇārthāya dīyatāṃ me kramatrayam .. 9 ..
1.21.d:
लोकत्रयं मम हृतं त्वया विक्रम्य बाष्कले ॥
तत्राग्निशरणार्थाय दीयतां मे क्रमत्रयम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.21.m: "The three worlds were taken from me by you, having conquered them, O Bāṣkali! / Therefore, give me three paces for the sake of an agniśaraṇa [fire-sanctuary],

1.21.s:
atīva hrasvagātrasya vāmanasyāsya mā ciram ..
evamuktastu śakreṇa tadā dātā kramatrayam .. 1.21.10 ..
1.21.d:
अतीव ह्रस्वगात्रस्य वामनस्यास्य मा चिरम् ॥
एवमुक्तस्तु शक्रेण तदा दाता क्रमत्रयम् ॥ 1.21.10 ॥
1.21.m: of this dwarf whose limbs are very short, without delay!" / Addressed thus by Śakra, he then became one who gives the three paces.

1.21.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
ityevamukto devena brahmā svabhavanaṃ gataḥ ..
devo'pi vāmano bhūtvā prayāto yatra bāṣkaliḥ .. 11 ..
1.21.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
इत्येवमुक्तो देवेन ब्रह्मा स्वभवनं गतः ॥
देवोऽपि वामनो भूत्वा प्रयातो यत्र बाष्कलिः ॥ 11 ॥
1.21.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having been spoken to thus by the god, Brahmā went to his own abode. / The god also, having become a dwarf, went to where Bāṣkali was.

1.21.s:
bāṣkalirvāmanaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayotphullalocanaḥ ..
nirīkṣya taṃ yathākāmamasurairbahubhirvṛtaḥ .. 12 ..
1.21.d:
बाष्कलिर्वामनं दृष्ट्वा विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनः ॥
निरीक्ष्य तं यथाकाममसुरैर्बहुभिर्वृतः ॥ 12 ॥
1.21.m: Bāṣkali, seeing the dwarf, his eyes wide with astonishment, / looked at him to his heart's content, surrounded by many asuras.

1.21.s:
etasminneva kāle tu śakrastaṃ deśamāyayau ..
pādyārghyācamanīyādyaiḥ śakraṃ saṃpūjya bāṣkaliḥ .. 13 ..
1.21.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु शक्रस्तं देशमाययौ ॥
पाद्यार्घ्याचमनीयाद्यैः शक्रं संपूज्य बाष्कलिः ॥ 13 ॥
1.21.m: At that very time, Śakra came to that place. / Having honoured Śakra with water for the feet, arghya, water for sipping, and other offerings, Bāṣkali,

1.21.s:
kimāgamanakāryaṃ te tamuvāca prahṛṣṭavāk ..
atyāścaryamidaṃ manye tavāgamana kāraṇam .. 14 ..
1.21.d:
किमागमनकार्यं ते तमुवाच प्रहृष्टवाक् ॥
अत्याश्चर्यमिदं मन्ये तवागमन कारणम् ॥ 14 ॥
1.21.m: with a joyful voice, said to him: "What is the purpose of your coming? / I consider this reason for your coming to be a great wonder."

1.21.s:
śakra uvāca ..
lokatrayaṃ me'pahṛtaṃ vikrameṇa tu bāṣkale! ..
tatrāgniśaraṇārthāya dīyatāṃ me kramatrayam .. 15 ..
1.21.d:
शक्र उवाच ॥
लोकत्रयं मेऽपहृतं विक्रमेण तु बाष्कले! ॥
तत्राग्निशरणार्थाय दीयतां मे क्रमत्रयम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.21.m: Śakra said: / "The three worlds were taken away from me by conquest, O Bāṣkali! / Therefore, let three paces be given to me for the sake of an agniśaraṇa,

1.21.s:
atīva hrasvagātrasya vāmanasyāsya pārthiva ..
bhūmibhāge tu pārakye vastuṃ na tvahamutsahe..16..
1.21.d:
अतीव ह्रस्वगात्रस्य वामनस्यास्य पार्थिव ॥
भूमिभागे तु पारक्ये वस्तुं न त्वहमुत्सहे॥16॥
1.21.m: of this dwarf whose limbs are very short, O earthly king! / For I do not wish to dwell upon a portion of land belonging to another."

1.21.s:
bāṣkaliruvāca ..
kramatrayaṃ vāmanake devarāja kṛtaṃ śubham ..
tatrāssvamuditaḥ prāptaḥ sukhī surapate bhava .. 17 ..
1.21.d:
बाष्कलिरुवाच ॥
क्रमत्रयं वामनके देवराज कृतं शुभम् ॥
तत्रास्स्वमुदितः प्राप्तः सुखी सुरपते भव ॥ 17 ॥
1.21.m: Bāṣkali said: / "Three paces of the little dwarf are granted, auspiciously, O king of gods! / Dwell there rejoiced, arrived, and be happy, O lord of the gods!"

1.21.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamukto bāṣkalinā tyaktvā rūpaṃ tu vāmanam ..16..
1.21.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्तो बाष्कलिना त्यक्त्वा रूपं तु वामनम् ॥16॥
1.21.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Spoken to thus by Bāṣkali, having cast off the form of the dwarf,

1.21.s:
harirvicakrame lokāndevānāṃ hitakāmyayā ..
brahmalokaṃ tato gatvā..... ..
devasya vāmaścaraṇo niviṣṭo dānavālaye .. 19 ..
1.21.d:
हरिर्विचक्रमे लोकान्देवानां हितकाम्यया ॥
ब्रह्मलोकं ततो गत्वा॥॥॥।
देवस्य वामश्चरणो निविष्टो दानवालये ॥ 19 ॥
1.21.m: Hari strode across the worlds out of desire for the welfare of the gods. / Then, having reached the world of Brahmā […] / the left foot of the god was placed in the abode of the dānavas.

1.21.s:
tataḥ kramaṃ sa prathamaṃ dadau sūryye jagatpatiḥ ..
dvitīyaṃ ca dhruve devastṛtīyena ca yādava . .. 1.21.20 ..
1.21.d:
ततः क्रमं स प्रथमं ददौ सूर्य्ये जगत्पतिः ॥
द्वितीयं च ध्रुवे देवस्तृतीयेन च यादव ॥। 1.21.20 ॥
1.21.m: Then the lord of the universe set his first step on the sun, / and the god [set] the second on the pole star; and with the third, O descendant of Yadu,

1.21.s:
brahmāṇḍaṃ tāḍayāmāsa hyasaṃpūrṇena keśavaḥ ..
brahmāṇḍastāḍitastena chidratāmagamatprabho ..21..
1.21.d:
ब्रह्माण्डं ताडयामास ह्यसंपूर्णेन केशवः ॥
ब्रह्माण्डस्ताडितस्तेन छिद्रतामगमत्प्रभो ॥21॥
1.21.m: Keśava struck the cosmic egg, before it was completely filled. / Struck by him, the cosmic egg incurred a perforation, O lord.

1.21.s:
brahmāṇḍabāhyatoyena śataghnenāmbhasāvṛtam ..
tenacchidreṇa tattoyaṃ viveśāṇḍaṃ mahīpate .. 22 ..
1.21.d:
ब्रह्माण्डबाह्यतोयेन शतघ्नेनाम्भसावृतम् ॥
तेनच्छिद्रेण तत्तोयं विवेशाण्डं महीपते ॥ 22 ॥
1.21.m: By the water outside the cosmic egg, surrounded by waters capable of destroying hundreds, / through that perforation, that water entered the cosmic egg, O ruler of the earth.

1.21.s:
aṃguṣṭhāgrakṣatādaṇḍādyatpraviṣṭaṃ jalaṃ śuci ..
prāptā devanadītvaṃ tu sā tu viṣṇupadī nadī .. 23 ..
1.21.d:
अंगुष्ठाग्रक्षतादण्डाद्यत्प्रविष्टं जलं शुचि ॥
प्राप्ता देवनदीत्वं तु सा तु विष्णुपदी नदी ॥ 23 ॥
1.21.m: The pure water that entered the cosmic egg from the wound made by the tip of the big toe, / that river Viṣṇupadī indeed attained the status of the river of the gods.

1.21.s:
devanadyā tayā vyāptaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ sakalaṃ nṛpa! ..
vibhūtibhirmahābhāga sarvānugrahakāmyayā .. 24 ..
1.21.d:
देवनद्या तया व्याप्तं ब्रह्माण्डं सकलं नृप! ॥
विभूतिभिर्महाभाग सर्वानुग्रहकाम्यया ॥ 24 ॥
1.21.m: By that river of the gods, the entire cosmic egg was pervaded, O king, / through its manifestations, O fortunate one, out of a desire to show grace to all.

1.21.s:
vāmanena samākrāntāḥ sarve lokā yadānagha! ..
asuraiste tadā tyaktā devānāṃ satyabāndhavaiḥ .. 25 ..
1.21.d:
वामनेन समाक्रान्ताः सर्वे लोका यदानघ! ॥
असुरैस्ते तदा त्यक्ता देवानां सत्यबान्धवैः ॥ 25 ॥
1.21.m: When all the worlds were traversed by the dwarf, O sinless one, / they were abandoned then by the asuras, who were true kin to the gods.

1.21.s:
pātālaśca yadā tena nākrāntaṃ harimedhasā ..
asuraistaistadā ghorairuṣyate yadunandana! .. 26 ..
1.21.d:
पातालश्च यदा तेन नाक्रान्तं हरिमेधसा ॥
असुरैस्तैस्तदा घोरैरुष्यते यदुनन्दन! ॥ 26 ॥
1.21.m: And when the netherworld was not traversed by that Harimedhas, / it was then inhabited by those terrible asuras, O joy of the Yadus!

1.21.s:
devo'pi hṛtvā trailokyaṃ jagāmādarśanaṃ tadā ..
pātālanilayaścāpi sukhamāste sa bāṣkaliḥ .. 27 ..
1.21.d:
देवोऽपि हृत्वा त्रैलोक्यं जगामादर्शनं तदा ॥
पातालनिलयश्चापि सुखमास्ते स बाष्कलिः ॥ 27 ॥
1.21.m: The god, too, having seized the three worlds, vanished from sight then. / And that Bāṣkali dwells happily, residing in the netherworld.

1.21.s:
śakro'pi pālayāmāsa vipaścidbhuvanaṃ tadā ..
imaṃ trivikramaṃ nāma prādurbhāvaṃ jagadguroḥ .. 28 ..
1.21.d:
शक्रोऽपि पालयामास विपश्चिद्भुवनं तदा ॥
इमं त्रिविक्रमं नाम प्रादुर्भावं जगद्गुरोः ॥ 28 ॥
1.21.m: Śakra also, wise, then ruled over the world. / This manifestation of the teacher of the universe, named Trivikrama,

1.21.s: gaṅgāsaṃbhavasaṃyuktaṃ sarvakilviṣanāśanam .. 29 ..
1.21.d: गङ्गासंभवसंयुक्तं सर्वकिल्विषनाशनम् ॥ 29 ॥
1.21.m: joined with the origin of the Gaṅgā, destroys all sins.

1.21.s:
tenaiva devadevena prāpte vaivasvate'ntare ..
bhūyo lokāstrayaḥ krāntāḥ padā saṃyamino nṛpa .. 1.21.30 ..
1.21.d:
तेनैव देवदेवेन प्राप्ते वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे ॥
भूयो लोकास्त्रयः क्रान्ताः पदा संयमिनो नृप ॥ 1.21.30 ॥
1.21.m: By that very god of gods, when the Vaivasvata interval arrived, / the three worlds were again traversed with his foot, O king of self-restraint.

1.21.s:
anena kāraṇenoktā gaṃgā viṣṇupadī nṛpa ..
yayā sarvamidaṃ vyāptaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram ..31..
1.21.d:
अनेन कारणेनोक्ता गंगा विष्णुपदी नृप ॥
यया सर्वमिदं व्याप्तं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥31॥
1.21.m: For this reason, the Gaṅgā is called Viṣṇupadī, O king, / by which all this threefold world, with the moving and the unmoving, was pervaded.

1.21.s:
gaṃgāsamutpattiriyaṃ mayoktā śrutvaiva yāṃ muñcati sarvapāpam ..
pāpairviśiṣṭo'pi naro nṛvīra sādhuvratastu tridivaṃ prayāti .. 32 ..
1.21.d:
गंगासमुत्पत्तिरियं मयोक्ता श्रुत्वैव यां मुञ्चति सर्वपापम् ॥
पापैर्विशिष्टोऽपि नरो नृवीर साधुव्रतस्तु त्रिदिवं प्रयाति ॥ 32 ॥
1.21.m: This origin of the Gaṅgā has been spoken by me; upon merely hearing it, a man casts off all sin. / Even a man distinguished by sins, O hero among men, if observing virtuous vows, goes to heaven.

1.22.s:
vajra uvāca ..
brahmanviṣṇupadī gaṃgā trailokyaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhati ..
yathā tathā bhṛguśreṣṭha sarvameva prakīrtaya .. 1 ..
1.22.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
ब्रह्मन्विष्णुपदी गंगा त्रैलोक्यं व्याप्य तिष्ठति ॥
यथा तथा भृगुश्रेष्ठ सर्वमेव प्रकीर्तय ॥ 1 ॥
1.22.m: Vajra said: / O brahmin, the Gaṅgā, Viṣṇupadī, stands pervading the three worlds; / proclaim entirely, O best of the Bhṛgus, how that is so.

1.22.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
praviśya devī brahmāṇḍaṃ viṣṇulokamupāgatā ..
brāhmīṃ sabhāṃ plāvayitvā tapolokamupāgatā .. 2 ..
1.22.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
प्रविश्य देवी ब्रह्माण्डं विष्णुलोकमुपागता ॥
ब्राह्मीं सभां प्लावयित्वा तपोलोकमुपागता ॥ 2 ॥
1.22.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having entered the cosmic egg, the goddess reached the world of Viṣṇu. / Having inundated the hall of Brahmā, she reached Tapoloka.

1.22.s:
janalokaṃ gatā tasmānmaharllokaṃ tato gatā ..
svargalokaṃ samāsādya praviṣṭā candramaṇḍalam .. 3 ..
1.22.d:
जनलोकं गता तस्मान्महर्ल्लोकं ततो गता ॥
स्वर्गलोकं समासाद्य प्रविष्टा चन्द्रमण्डलम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.22.m: From there she went to Janaloka; then she went to Maharloka. / Having reached the heavenly world, she entered the orb of the moon.

1.22.s:
candramaṇḍalavibhraṣṭā bhuvarlokamupāgatā ..
ākāśagaṃgā kathitā tatra sā rativardhinī ..4 ..
1.22.d:
चन्द्रमण्डलविभ्रष्टा भुवर्लोकमुपागता ॥
आकाशगंगा कथिता तत्र सा रतिवर्धिनी ॥4 ॥
1.22.m: Fallen from the orb of the moon, she arrived at Bhuvarloka. / She is proclaimed there as the Ākāśagaṅgā, increasing delight.

1.22.s:
tasyāstu dṛśyate panthāḥ satataṃ vyomni nirmale ..
ākāśagaṃgāmadhye sā merau nipatitā girau .. 5 ..
1.22.d:
तस्यास्तु दृश्यते पन्थाः सततं व्योम्नि निर्मले ॥
आकाशगंगामध्ये सा मेरौ निपतिता गिरौ ॥ 5 ॥
1.22.m: Her course is seen perpetually in the spotless sky. / Flowing in the midst of the Ākāśagaṅgā, she fell upon Mount Meru.

1.22.s:
merumadhyādadṛśyantī dṛśyantī ca tathā kvacit ..
prayātā sarvavarṣāṇi dvīpāni ca mahāmate....
sā tu devī jayā nāma kuruvarṣe hradāstu te ..
tebhyaḥ śāntā ca sādhvī ca dvidhā gaṃgā vinissṛtā .. 7 ..
1.22.d:
मेरुमध्याददृश्यन्ती दृश्यन्ती च तथा क्वचित् ॥
प्रयाता सर्ववर्षाणि द्वीपानि च महामते॥॥
सा तु देवी जया नाम कुरुवर्षे ह्रदास्तु ते ॥
तेभ्यः शान्ता च साध्वी च द्विधा गंगा विनिस्सृता ॥ 7 ॥
1.22.m: Invisible from the middle of Meru, and likewise visible somewhere, / she went to all the continents and islands, O highly intelligent one. […] / That goddess is named Jayā; and there are lakes in the Kuru realm; / from them the Gaṅgā issued forth in two forms, peaceful and virtuous.

1.22.s:
jyotsnā ca mṛgamandā ca smṛtā hairaṇvatī śubhā ..
puṇḍarīkā payodā ca ramye varṣe nigadyate .. 8 .
1.22.d:
ज्योत्स्ना च मृगमन्दा च स्मृता हैरण्वती शुभा ॥
पुण्डरीका पयोदा च रम्ये वर्षे निगद्यते ॥ 8 ।
1.22.m: Jyotsnā and Mṛgamandā, the auspicious Hairaṇvatī, are recorded; / Puṇḍarīkā and Payodā are spoken of in the charming realm.

1.22.s:
bhadrā ca kathitā devī gāndharvī ca mano'nugā ..
ilāvṛte tathā saiva proktā jāmbavatī śubhā .. 9 ..
1.22.d:
भद्रा च कथिता देवी गान्धर्वी च मनोऽनुगा ॥
इलावृते तथा सैव प्रोक्ता जाम्बवती शुभा ॥ 9 ॥
1.22.m: And the goddess is called Bhadrā, and Gāndharvī who follows the mind; / in Ilāvṛta, that very one is spoken of as the auspicious Jāmbavatī.

1.22.s:
tasyāstīrabhavaṃ mūrdhni kanakaṃ dhāryate suraiḥ..
ketumāle ca kathitā nirmalā naḍvalā tathā .. 1.22.10 ..
1.22.d:
तस्यास्तीरभवं मूर्ध्नि कनकं धार्यते सुरैः॥
केतुमाले च कथिता निर्मला नड्वला तथा ॥ 1.22.10 ॥
1.22.m: Gold born upon her banks is worn upon their heads by the gods. / And in Ketumāla she is spoken of as the stainless Naḍvalā.

1.22.s:
manasvinī jyotiṣmatī harivarṣe nigadyate..
tathā kimpuruṣākhye tu rambhā candravatī śubhā ..11...
1.22.d:
मनस्विनी ज्योतिष्मती हरिवर्षे निगद्यते॥
तथा किम्पुरुषाख्ये तु रम्भा चन्द्रवती शुभा ॥11॥।
1.22.m: She is proclaimed as Manasvinī and Jyotiṣmatī in Harivarṣa; / and in the realm named Kimpuruṣa, as the auspicious Rambhā and Candravatī.

1.22.s:
indradyumnapayodā sā kāśaikā matipāvanī ..
manojavā tāmraparṇī gabhastimatimālinī .. 12 ..
1.22.d:
इन्द्रद्युम्नपयोदा सा काशैका मतिपावनी ॥
मनोजवा ताम्रपर्णी गभस्तिमतिमालिनी ॥ 12 ॥
1.22.m: She is Indradyumnapayodā, Kāśaikā that purifies the intellect, / Manojavā, Tāmraparṇī, and Gabhastimatimālinī.

1.22.s:
nāgadvīpe nāgavatī saumye somaprabhā tathā ..
rudralokaṃ tataḥ prāptā brahmalokaṃ tato gatā .. 13 ..
1.22.d:
नागद्वीपे नागवती सौम्ये सोमप्रभा तथा ॥
रुद्रलोकं ततः प्राप्ता ब्रह्मलोकं ततो गता ॥ 13 ॥
1.22.m: She is Nāgavatī in Nāgadvīpa, and likewise Somaprabhā in Saumya. / Then she reached Rudraloka; then she went to the world of Brahmā.

1.22.s:
gāndharvī caiva gandharvī vāruṇe varuṇahradā ..
hrādinī hlādinī caiva puṇyatoyā ca varṣiṇī .. 14 ..
1.22.d:
गान्धर्वी चैव गन्धर्वी वारुणे वरुणह्रदा ॥
ह्रादिनी ह्लादिनी चैव पुण्यतोया च वर्षिणी ॥ 14 ॥
1.22.m: She is Gāndharvī and Gandharvī; in Vāruṇa she is Varuṇahradā, / Hrādinī, Hlādinī, Puṇyatoyā, and Varṣiṇī.

1.22.s:
sītā cakṣuśca sindhuśca gaṃgā cāsminprakīrtitā ..
amarānniṣadhānsarvāndhīvarānṛṣikāṃstathā .. 15 ..
1.22.d:
सीता चक्षुश्च सिन्धुश्च गंगा चास्मिन्प्रकीर्तिता ॥
अमरान्निषधान्सर्वान्धीवरानृषिकांस्तथा ॥ 15 ॥
1.22.m: In this [realm] she is proclaimed as Sītā, Cakṣu, Sindhu, and Gaṅgā. / She visits all the Amaras, Niṣadhas, Dhīvaras, and Ṛṣikas,

1.22.s:
oṣṭhaprāvaraṇānsaumyānkarṇaprāvaraṇāṃstathā ....
kālodarānvikarṇāṃśca hrādinī tu niṣevate .. 16 ..
1.22.d:
ओष्ठप्रावरणान्सौम्यान्कर्णप्रावरणांस्तथा ॥॥
कालोदरान्विकर्णांश्च ह्रादिनी तु निषेवते ॥ 16 ॥
1.22.m: those whose lips are coverings, the Saumyas, and those whose ears are coverings, / the Kālodaras, and the Vikarṇas; Hrādinī indeed visits them.

1.22.s:
indradyumnasaraḥ puṇyamupacārādajāyata ..
tathā kharapadāndeśānvetraśaṅkupadānapi .. 17 ..
1.22.d:
इन्द्रद्युम्नसरः पुण्यमुपचारादजायत ॥
तथा खरपदान्देशान्वेत्रशङ्कुपदानपि ॥ 17 ॥
1.22.m: The holy lake of Indradyumna was produced by her attendance. / Likewise the regions of the Kharapadas and also the Vetraśaṅkupadas,

1.22.s:
tañjānakāmataṃ caiva hlādinī tu niṣevate ..
daradāñjahuḍāṃścaiva kāśmīrānnairasānkurūn .. 18 ..
gāndhārāndaradābhīrānkuparvānbhīmarauravān .. 53.
1.22.d:
तञ्जानकामतं चैव ह्लादिनी तु निषेवते ॥
दरदाञ्जहुडांश्चैव काश्मीरान्नैरसान्कुरून् ॥ 18 ॥
गान्धारान्दरदाभीरान्कुपर्वान्भीमरौरवान् ॥ 53.
1.22.m:
Tañjāna and Kāmata—Hlādinī indeed visits them. / The Daradas, Jahuḍas, Kāśmīras, Nairasas, Kurus,
Gāndhāras, Daradābhīras, Kuparvas, Bhīmarauravas,

1.22.s: śivaparvānindraparvānsindhutīrānniṣevate .. 19 ..
1.22.d: शिवपर्वानिन्द्रपर्वान्सिन्धुतीरान्निषेवते ॥ 19 ॥
1.22.m: Śivaparvas, Indraparvas, and the banks of the Sindhu she visits.

1.22.s:
devāndaityānkālakeyāngandharvānkinnarāṃstathā ..
vidyādharāṃstathā nāgānsuparvānsumanoharān .. 1.22.20 ..
1.22.d:
देवान्दैत्यान्कालकेयान्गन्धर्वान्किन्नरांस्तथा ॥
विद्याधरांस्तथा नागान्सुपर्वान्सुमनोहरान् ॥ 1.22.20 ॥
1.22.m: The gods, daityas, Kālakeyas, gandharvas, kinnaras, / vidyādharas, and nāgas, possessing good joints and highly captivating,

1.22.s:
kalāpagrāmakāṃścaiva naranārāyaṇāśramam ..
kirātāṃśca pulindāṃśca mayasya nagarīṃ tathā .. 21 ..
1.22.d:
कलापग्रामकांश्चैव नरनारायणाश्रमम् ॥
किरातांश्च पुलिन्दांश्च मयस्य नगरीं तथा ॥ 21 ॥
1.22.m: the inhabitants of Kalāpagrāma, the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, / the Kirātas, Pulindas, and the city of Maya,

1.22.s:
kutūnsabhāratāṃścaiva pulindām̐ścaiva bhāgaśaḥ ..
pāñcālānkāśayānvatsānmāgadhāṃstāmraliptakān .. 22 ..
1.22.d:
कुतून्सभारतांश्चैव पुलिन्दाम्̐श्चैव भागशः ॥
पाञ्चालान्काशयान्वत्सान्मागधांस्ताम्रलिप्तकान् ॥ 22 ॥
1.22.m: the Kutus along with the Bhāratas, and the Pulindas region by region, / the Pāñcālas, Kāśis, Vatsas, Māgadhas, and Tāmraliptakas,

1.22.s:
sahyottarāṃśca vaṅgāṃśca tathā śrāvastivāsina ..
aṅgānvaṃgānsapuṇḍrāṃśca gaṃgā bhāvayate śubhā .. 23 ..
1.22.d:
सह्योत्तरांश्च वङ्गांश्च तथा श्रावस्तिवासिन ॥
अङ्गान्वंगान्सपुण्ड्रांश्च गंगा भावयते शुभा ॥ 23 ॥
1.22.m: those north of the Sahya, the Vaṅgas, and the dwellers of Śrāvastī, / the Aṅgas, Vaṅgas, and Puṇḍras—the auspicious Gaṅgā causes to flourish.

1.22.s:
hrādinī hlādinī caiva pāvanī jāhnavī tathā ..
praviṣṭā sāgaraṃ pūrvaṃ dvīpesminnṛpasattama .. 24 ..
1.22.d:
ह्रादिनी ह्लादिनी चैव पावनी जाह्नवी तथा ॥
प्रविष्टा सागरं पूर्वं द्वीपेस्मिन्नृपसत्तम ॥ 24 ॥
1.22.m: The Hrādinī, Hlādinī, Pāvanī, and Jāhnavī / entered the eastern ocean in this continent, O best of kings.

1.22.s:
sītācakṣuśca sindhuśca paścimaṃ nṛpa sāgaram ..
gaṅgāvyāptistava proktā jambūdvīpe mayānagha .. 25 ..
1.22.d:
सीताचक्षुश्च सिन्धुश्च पश्चिमं नृप सागरम् ॥
गङ्गाव्याप्तिस्तव प्रोक्ता जम्बूद्वीपे मयानघ ॥ 25 ॥
1.22.m: The Sītā, Cakṣu, and Sindhu entered the western ocean, O king. / The pervasive course of Gaṅgā in Jambūdvīpa has thus been spoken to you by me, O sinless one.

1.22.s:
lokeṣu ca tathā rājandvīpeṣvanyeṣu me śṛṇu ..
sukumārī kumārī ca sukṛtā sevinī tathā .. 26 ..
1.22.d:
लोकेषु च तथा राजन्द्वीपेष्वन्येषु मे शृणु ॥
सुकुमारी कुमारी च सुकृता सेविनी तथा ॥ 26 ॥
1.22.m: And in the other worlds and continents, O king, hear from me: / the Sukumārī, Kumārī, Sukṛtā, Sevinī,

1.22.s:
ikṣuśca veṇukā nandā śākadvīpe ca saptadhā ..
śālmale tvatha gomede dvīpe puṣkarasaṃjñake .. 27 ..
1.22.d:
इक्षुश्च वेणुका नन्दा शाकद्वीपे च सप्तधा ॥
शाल्मले त्वथ गोमेदे द्वीपे पुष्करसंज्ञके ॥ 27 ॥
1.22.m: the Ikṣu, Veṇukā, and Nandā exist sevenfold in Śākadvīpa. / In Śālmala, Gomeda, and the continent named Puṣkara,

1.22.s:
nadītvaṃ sā samutsṛjya codadhitvamupāgatā ..
tasmindvīpatraye nadyo na santi yadunandana ..28..
1.22.d:
नदीत्वं सा समुत्सृज्य चोदधित्वमुपागता ॥
तस्मिन्द्वीपत्रये नद्यो न सन्ति यदुनन्दन ॥28॥
1.22.m: she abandoned her state as a river and attained the state of the ocean. / In those three continents, O scion of Yadu, there are no rivers.

1.22.s:
udakānyudbhidānyeva teṣu santi sahasraśaḥ ..
evaṃ bhūmitalaṃ plāvya pātālaṃ kṛṣṇamṛttikam .. 29 ..
1.22.d:
उदकान्युद्भिदान्येव तेषु सन्ति सहस्रशः ॥
एवं भूमितलं प्लाव्य पातालं कृष्णमृत्तिकम् ॥ 29 ॥
1.22.m: Waters spring up there in thousands. / Having thus flooded the earth's surface, [she reached] the netherworld of black earth.

1.22.s:
ekībhūtā praviṣṭā sā bhogavatyāṃ samīpataḥ ..
śvetabhaumaṃ gatā tasmādraktabhaumaṃ tato gatā .. 1.22.30 ..
1.22.d:
एकीभूता प्रविष्टा सा भोगवत्यां समीपतः ॥
श्वेतभौमं गता तस्माद्रक्तभौमं ततो गता ॥ 1.22.30 ॥
1.22.m: Having become one, she entered near Bhogavatī. / Thence she went to the white-earthed [realm], and from there to the red-earthed [realm].

1.22.s:
śilābhaumaṃ gatā tasmādrukmabhaumaṃ tato gatā ..
rukmabhaumādapi gatā raudraṃ tejassudāruṇam .. 31 ..
1.22.d:
शिलाभौमं गता तस्माद्रुक्मभौमं ततो गता ॥
रुक्मभौमादपि गता रौद्रं तेजस्सुदारुणम् ॥ 31 ॥
1.22.m: From there she went to the stony-earthed [realm], and thence to the gold-earthed [realm]. / From the gold-earthed [realm] she went further to the fierce and terrible radiance.

1.22.s:
tato'pi vilayaṃ gatvā vārāhaṃ lokamāgatā ..
vārāhalokādbrahmāṇḍaṃ tadarthaṃ bhinna vāhinī .. 32 ..
1.22.d:
ततोऽपि विलयं गत्वा वाराहं लोकमागता ॥
वाराहलोकाद्ब्रह्माण्डं तदर्थं भिन्न वाहिनी ॥ 32 ॥
1.22.m: Dissolving even from there, she went to the world of the Boar. / Flowing onward from the world of the Boar, she cleaved the cosmic egg for that purpose.

1.22.s: chidreṇa tena sā devī svāṃ yoniṃ punarāgatā .. 33 ..
1.22.d: छिद्रेण तेन सा देवी स्वां योनिं पुनरागता ॥ 33 ॥
1.22.m: Through that opening, that goddess returned again to her own source.

1.22.s:
evaṃ narendreśa jagatsamagramākramya gaṃgā satataṃ sthitā yā ..
tasyāḥ prabhāvaśravaṇādaśeṣaṃ pāpaṃ narāṇāṃ samupaiti śāṃtim .. 34 .. ..
1.22.d:
एवं नरेन्द्रेश जगत्समग्रमाक्रम्य गंगा सततं स्थिता या ॥
तस्याः प्रभावश्रवणादशेषं पापं नराणां समुपैति शांतिम् ॥ 34 ॥ ॥
1.22.m: Thus, O lord of kings, having pervaded the entire world, Gaṅgā remains constantly present; / from hearing of her power, all sins of mortals go to appeasement.

1.23.s:
vajra uvāca ..
bhagīrathasya rājarṣervaṃśamuttamapūruṣaṃ ..
tvatto'haṃ śrotumicchāmi gaṅgā yenāvatāritā .. 1 ..
1.23.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
भगीरथस्य राजर्षेर्वंशमुत्तमपूरुषं ॥
त्वत्तोऽहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि गङ्गा येनावतारिता ॥ 1 ॥
1.23.m: Vajra said: / I desire to hear from you the lineage of the royal sage Bhagīratha, / the excellent person by whom Gaṅgā was brought down.

1.23.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
bhagīrathasutaḥ śrīmānviśruto nāma dhārmikaḥ ..
viśrutasyātmajaḥ śrīmānnābhāga iti viśrutaḥ .. 2 ..
1.23.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
भगीरथसुतः श्रीमान्विश्रुतो नाम धार्मिकः ॥
विश्रुतस्यात्मजः श्रीमान्नाभाग इति विश्रुतः ॥ 2 ॥
1.23.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Bhagīratha's glorious and righteous son was named Viśruta. / Viśruta's glorious son was famed as Nābhāga.

1.23.s:
ambarīṣastu nābhāgirayutāristadātmajaḥ ..
tatsuto ṛtuparṇaśca rājā nalasakho balī .. 3 ..
1.23.d:
अम्बरीषस्तु नाभागिरयुतारिस्तदात्मजः ॥
तत्सुतो ऋतुपर्णश्च राजा नलसखो बली ॥ 3 ॥
1.23.m: Ambarīṣa was the son of Nābhāga, and Ayutāris was his son. / His son was the mighty king Ṛtuparṇa, friend of Nala.

1.23.s:
śarvakāmaḥ sutastasya sudāsastasya cātmajaḥ ..
tasya mitrasahaḥ putraḥ tasya putrośmako nṛpa .. 4 ..
1.23.d:
शर्वकामः सुतस्तस्य सुदासस्तस्य चात्मजः ॥
तस्य मित्रसहः पुत्रः तस्य पुत्रोश्मको नृप ॥ 4 ॥
1.23.m: Śarvakāma was his son, and Sudāsa was his son. / His son was Mitrasaha, and his son was Aśmaka, O king.

1.23.s:
mūlakastatsuto rājā mahābuddhirnareśvaraḥ ..
kṣatriyāṇāṃ vadhe ghore rāmeṇa vinipātitaḥ .. 5 ..
1.23.d:
मूलकस्तत्सुतो राजा महाबुद्धिर्नरेश्वरः ॥
क्षत्रियाणां वधे घोरे रामेण विनिपातितः ॥ 5 ॥
1.23.m: Mūlaka was his son, a king and lord of men of great intellect. / During the terrible slaughter of the kṣatriyas, he was struck down by Rāma.

1.23.s:
purā pitṛvadhāmarṣādrāmo bhārgavanandanaḥ ..
triḥsaptakṛtvaḥ pṛthivīṃ cakre niḥkṣatriyāmimām ..6..
1.23.d:
पुरा पितृवधामर्षाद्रामो भार्गवनन्दनः ॥
त्रिःसप्तकृत्वः पृथिवीं चक्रे निःक्षत्रियामिमाम् ॥6॥
1.23.m: Formerly, out of fury over the murder of his father, Rāma, descendant of Bhṛgu, / rid this earth of kṣatriyas thrice seven times.

1.23.s:
bhagīrathakulotpannaṃ mūlakaṃ nāma jaghnivān ..
vajra uvāca ..
kathaṃ rāmeṇa vasudhā purā niḥkṣattriyā kṛtā ..
kimarthaṃ ca mahābhāga tanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ .. 7..
1.23.d:
भगीरथकुलोत्पन्नं मूलकं नाम जघ्निवान् ॥
वज्र उवाच ॥
कथं रामेण वसुधा पुरा निःक्षत्त्रिया कृता ॥
किमर्थं च महाभाग तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥ 7॥
1.23.m: He slew the king named Mūlaka born in the lineage of Bhagīratha. / Vajra said: / How was the earth made devoid of kṣatriyas by Rāma in ancient times, / and for what reason, O fortunate one? Explain that to me as I ask.

1.23.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
somavaṃśasamutpanno yayātirnāma pārthivaḥ ..
tasyāpi saṃhataḥ putro babhūva pṛthivīpatiḥ .. 6 ..
1.23.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
सोमवंशसमुत्पन्नो ययातिर्नाम पार्थिवः ॥
तस्यापि संहतः पुत्रो बभूव पृथिवीपतिः ॥ 6 ॥
1.23.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / There was a king named Yayāti born in the Lunar dynasty. / His son was Saṃhata, who also became ruler of the earth.

1.23.s:
sahasrajitsutastasya nabhajittasya cātmajaḥ ..
tasyāpi haihayaḥ putraḥ kuntistasyāpi cātmajaḥ .. 9 ..
1.23.d:
सहस्रजित्सुतस्तस्य नभजित्तस्य चात्मजः ॥
तस्यापि हैहयः पुत्रः कुन्तिस्तस्यापि चात्मजः ॥ 9 ॥
1.23.m: Sahasrajit was his son, and Nabhajit was his son. / Haihaya was his son, and Kunti was his son.

1.23.s:
tasyāpi saṃhataḥ putro mahiṣmāṃ'stasya cātmajaḥ ..
māhiṣmatī kṛtā yena nagarī sumanoharā .. 1.23.10 ..
1.23.d:
तस्यापि संहतः पुत्रो महिष्मांऽस्तस्य चात्मजः ॥
माहिष्मती कृता येन नगरी सुमनोहरा ॥ 1.23.10 ॥
1.23.m: His son was Saṃhata, and Mahiṣmat was his son, / by whom the highly delightful city of Māhiṣmatī was built.

1.23.s:
bhadraśreṇyaḥ sutastasya durmadastasya cātmajaḥ ..
kanakastatsuto rājā kṛtavīryastadātmajaḥ ..1 1..
1.23.d:
भद्रश्रेण्यः सुतस्तस्य दुर्मदस्तस्य चात्मजः ॥
कनकस्तत्सुतो राजा कृतवीर्यस्तदात्मजः ॥1 1॥
1.23.m: Bhadraśreṇya was his son, and Durmada was his son. / King Kanaka was his son, and Kṛtavīrya was his son.

1.23.s:
arjunastanayastasya saptadvīpeśvaro'bhavat..
dattātreyo'tha bhagavānviṣṇurūpānurūpadhṛk..12..
1.23.d:
अर्जुनस्तनयस्तस्य सप्तद्वीपेश्वरोऽभवत्॥
दत्तात्रेयोऽथ भगवान्विष्णुरूपानुरूपधृक्॥12॥
1.23.m: Arjuna was his son, who became the ruler of seven continents. / Then, having propitiated with asceticism the blessed lord Dattātreya, / who assumed a form suitable to the form of Viṣṇu,

1.23.s:
ārādhya tapasā yena prāptaṃ rājyaṃ sudurlabham ..
tathā bāhusahasraṃ ca matiṃ dharme tathottamām .. 13 ..
1.23.d:
आराध्य तपसा येन प्राप्तं राज्यं सुदुर्लभम् ॥
तथा बाहुसहस्रं च मतिं धर्मे तथोत्तमाम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.23.m: he attained a kingdom most difficult to obtain, / a thousand arms, and an intellect supremely intent on dharma,

1.23.s:
adharme varttamānasya maraṇaṃ ca janārdanāt ..
yuddhena pṛthivīṃ jitvā dharmeṇaivānuraṃjayan .. 14 ..
1.23.d:
अधर्मे वर्त्तमानस्य मरणं च जनार्दनात् ॥
युद्धेन पृथिवीं जित्वा धर्मेणैवानुरंजयन् ॥ 14 ॥
1.23.m: and, should he turn toward adharma, death at the hands of Janārdana. / Having conquered the earth through war, he delighted it solely through dharma.

1.23.s:
teneyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā saptadvīpā sapattanā ..
saptodadhiparikṣiptā kṣātreṇa vidhinā jitā .. 15 ..
1.23.d:
तेनेयं पृथिवी सर्वा सप्तद्वीपा सपत्तना ॥
सप्तोदधिपरिक्षिप्ता क्षात्रेण विधिना जिता ॥ 15 ॥
1.23.m: By him this entire earth of seven continents and cities, / surrounded by seven oceans, was conquered according to the rule of kṣatriyas.

1.23.s:
pātālanagare śaile vasudhāyāṃ rasātale ..
tasya pārthivasiṃhasya cakraṃ na pratihanyate ..16..
1.23.d:
पातालनगरे शैले वसुधायां रसातले ॥
तस्य पार्थिवसिंहस्य चक्रं न प्रतिहन्यते ॥16॥
1.23.m: In the subterranean city, on the mountains, on earth, and in Rasātala, / the discus of that lion among kings was never obstructed.

1.23.s:
dvīpeṣu sa hi sarveṣu khātaṃ khātamathā'karot ..
yūpacihnāni ca tathā khaḍgī śataśanī rathī .. 17 ..
1.23.d:
द्वीपेषु स हि सर्वेषु खातं खातमथाऽकरोत् ॥
यूपचिह्नानि च तथा खड्गी शतशनी रथी ॥ 17 ॥
1.23.m: In every continent he dug excavation after excavation, / and erected sacrificial posts, bearing sword, having a hundred lightning-bolts, mounted on a chariot.

1.23.s:
deśānanucaranyogātsadā paśyati taskarān..
sa eva paśupālobhūtkṣetrapālaḥ sa eva ca .. 18 ..
1.23.d:
देशाननुचरन्योगात्सदा पश्यति तस्करान्॥
स एव पशुपालोभूत्क्षेत्रपालः स एव च ॥ 18 ॥
1.23.m: Ranging over realms through yoga, he constantly watched for thieves. / He himself became the cowherd, and he himself the protector of fields.

1.23.s:
sa eva vṛṣṭyā parjanyo yogitvādarjuno'bhavat ..
sa tu bāhusahasreṇa jyāghātakaṭhinatvacā .. 19 ..
1.23.d:
स एव वृष्ट्या पर्जन्यो योगित्वादर्जुनोऽभवत् ॥
स तु बाहुसहस्रेण ज्याघातकठिनत्वचा ॥ 19 ॥
1.23.m: Due to his yogic power, Arjuna himself became Parjanya with rain. / With his thousand arms whose skin was hardened by bowstring blows,

1.23.s:
bhāti raśmisahasreṇa śāradeneva bhāskaraḥ ..
rākṣasā nirjitāstena tena baddhaśca rāvaṇaḥ .. 1.23.20 ..
1.23.d:
भाति रश्मिसहस्रेण शारदेनेव भास्करः ॥
राक्षसा निर्जितास्तेन तेन बद्धश्च रावणः ॥ 1.23.20 ॥
1.23.m: he shone like an autumn sun with a thousand rays. / The rākṣasas were vanquished by him, and Rāvaṇa was bound by him.

1.23.s:
jitvā bhogavatī tena karkoṭakasutā hṛtā ..
tasya bāhusahasreṇa kṣobhyamāṇe mahodadhau ..
bhavanti līnā niśceṣṭāḥ pātālasthā mahāsurāḥ .. 21 ..
1.23.d:
जित्वा भोगवती तेन कर्कोटकसुता हृता ॥
तस्य बाहुसहस्रेण क्षोभ्यमाणे महोदधौ ॥
भवन्ति लीना निश्चेष्टाः पातालस्था महासुराः ॥ 21 ॥
1.23.m: Having conquered Bhogavatī, he carried off the daughter of Karkoṭaka. / When the great ocean was churned by his thousand arms, / the great asuras residing in the netherworld remained curled up and motionless,

1.23.s:
mandarakṣobhacakitā amṛtotpādaśaṅkitāḥ ..
nataniścalamūrdhāno bhavanti ca mahoragāḥ .. 22 ..
1.23.d:
मन्दरक्षोभचकिता अमृतोत्पादशङ्किताः ॥
नतनिश्चलमूर्धानो भवन्ति च महोरगाः ॥ 22 ॥
1.23.m: startled like the churning of Mandara, fearing the emergence of amṛta; / and the great serpents kept their heads bowed and motionless.

1.23.s:
daśayajñasahasrāṇi teneṣṭāni mahīkṣitā ..
dvīpe dvīpe mahārāja dharmajñena mahātmanā .. 23 ..
1.23.d:
दशयज्ञसहस्राणि तेनेष्टानि महीक्षिता ॥
द्वीपे द्वीपे महाराज धर्मज्ञेन महात्मना ॥ 23 ॥
1.23.m: Ten thousand sacrifices were offered by that ruler of the earth, / the high-souled knower of dharma, in continent after continent, O great king.

1.23.s:
sarve yajñā mahārāja tasyāsanbhūridakṣiṇāḥ ..
sarve kāñcanavedīkāḥ sarve yūpaiśca kāñcanaiḥ ..24 ..
1.23.d:
सर्वे यज्ञा महाराज तस्यासन्भूरिदक्षिणाः ॥
सर्वे काञ्चनवेदीकाः सर्वे यूपैश्च काञ्चनैः ॥24 ॥
1.23.m: All his sacrifices, O great king, were endowed with abundant sacrificial fees; / all had golden altars and all had golden sacrificial posts.

1.23.s:
dvijānāṃ pariveṣṭārastasya yajñeṣu devatāḥ ..
svayamāsanmahārāja svayaṃ bhāgaharāstathā .. 25 ..
1.23.d:
द्विजानां परिवेष्टारस्तस्य यज्ञेषु देवताः ॥
स्वयमासन्महाराज स्वयं भागहरास्तथा ॥ 25 ॥
1.23.m: The gods themselves served the twice-born at his sacrifices, / O great king, and they personally received their portions.

1.23.s:
tasya yajñe jagau gāthā nāradassumahattapāḥ ..
na nūnaṃ kārtavīryasya gatiṃ yāsyanti pārthivāḥ .. 26 ..
1.23.d:
तस्य यज्ञे जगौ गाथा नारदस्सुमहत्तपाः ॥
न नूनं कार्तवीर्यस्य गतिं यास्यन्ति पार्थिवाः ॥ 26 ॥
1.23.m: At his sacrifice, Nārada of great ascetic heat sang this verse: / 'Surely other kings will never attain the path of Kārtavīrya,

1.23.s: yajñairdānaistapobhirvā vikrameṇa śrutena vā .. 27 ..
1.23.d: यज्ञैर्दानैस्तपोभिर्वा विक्रमेण श्रुतेन वा ॥ 27 ॥
1.23.m: neither by sacrifices, nor by gifts, nor by austerities, nor by valour, nor by sacred learning!'

1.23.s:
pañcāśītisahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ sa mahīpatiḥ ..
saptadvīpeśvaraḥ samrāṭ cakravarttī babhūva ha ..28..
1.23.d:
पञ्चाशीतिसहस्राणि वर्षाणां स महीपतिः ॥
सप्तद्वीपेश्वरः सम्राट् चक्रवर्त्ती बभूव ह ॥28॥
1.23.m: For eighty-five thousand years that ruler of the earth / reigned as supreme lord of the seven continents and universal monarch.

1.23.s:
tasya rājñastu vasudhā bahupārthivasaṅkulā ..
bhārākrāntā vilulitā babhūva pṛthivīpate..29..
1.23.d:
तस्य राज्ञस्तु वसुधा बहुपार्थिवसङ्कुला ॥
भाराक्रान्ता विलुलिता बभूव पृथिवीपते॥29॥
1.23.m: Under that king, however, the earth was crowded with many rulers; / overwhelmed by the burden and agitated, O lord of the earth, she became [distressed].

1.23.s:
tasya rājño gatātaṅkairbahuputrairnarottama ..
tejoyuktaiḥ samākīrṇā vasudhā vasudhādhipa .. 1.23.30 ..
1.23.d:
तस्य राज्ञो गतातङ्कैर्बहुपुत्रैर्नरोत्तम ॥
तेजोयुक्तैः समाकीर्णा वसुधा वसुधाधिप ॥ 1.23.30 ॥
1.23.m: O best of men, teeming with that king’s many fearless sons / endowed with splendor, the earth [was troubled], O ruler of the earth.

1.23.s:
bahunāgāśvasaṃkīrṇā bahugokulasaṅkulā ..
na śaktā nṛpate soḍhuṃ tejastadatimānuṣam .. 31 ..
1.23.d:
बहुनागाश्वसंकीर्णा बहुगोकुलसङ्कुला ॥
न शक्ता नृपते सोढुं तेजस्तदतिमानुषम् ॥ 31 ॥
1.23.m: Crowded with many elephants and horses, overflowing with numerous herds of cattle, / she was unable to endure that superhuman splendor, O king.

1.23.s: jvālāvalivapuḥ śrāntā khinnā nākamupāgatā .. 32 ..
1.23.d: ज्वालावलिवपुः श्रान्ता खिन्ना नाकमुपागता ॥ 32 ॥
1.23.m: Her body a mass of flames, weary and distressed, she went to heaven.

1.23.s:
evaṃ prabhāve naradevanāthe pṛthvīṃ samagrāṃ paripālyamāne ..
bhāreṇa sannā pṛthivī jagāma mahendralokaṃ munidevajuṣṭam .. 33 ..
1.23.d:
एवं प्रभावे नरदेवनाथे पृथ्वीं समग्रां परिपाल्यमाने ॥
भारेण सन्ना पृथिवी जगाम महेन्द्रलोकं मुनिदेवजुष्टम् ॥ 33 ॥
1.23.m: While that ruler of men of such power was protecting the entire earth, / sunk under her burden, the earth went to the world of Mahendra, frequented by sages and gods.

1.24.s:
vajra uvāca ..
devakāryaṃ vinā viṣṇurnotpatsyati mahītale ..
kasminkārye babhūvāsau dattātreya iti śrutaḥ .. 1 ..
1.24.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
देवकार्यं विना विष्णुर्नोत्पत्स्यति महीतले ॥
कस्मिन्कार्ये बभूवासौ दत्तात्रेय इति श्रुतः ॥ 1 ॥
1.24.m: Vajra said: / Viṣṇu does not take birth on the earth's surface except for the sake of the gods. / For what task did he become known as Dattātreya?

1.24.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
śakreṇa ca yadā vṛtro hato vīryopabṛṃhitaḥ .. 2 ..
1.24.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
शक्रेण च यदा वृत्रो हतो वीर्योपबृंहितः ॥ 2 ॥
1.24.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When Vṛtra, fortified by vigor, was slain by Śakra,

1.24.s:
tasminhate'sure tvaṣṭā viśvarūpamavāsṛjat ..
tapasyantaṃ ca taṃ gatvā jaghāna ca śacīpatiḥ .. 3 ..
1.24.d:
तस्मिन्हतेऽसुरे त्वष्टा विश्वरूपमवासृजत् ॥
तपस्यन्तं च तं गत्वा जघान च शचीपतिः ॥ 3 ॥
1.24.m: when that asura was slain, Tvaṣṭṛ brought forth Viśvarūpa; / and going thither while he was practicing asceticism, the husband of Śacī killed him.

1.24.s:
tasminhate brahmahatyā jagāma balasūdanam ..
brahmahatyābhibhūtastu rājyaṃ tyaktvā triviṣṭape .. 4 ..
1.24.d:
तस्मिन्हते ब्रह्महत्या जगाम बलसूदनम् ॥
ब्रह्महत्याभिभूतस्तु राज्यं त्यक्त्वा त्रिविष्टपे ॥ 4 ॥
1.24.m: When he was killed, [the sin of] killing a brahmin came upon the slayer of Bala; / overwhelmed by [the sin of] killing a brahmin, he abandoned his sovereignty in heaven.

1.24.s:
mānase bisatantustho babhūva sa purandaraḥ ..
rājā kṛtaḥ śakrahīnairdevaistu nahuṣastadā .. 5 ..
1.24.d:
मानसे बिसतन्तुस्थो बभूव स पुरन्दरः ॥
राजा कृतः शक्रहीनैर्देवैस्तु नहुषस्तदा ॥ 5 ॥
1.24.m: That Purandara took up residence in a lotus fibre in Lake Mānasa. / Then Nahuṣa was made king by the gods who were deprived of Śakra.

1.24.s:
so'kāmayata paulomīṃ śakrasya mahiṣīṃ priyām ..
kālālābhaparā prāha śakraṃ devī tathā śacī .. 6 ..
1.24.d:
सोऽकामयत पौलोमीं शक्रस्य महिषीं प्रियाम् ॥
कालालाभपरा प्राह शक्रं देवी तथा शची ॥ 6 ॥
1.24.m: He desired Paulomī, Śakra's beloved queen consort. / Intent on gaining time, Queen Śacī said to Śakra:

1.24.s:
apūrveṇa hi yānena samīpaṃ me sureśvara ..
ṛṣibhiḥ śibikāṃ yuktvā sa jagāma tadantikam .. 7..
1.24.d:
अपूर्वेण हि यानेन समीपं मे सुरेश्वर ॥
ऋषिभिः शिबिकां युक्त्वा स जगाम तदन्तिकम् ॥ 7॥
1.24.m: "O lord of the gods, [come] to my presence by an unprecedented conveyance." / Yoking the ṛṣis to a palanquin, he approached her.

1.24.s:
śibikāṃ vahamānaṃ tu mandaṃmandaṃ dvijottamam ..
pādena tāḍayāmāsa so'gastyaṃ pāpaniścayaḥ .. 8 ..
1.24.d:
शिबिकां वहमानं तु मन्दंमन्दं द्विजोत्तमम् ॥
पादेन ताडयामास सोऽगस्त्यं पापनिश्चयः ॥ 8 ॥
1.24.m: As he was carrying the palanquin slowly, very slowly, that man of evil resolve / struck the best of the twice-born, Agastya, with his foot.

1.24.s:
agastyena tathā śapto bhava sarpo mahīpate ..
yudhiṣṭhireṇa saṃgamya śāpamokṣamavāpsyasi .. 9 ..
1.24.d:
अगस्त्येन तथा शप्तो भव सर्पो महीपते ॥
युधिष्ठिरेण संगम्य शापमोक्षमवाप्स्यसि ॥ 9 ॥
1.24.m: He was thus cursed by Agastya: "Become a serpent, O king! / Having met Yudhiṣṭhira, you will obtain release from the curse."

1.24.s:
evamukte tu muninā sarpatvaṃ sa jagāma vai ..
naṣṭe śakre ca patite nahuṣe pāpaniścaye .. 1.24.10 ..
1.24.d:
एवमुक्ते तु मुनिना सर्पत्वं स जगाम वै ॥
नष्टे शक्रे च पतिते नहुषे पापनिश्चये ॥ 1.24.10 ॥
1.24.m: When this was spoken by the sage, he indeed attained the state of a serpent. / Śakra being lost and Nahuṣa of evil resolve having fallen,

1.24.s:
rajastamobhyāmākrāntā babhūvustridaśālayāḥ ..
tataḥ pravṛttā loke'sminnanāvṛṣṭiḥ sudāruṇā .. 11 ..
1.24.d:
रजस्तमोभ्यामाक्रान्ता बभूवुस्त्रिदशालयाः ॥
ततः प्रवृत्ता लोकेऽस्मिन्ननावृष्टिः सुदारुणा ॥ 11 ॥
1.24.m: the abodes of the gods became overcome by passion and darkness. / Then a terrible drought began in this world.

1.24.s:
durbhikṣamarakau cobhau viṣaṇṇāstridaśālayāḥ ..
naṣṭotsavamahāyajñaṃ nirvaṣaṭkāramaṅgalam .. 12 ..
1.24.d:
दुर्भिक्षमरकौ चोभौ विषण्णास्त्रिदशालयाः ॥
नष्टोत्सवमहायज्ञं निर्वषट्कारमङ्गलम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.24.m: Both famine and plague [arose], and the abodes of the gods were dejected; / great sacrifices and festivals vanished, and auspicious invocations of vaṣaṭ ceased.

1.24.s:
anāvṛṣṭihataṃ sarvaṃ babhūva vasudhātalam ..
kṣutkṣāmamānuṣaprāyaṃ vinaṣṭapaśusañcayam .. 13 ..
1.24.d:
अनावृष्टिहतं सर्वं बभूव वसुधातलम् ॥
क्षुत्क्षाममानुषप्रायं विनष्टपशुसञ्चयम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.24.m: The entire surface of the earth was devastated by drought, / mostly populated by emaciated human beings, its multitude of cattle destroyed,

1.24.s:
kapālāsthisamākīrṇaṃ keśaśaivālasaṃkulam ..
snāyubhagnadvijagaṇaiḥ kravyādairatisaṃkulam .. 14 ..
1.24.d:
कपालास्थिसमाकीर्णं केशशैवालसंकुलम् ॥
स्नायुभग्नद्विजगणैः क्रव्यादैरतिसंकुलम् ॥ 14 ॥
1.24.m: strewn with skulls and bones, tangled with hair like moss, / crowded with carnivorous beasts and flocks of birds whose tendons were broken,

1.24.s:
nirgandhikuṇapākīrṇaṃ śūnyaprāyaṃ vibhīṣaṇam ..
kṣutkṣāmabhūtasaṅghābhyāṃ vinivṛttavaṇikpatham .. 15 ..
1.24.d:
निर्गन्धिकुणपाकीर्णं शून्यप्रायं विभीषणम् ॥
क्षुत्क्षामभूतसङ्घाभ्यां विनिवृत्तवणिक्पथम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.24.m: strewn with foul-smelling corpses, practically empty, terrifying, / with trader paths discontinued, with hordes of creatures emaciated by hunger,

1.24.s:
pranaṣṭakṛṣivārtaṃ ca dātṛbhiśca vivarjitam ..
narake'pi mahāghore nirākrandairjanaiyutaiḥ .. 16 ..
1.24.d:
प्रनष्टकृषिवार्तं च दातृभिश्च विवर्जितम् ॥
नरकेऽपि महाघोरे निराक्रन्दैर्जनैयुतैः ॥ 16 ॥
1.24.m: with agriculture and trade destroyed, abandoned by generous givers, / even like a dreadfully terrible hell filled with lamenting people,

1.24.s:
durlabhānnaṃ nirānandaṃ skandhāsaktakumārakaiḥ ..
itaścetaśca yāsyadbhirdānavairatisaṃkulam .. 17 ..
1.24.d:
दुर्लभान्नं निरानन्दं स्कन्धासक्तकुमारकैः ॥
इतश्चेतश्च यास्यद्भिर्दानवैरतिसंकुलम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.24.m: bereft of food, joyless, with children clinging to shoulders, / crowded with demons wandering hither and thither,

1.24.s:
śuṣkatoyāśayaṃ bhīmaṃ nāmaśeṣamahāpagam ..
tasminkāle mahāghore cotsṛṣṭaniyamā dvijāḥ .. 18 ..
1.24.d:
शुष्कतोयाशयं भीमं नामशेषमहापगम् ॥
तस्मिन्काले महाघोरे चोत्सृष्टनियमा द्विजाः ॥ 18 ॥
1.24.m: its reservoirs dried up, fearful, its great rivers remaining in name only. / In that dreadful time, the twice-born abandoned their observances,

1.24.s:
āryāvartaṃ parityajya mlecchadeśamupāśritāḥ ..
bhakṣyābhakṣyaṃ parityajya kurvāṇāḥ prāṇadhāraṇam .. 19 ..
1.24.d:
आर्यावर्तं परित्यज्य म्लेच्छदेशमुपाश्रिताः ॥
भक्ष्याभक्ष्यं परित्यज्य कुर्वाणाः प्राणधारणम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.24.m: and forsaking Āryāvarta, they took refuge in mleccha territory, / sustaining their life while ignoring what should and should not be eaten.

1.24.s:
prāṇadhāraṇasaktānāṃ kṣudhāvyākulacetasām ..
teṣāṃ brahma tadā naṣṭaṃ dhāvatāṃ ca itastataḥ .. 1.24.20 ..
1.24.d:
प्राणधारणसक्तानां क्षुधाव्याकुलचेतसाम् ॥
तेषां ब्रह्म तदा नष्टं धावतां च इतस्ततः ॥ 1.24.20 ॥
1.24.m: For those intent on sustaining life, their minds agitated by hunger, / their sacred knowledge was destroyed as they ran hither and thither.

1.24.s:
tadā naṣṭeṣu deveṣu mlecchībhūtamidaṃ jagat ..
mlecchībhūte jagatyasminsvadhāsvāhāvivarjitāḥ .. 21 ..
1.24.d:
तदा नष्टेषु देवेषु म्लेच्छीभूतमिदं जगत् ॥
म्लेच्छीभूते जगत्यस्मिन्स्वधास्वाहाविवर्जिताः ॥ 21 ॥
1.24.m: Then, with the gods lost, this world became barbarized. / When this world became barbarized, deprived of svadhā and svāhā,

1.24.s:
yathā martyāstathā jātāḥ sarve te devatāgaṇāḥ ..
kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhaistridaśaiḥ prārthitaśca janārdanaḥ .. 22 ..
1.24.d:
यथा मर्त्यास्तथा जाताः सर्वे ते देवतागणाः ॥
क्षुत्क्षामकण्ठैस्त्रिदशैः प्रार्थितश्च जनार्दनः ॥ 22 ॥
1.24.m: all those hosts of deities became just like mortals. / Janārdana was prayed to by the gods whose throats were withered by hunger.

1.24.s: śakrārthaṃ tridaśā gatvā trailokyahitakāmyayā .. 23 ..
1.24.d: शक्रार्थं त्रिदशा गत्वा त्रैलोक्यहितकाम्यया ॥ 23 ॥
1.24.m: Desiring the welfare of the three worlds, the gods went on Śakra's behalf.

1.24.s:
tānuvāca harirdevaḥ sarve gacchantu mānasam ..
bisataṃtugataṃ śakraṃ tasmāllapsyatha mā ciram .. 24 ..
1.24.d:
तानुवाच हरिर्देवः सर्वे गच्छन्तु मानसम् ॥
बिसतंतुगतं शक्रं तस्माल्लप्स्यथ मा चिरम् ॥ 24 ॥
1.24.m: Lord Hari said to them: "Let all go to Lake Mānasa; / from there you will obtain Śakra, who has entered a lotus fibre, without delay.

1.24.s:
yajatāṃ so'śvamedhena māmeva surasattamāḥ! ..
ahameva kariṣyāmi vipāpmānaṃ biḍaujasam .. 25 ..
1.24.d:
यजतां सोऽश्वमेधेन मामेव सुरसत्तमाः! ॥
अहमेव करिष्यामि विपाप्मानं बिडौजसम् ॥ 25 ॥
1.24.m: Let him worship me alone with a horse sacrifice, O best of gods! / I myself will make Biḍaujas free from sin.

1.24.s: tatkṛtā brahmahatyāṃ tu caturdhā sa kariṣyati .. 26 ..
1.24.d: तत्कृता ब्रह्महत्यां तु चतुर्धा स करिष्यति ॥ 26 ॥
1.24.m: He shall divide that [sin of] killing a brahmin into four parts:

1.24.s:
amedhyakṣepake vahnau pādenaikena yāsyati ..
tathā caikena pādena hyaśucikṣepake jale .. 27 ..
1.24.d:
अमेध्यक्षेपके वह्नौ पादेनैकेन यास्यति ॥
तथा चैकेन पादेन ह्यशुचिक्षेपके जले ॥ 27 ॥
1.24.m: With one portion, it will enter fire when impure substances are thrown into it; / and with one portion, it will enter water when impurity is cast into it;

1.24.s:
pādenaikena ca tathā sarvakāle drumacchidam ..
rajasvalāṃgaṃ pādena tathā caikena yāsyati.. 28 ..
1.24.d:
पादेनैकेन च तथा सर्वकाले द्रुमच्छिदम् ॥
रजस्वलांगं पादेन तथा चैकेन यास्यति॥ 28 ॥
1.24.m: with one portion, it will enter him who cuts down trees at all times; / and with one portion, it will enter the body of a menstruating woman.

1.24.s:
ahamaṃśena yāsyāmi bhūtalaṃ surakāraṇāt ..
naṣṭe ca bhūtale dharmaṃ sthāpayiṣyāmyahaṃ punaḥ .. 29 ..
1.24.d:
अहमंशेन यास्यामि भूतलं सुरकारणात् ॥
नष्टे च भूतले धर्मं स्थापयिष्याम्यहं पुनः ॥ 29 ॥
1.24.m: I will go to the surface of the earth in part for the sake of the gods; / and when [righteousness] is destroyed on the surface of the earth, I will establish dharma anew."

1.24.s:
etatsarvaṃ yathoddiṣṭaṃ devadevena śārṅgiṇā ..
cakrussuragaṇāḥ sarve rājyaṃ cāvāpa vṛtrahā .. 1.24.30 ..
1.24.d:
एतत्सर्वं यथोद्दिष्टं देवदेवेन शार्ङ्गिणा ॥
चक्रुस्सुरगणाः सर्वे राज्यं चावाप वृत्रहा ॥ 1.24.30 ॥
1.24.m: All the hosts of gods did everything just as was instructed / by the god of gods, the bow-holder, and the slayer of Vṛtra regained his kingdom.

1.24.s:
śakreṇa nityaṃ bisatantugena dhyāto mahātmā hariraprameyaḥ ..
hatvāpi kāmena sa vipramukhyaṃ lebhe trilokīṃ punareva tasmāt .. 31 ..
1.24.d:
शक्रेण नित्यं बिसतन्तुगेन ध्यातो महात्मा हरिरप्रमेयः ॥
हत्वापि कामेन स विप्रमुख्यं लेभे त्रिलोकीं पुनरेव तस्मात् ॥ 31 ॥
1.24.m: While residing in the lotus fibre, Śakra constantly meditated upon the high-souled, immeasurable Hari; / therefore, even having willfully slain the foremost of brahmins, he gained the three worlds once again.

1.25.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
brahmaṇo'triḥ sutaḥ śrīmānprabhāvādbrahmaṇā samaḥ ...
prabhākarastasya sutaḥ pitāmahasamo guṇaiḥ ..1..
1.25.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
ब्रह्मणोऽत्रिः सुतः श्रीमान्प्रभावाद्ब्रह्मणा समः ॥।
प्रभाकरस्तस्य सुतः पितामहसमो गुणैः ॥1॥
1.25.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Brahmā's glorious son Atri was equal to Brahmā in majesty; / his son Prabhākara was equal to the Grandfather in virtues,

1.25.s:
svarbhānunā hate sūrye patamāne divo mahīm ..
tamobhibhūte tapasā prabhā yena vivardhitā .. 2 ..
1.25.d:
स्वर्भानुना हते सूर्ये पतमाने दिवो महीम् ॥
तमोभिभूते तपसा प्रभा येन विवर्धिता ॥ 2 ॥
1.25.m: by whom, when the sun was struck by Svarbhānu and was falling from heaven to earth, / overcome by darkness, the light was augmented through austerity.

1.25.s:
svastyastviti sa hovāca patamānaṃ divākaram ..
vacanāttasya brahmarṣeḥ sa papāta divo mahīm ..3..
1.25.d:
स्वस्त्यस्त्विति स होवाच पतमानं दिवाकरम् ॥
वचनात्तस्य ब्रह्मर्षेः स पपात दिवो महीम् ॥3॥
1.25.m: He said, "May there be well-being!" to the falling sun; / by the word of that brahmin-seer, he [prevented him from] falling from heaven to earth.

1.25.s:
atriśreṣṭhāni gotrāṇi yaścakāra mahāyaśāḥ ..
yajñeṣvatrivanaṃ yaśca surairyasya prakīrtitam .. 4 ..
1.25.d:
अत्रिश्रेष्ठानि गोत्राणि यश्चकार महायशाः ॥
यज्ञेष्वत्रिवनं यश्च सुरैर्यस्य प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.25.m: He of great fame established the clans that are foremost among the Atris; / and in sacrifices, he was proclaimed by the gods as the forest of Atri.

1.25.s:
tasya putratvamāpannau janārdanamaheśvarau ..
dattātreyo'tha durvāsā loke khyātimupāgatau .. 5..
1.25.d:
तस्य पुत्रत्वमापन्नौ जनार्दनमहेश्वरौ ॥
दत्तात्रेयोऽथ दुर्वासा लोके ख्यातिमुपागतौ ॥ 5॥
1.25.m: Janārdana and Maheśvara became his sons; / they became famous in the world as Dattātreya and Durvāsas.
Assuming the form of Dattātreya, the blessed slayer of Madhu / taught the Vedas to the brahmins who observed their vows,

1.25.s:
teṣu naṣṭeṣu vedeṣu kriyāsu ca makheṣu ca ..
cāturvaṇye samākīrṇe dharme śithilatāṃ gate .. .. 7 ..
1.25.d:
तेषु नष्टेषु वेदेषु क्रियासु च मखेषु च ॥
चातुर्वण्ये समाकीर्णे धर्मे शिथिलतां गते ॥ ॥ 7 ॥
1.25.m: when those Vedas, rituals, and sacrifices were lost, / when the four classes were intermingled and dharma had become slack,

1.25.s:
abhivardhati cādharme satye naṣṭe'nṛte sthite ..
prajāsu śīryamāṇāsu dharme cākulatāṃ gate .. 8 ..
1.25.d:
अभिवर्धति चाधर्मे सत्ये नष्टेऽनृते स्थिते ॥
प्रजासु शीर्यमाणासु धर्मे चाकुलतां गते ॥ 8 ॥
1.25.m: and when adharma was increasing, truth had perished, falsehood stood firm, / when subjects were decaying and dharma had fallen into confusion.

1.25.s:
sayajñāḥ sakriyā vedāḥ pratyānītā hi tena vai ..
cāturvarṇyamasaṃkīrṇa kṛtaṃ tena mahātmanā ..9 ..
1.25.d:
सयज्ञाः सक्रिया वेदाः प्रत्यानीता हि तेन वै ॥
चातुर्वर्ण्यमसंकीर्ण कृतं तेन महात्मना ॥9 ॥
1.25.m: Indeed, by him the Vedas along with sacrifices and rituals were brought back; / by that great-souled one the fourfold social order was made unmixed.

1.25.s:
durbhikṣamarakau naṣṭau tasmiñjāte mahītale ..
pravavarṣa ca devendraḥ sahasranayanaḥ kṣitau ..1.25.1 0..
1.25.d:
दुर्भिक्षमरकौ नष्टौ तस्मिञ्जाते महीतले ॥
प्रववर्ष च देवेन्द्रः सहस्रनयनः क्षितौ ॥1.25.1 0॥
1.25.m: When he was born upon the surface of the earth, famine and pestilence perished, / and the lord of the gods, the thousand-eyed one, rained down upon the earth.

1.25.s:
bhūya eva jagadvṛttaṃ yathāpūrvaṃ jagatpate ..
pranaṣṭakaluṣe loke sanmārgastheṣu rājasu .. 11 ..
1.25.d:
भूय एव जगद्वृत्तं यथापूर्वं जगत्पते ॥
प्रनष्टकलुषे लोके सन्मार्गस्थेषु राजसु ॥ 11 ॥
1.25.m: Once again the conduct of the world became as it was before, O lord of the world, / when the world was freed of impurity and kings walked on the path of the good,

1.25.s:
yajatsu vipramukhyeṣu tapasyabhirateṣu ca ..
vārtāsakteṣu vaiśyeṣu śuśrūṣuṣvantyajeṣu ca .. 12 ..
1.25.d:
यजत्सु विप्रमुख्येषु तपस्यभिरतेषु च ॥
वार्तासक्तेषु वैश्येषु शुश्रूषुष्वन्त्यजेषु च ॥ 12 ॥
1.25.m: when foremost brahmins sacrificed and were devoted to asceticism, / when vaiśyas were occupied with trade and agriculture, and the lowest-born were eager to serve,

1.25.s:
muditeṣu ca lokeṣu trailokye devasādgate ..
viṣṇorbhāge kṣitigate kārtavīryārjunastadā .. 13 ..
1.25.d:
मुदितेषु च लोकेषु त्रैलोक्ये देवसाद्गते ॥
विष्णोर्भागे क्षितिगते कार्तवीर्यार्जुनस्तदा ॥ 13 ॥
1.25.m: when the worlds rejoiced and the three worlds came under the rule of the gods. / When a portion of Viṣṇu came down to earth, then Kārtavīrya Arjuna,

1.25.s:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi kṛtavānduścaraṃ tapaḥ ..
prayāgavanamāsādya dattātreyāśramaṃ prati ..14..
1.25.d:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि कृतवान्दुश्चरं तपः ॥
प्रयागवनमासाद्य दत्तात्रेयाश्रमं प्रति ॥14॥
1.25.m: having gone to the forest of Prayāga, to the hermitage of Dattātreya, / performed difficult asceticism for ten thousand years.

1.25.s:
ārādhayāmāsa tadā dattaṃ śuśrūṣayā nṛpa..
tena dattavaraścakre sarājyaṃ hatakaṇṭakam ..15..
1.25.d:
आराधयामास तदा दत्तं शुश्रूषया नृप॥
तेन दत्तवरश्चक्रे सराज्यं हतकण्टकम् ॥15॥
1.25.m: Then, O king, he worshipped Datta with service; / granted a boon by him, he made his kingdom free of thorns.

1.25.s:
āryāvarteṣu nirmlecchā kṛtā tena vasundharā ..
tasminrājani dharmajñe daityairdevanipātitaiḥ .. 16 ..
1.25.d:
आर्यावर्तेषु निर्म्लेच्छा कृता तेन वसुन्धरा ॥
तस्मिन्राजनि धर्मज्ञे दैत्यैर्देवनिपातितैः ॥ 16 ॥
1.25.m: By him the earth in the lands of the Āryas was cleared of barbarians. / While that king who knew dharma was ruling, through the Daityas who had been struck down by the gods

1.25.s:
saṃprāptairbhūmipālatvaṃ vasudhā bhārapīḍitā ..
nākapṛṣṭhaṃ yayau śīghraṃ śakradarśanalālasā .. 17..
1.25.d:
संप्राप्तैर्भूमिपालत्वं वसुधा भारपीडिता ॥
नाकपृष्ठं ययौ शीघ्रं शक्रदर्शनलालसा ॥ 17॥
1.25.m: and had attained the status of kings, the earth, oppressed by their burden, / went swiftly to the vault of heaven, longing for the sight of Śakra.

1.25.s:
vajra uvāca ..
āsādyalokaṃ tridiveśvarasya bhāreṇa khinnā vasudhā narendraiḥ ..
kiṃ tatra cakre vada tanmamādya dṛṣṭvā kṣitiṃ yacca cakāra śakraḥ ..18..
1.25.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
आसाद्यलोकं त्रिदिवेश्वरस्य भारेण खिन्ना वसुधा नरेन्द्रैः ॥
किं तत्र चक्रे वद तन्ममाद्य दृष्ट्वा क्षितिं यच्च चकार शक्रः ॥18॥
1.25.m: Vajra said: / Having reached the world of the lord of heaven, being distressed by the burden of the kings, / tell me today what the earth did there, and what Śakra did upon seeing the earth.

1.26.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
nākapṛṣṭhagatā bhūmirdadarśa madhusūdanam ..
ratnāsanagataṃ vīraṃ śriyā paramayā yutam .. 1 ..
1.26.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
नाकपृष्ठगता भूमिर्ददर्श मधुसूदनम् ॥
रत्नासनगतं वीरं श्रिया परमया युतम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.26.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having reached the vault of heaven, the earth saw Madhusūdana, / the hero seated upon a jeweled throne, accompanied by supreme Lakṣmī,

1.26.s:
upāsyamānaṃ tridaśairbhāsayantaṃ sabhāṃ śubhām ..
ādityairvasubhiḥ sādhyairviśvedevairmarudgaṇaiḥ ..2 ..
1.26.d:
उपास्यमानं त्रिदशैर्भासयन्तं सभां शुभाम् ॥
आदित्यैर्वसुभिः साध्यैर्विश्वेदेवैर्मरुद्गणैः ॥2 ॥
1.26.m: attended by the thirty [gods], illuminating the auspicious assembly / together with the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, and the hosts of Maruts,

1.26.s:
rudrairbhṛgvaṅgirobhiśca nāsatyaiśca mahātmabhiḥ ..
ṛṣibhiḥ sūryasaṃkāśaistapasā dyotitaprabhaiḥ .. 3 ..
1.26.d:
रुद्रैर्भृग्वङ्गिरोभिश्च नासत्यैश्च महात्मभिः ॥
ऋषिभिः सूर्यसंकाशैस्तपसा द्योतितप्रभैः ॥ 3 ॥
1.26.m: with the Rudras, the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases, the great-souled Nāsatyas, / and the sages resembling the sun, their splendor shining through asceticism,

1.26.s:
gandharvairapsarobhiśca stūyamānaṃ sahasraśaḥ ..
kirīṭottamasaṃcchannaṃ hārakeyūrabhūṣitam .. 4 ..
1.26.d:
गन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिश्च स्तूयमानं सहस्रशः ॥
किरीटोत्तमसंच्छन्नं हारकेयूरभूषितम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.26.m: praised in thousands by Gandharvas and Apsarases, / covered with an excellent diadem, adorned with necklaces and armlets,

1.26.s:
ratnāṅgadakṛtoddyotaṃ ratnagarbhasamaprabham ..
haricandana digdhāṃgaṃ nīlāmbaradharaṃ harim .. 5 ..
1.26.d:
रत्नाङ्गदकृतोद्द्योतं रत्नगर्भसमप्रभम् ॥
हरिचन्दन दिग्धांगं नीलाम्बरधरं हरिम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.26.m: making brilliance with jeweled armbands, having radiance like that of the ocean, / his limbs smeared with yellow sandalwood, Hari clad in dark blue garments,

1.26.s:
tiryaglalāṭakenā'kṣṇā tṛtīyena virājitam ..
paśyantaṃ sarvalokasya satataṃ dharmakarmaṇī .. 6 ..
1.26.d:
तिर्यग्ललाटकेनाऽक्ष्णा तृतीयेन विराजितम् ॥
पश्यन्तं सर्वलोकस्य सततं धर्मकर्मणी ॥ 6 ॥
1.26.m: shining with a third eye placed horizontally on his forehead, / constantly observing the dharma and actions of all the world.

1.26.s:
viṣṇoracintyamaṅgaṃ tattrailokyasyaiva kāraṇam ..
gobrāhmaṇahitāsaktaṃ dadarśa vasudhā tadā .. 7 ..
1.26.d:
विष्णोरचिन्त्यमङ्गं तत्त्रैलोक्यस्यैव कारणम् ॥
गोब्राह्मणहितासक्तं ददर्श वसुधा तदा ॥ 7 ॥
1.26.m: Then the earth saw that inconceivable body of Viṣṇu, the cause of the three worlds, / intent upon the welfare of cows and brahmins.

1.26.s:
sandhyāsaha samāsīnaṃ śriyā caiva janārdanam ..
taṃ vavande vasumatī daityabhārabharārditā .. 8 ..
1.26.d:
सन्ध्यासह समासीनं श्रिया चैव जनार्दनम् ॥
तं ववन्दे वसुमती दैत्यभारभरार्दिता ॥ 8 ॥
1.26.m: Janārdana seated together with Sandhyā and with Śrī— / to him the earth bowed, afflicted by the heavy weight of the Daityas.

1.26.s:
pādyārghyācamanīyādyaiḥ śakro'pi vasudhāṃ tadā ..
pūjayitvā sukhāsīnāṃ papracchāgamanakriyām .. 9 ..
1.26.d:
पाद्यार्घ्याचमनीयाद्यैः शक्रोऽपि वसुधां तदा ॥
पूजयित्वा सुखासीनां पप्रच्छागमनक्रियाम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.26.m: Then Śakra too, having honored the earth with water for the feet, respectful offering, water for sipping, and the like, / asked her, as she sat comfortably, the purpose of her arrival.

1.26.s: pṛṣṭā śakreṇa sā devī vaktuṃ samupacakrame .. 1.26.10 ..
1.26.d: पृष्टा शक्रेण सा देवी वक्तुं समुपचक्रमे ॥ 1.26.10 ॥
1.26.m: Questioned by Śakra, that goddess began to speak.

1.26.s:
pṛthivyuvāca ..
antarikṣaṃ divaṃ yacca tathaivā'haṃ jagatpate ..
tavāyattā mahābhāga tvaṃ hi deveśvaro vibhuḥ .. 11 ..
1.26.d:
पृथिव्युवाच ॥
अन्तरिक्षं दिवं यच्च तथैवाऽहं जगत्पते ॥
तवायत्ता महाभाग त्वं हि देवेश्वरो विभुः ॥ 11 ॥
1.26.m: The Earth said: / The intermediate space and heaven, and likewise I myself, O lord of the world, / are dependent on you, O illustrious one, for you are the all-powerful lord of the gods.

1.26.s:
tvayi bhāraṃ samāsajya vedābhyasanatatparaḥ ..
sukhamāste praśāntātmā brahmā śubhacaturmukhaḥ .. 12 ..
1.26.d:
त्वयि भारं समासज्य वेदाभ्यसनतत्परः ॥
सुखमास्ते प्रशान्तात्मा ब्रह्मा शुभचतुर्मुखः ॥ 12 ॥
1.26.m: Having placed the burden upon you, intent upon the practice of the Vedas, / the auspicious four-faced Brahmā sits at ease with tranquil mind.

1.26.s:
tvayi bhāraṃ samāsajya devadevo'pi śaṅkaraḥ ..
āste tapasyabhirataḥ kailāse parvatottame .. 13 ..
1.26.d:
त्वयि भारं समासज्य देवदेवोऽपि शङ्करः ॥
आस्ते तपस्यभिरतः कैलासे पर्वतोत्तमे ॥ 13 ॥
1.26.m: Having placed the burden upon you, even Śaṅkara, the god of gods, / sits devoted to asceticism on Kailāsa, the excellent mountain.

1.26.s:
tvayi bhāraṃ samāsajya sukhaṃ svapiti keśavaḥ ..
kṣīrodaśayane nityaṃ śeṣaparyaṅkamā sthitaḥ .. 14 ..
1.26.d:
त्वयि भारं समासज्य सुखं स्वपिति केशवः ॥
क्षीरोदशयने नित्यं शेषपर्यङ्कमा स्थितः ॥ 14 ॥
1.26.m: Having placed the burden upon you, Keśava sleeps happily / in his bed in the Ocean of Milk, always resting on the couch of Śeṣa.

1.26.s:
pitāmahasya yattejaḥ keśavasya śivasya ca ..
sthitaṃ tatsakalaṃ tubhyaṃ tvaṃ hi sarvamayo'rihā .. 15 ..
1.26.d:
पितामहस्य यत्तेजः केशवस्य शिवस्य च ॥
स्थितं तत्सकलं तुभ्यं त्वं हि सर्वमयोऽरिहा ॥ 15 ॥
1.26.m: Whatever majesty belongs to the Grandfather, to Keśava, and to Śiva, / all of that abides in you, for you consist of all, O slayer of foes.

1.26.s:
tvayā vinihato vṛtro balaścāpi niṣūditaḥ ..
tvayā ca nāśitaḥ pākastvayā daityā niṣūditāḥ .. 16 ..
1.26.d:
त्वया विनिहतो वृत्रो बलश्चापि निषूदितः ॥
त्वया च नाशितः पाकस्त्वया दैत्या निषूदिताः ॥ 16 ॥
1.26.m: By you Vṛtra was slain, and Bala was destroyed; / by you Pāka was ruined, and by you the Daityas were killed.

1.26.s:
brahmaṇyastvaṃ śaraṇyastvaṃ praṇatārtivināśanaḥ ..
sahasranayanaḥ śrīmānvajrapāṇirjagatpriyaḥ .. 17 ..
1.26.d:
ब्रह्मण्यस्त्वं शरण्यस्त्वं प्रणतार्तिविनाशनः ॥
सहस्रनयनः श्रीमान्वज्रपाणिर्जगत्प्रियः ॥ 17 ॥
1.26.m: You are devoted to brahmins, you are a refuge, the destroyer of the distress of those who bow to you, / thousand-eyed, glorious, thunderbolt-in-hand, beloved of the world.

1.26.s:
tejasā tapasā yajñaiḥ śrutena ca damena ca ..
tvatto viśiṣṭaṃ loke'sminna paśyāmi śacīpate .. 18 ..
1.26.d:
तेजसा तपसा यज्ञैः श्रुतेन च दमेन च ॥
त्वत्तो विशिष्टं लोकेऽस्मिन्न पश्यामि शचीपते ॥ 18 ॥
1.26.m: In majesty, asceticism, sacrifices, sacred knowledge, and self-restraint, / I see no one superior to you in this world, O lord of Śacī.

1.26.s:
vedeṣu sarahasyeṣu gīyase tvaṃ punaḥpunaḥ ..
vedāḥ pravṛttā yajñārthaṃ tadarthaṃ kratavastathā .. 19 ..
1.26.d:
वेदेषु सरहस्येषु गीयसे त्वं पुनःपुनः ॥
वेदाः प्रवृत्ता यज्ञार्थं तदर्थं क्रतवस्तथा ॥ 19 ॥
1.26.m: In the Vedas along with the secret teachings you are sung again and again; / the Vedas have arisen for the sake of sacrifice, and likewise sacrifices are for your sake.

1.26.s:
ye hatā dānavā yuddhe tvayā śakra punaḥpunaḥ ..
ta ime nṛṣu sambhūtāḥ kārtavīryaṃ samāśritāḥ .. 1.26.20 ..
1.26.d:
ये हता दानवा युद्धे त्वया शक्र पुनःपुनः ॥
त इमे नृषु सम्भूताः कार्तवीर्यं समाश्रिताः ॥ 1.26.20 ॥
1.26.m: Those Dānavas who were slain by you in battle, O Śakra, again and again, / have been born among men, resorting to Kārtavīrya.

1.26.s:
te'dya jātā mama vibho pīḍayanti ca māṃ bhṛśam ..
sā'haṃ bhārasamākrāntā tvāmadya śaraṇaṃ gatā .. 21 ..
1.26.d:
तेऽद्य जाता मम विभो पीडयन्ति च मां भृशम् ॥
साऽहं भारसमाक्रान्ता त्वामद्य शरणं गता ॥ 21 ॥
1.26.m: They are now born from me, O powerful one, and they afflict me exceedingly; / overwhelmed by their burden, I have come to you today for refuge.

1.26.s:
.. śakra uvāca ..
jānāmi bhārakhinnāṃ tvāṃ daityebhyo varavarṇini ..
teṣāṃ gatvā vadhopāyamahaṃ praṣṭāsmi vedhasam .. 22 ..
1.26.d:
॥ शक्र उवाच ॥
जानामि भारखिन्नां त्वां दैत्येभ्यो वरवर्णिनि ॥
तेषां गत्वा वधोपायमहं प्रष्टास्मि वेधसम् ॥ 22 ॥
1.26.m: Śakra said: / I know that you are distressed by the burden from the Daityas, O fair-complexioned one; / going to the Creator, I shall ask the means for their slaying.

1.26.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ityevamuktvā tridaśapradhānaḥ pṛdhvīsameto guruṇā ca rājan ..
yayau sabhāṃ devavarasya tasya pitāmahasyāpratimasya vīraḥ .. 23 ..
1.26.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
इत्येवमुक्त्वा त्रिदशप्रधानः पृध्वीसमेतो गुरुणा च राजन् ॥
ययौ सभां देववरस्य तस्य पितामहस्याप्रतिमस्य वीरः ॥ 23 ॥
1.26.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having spoken thus, the hero, the foremost of the thirty [gods], along with the Earth and with his preceptor, O king, / went to the assembly of that peerless Grandfather, the excellent god.

1.27.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
te sametāḥ samāsādya pitāmahasabhāṃ śubhām ..
padmāsanagataṃ tatra dadṛśuḥ padmasambhavam .. 1 ..
1.27.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
ते समेताः समासाद्य पितामहसभां शुभाम् ॥
पद्मासनगतं तत्र ददृशुः पद्मसम्भवम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.27.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Together having reached the auspicious assembly of the Grandfather, / they saw there the lotus-born one seated upon a lotus seat,

1.27.s:
padmapatrasavarṇāṃgaṃ padmabodhasamaprabham ..
caturvaktraṃ caturvedaṃ caturāśramapūjitam .. 2 ..
1.27.d:
पद्मपत्रसवर्णांगं पद्मबोधसमप्रभम् ॥
चतुर्वक्त्रं चतुर्वेदं चतुराश्रमपूजितम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.27.m: his limbs having the color of a lotus petal, his radiance equal to the blossoming of a lotus, / four-faced, possessing the four Vedas, worshipped by the four stages of life,

1.27.s:
cāturvarṇyadharaṃ devaṃ cāturhotrapravartakam ..
kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ śāntaṃ prabhuṃ prabhavatāmapi .. 3 ..
1.27.d:
चातुर्वर्ण्यधरं देवं चातुर्होत्रप्रवर्तकम् ॥
कृष्णाजिनधरं शान्तं प्रभुं प्रभवतामपि ॥ 3 ॥
1.27.m: the god who maintains the four castes, who sets in motion the duties of the four priests, / wearing a black antelope skin, peaceful, the sovereign even of those with sovereign power,

1.27.s:
svayaṃbhuvamacintyaṃ ca sargasaṃhārakārakam ..
taṃ samāsādya jagatī śakraśca guruṇā saha .. 4 ..
1.27.d:
स्वयंभुवमचिन्त्यं च सर्गसंहारकारकम् ॥
तं समासाद्य जगती शक्रश्च गुरुणा सह ॥ 4 ॥
1.27.m: self-born, inconceivable, the maker of creation and destruction. / Having approached him, the earth and Śakra, together with their preceptor,

1.27.s:
vavanduste mahābhāgaṃ tuṣṭuvuśca jagatprabhum ..
śakrādaya ūcuḥ ..
namaste devadeveśa sṛṣṭisaṃhārakāraṇa! ..
vedamūrte tadādhāra yajña yajñāṃga yajñapa .. 5 ..
1.27.d:
ववन्दुस्ते महाभागं तुष्टुवुश्च जगत्प्रभुम् ॥
शक्रादय ऊचुः ॥
नमस्ते देवदेवेश सृष्टिसंहारकारण! ॥
वेदमूर्ते तदाधार यज्ञ यज्ञांग यज्ञप ॥ 5 ॥
1.27.m: bowed to that illustrious one and praised the sovereign of the world. / Śakra and the others said: / Praise to you, O god, lord of gods, the cause of creation and destruction! / O you whose form is the Veda, its foundation, O sacrifice, limb of sacrifice, protector of sacrifice!

1.27.s:
yajñayone jagadyone sarvasattvābhayaprada ..
prajāpatipate deva jagadbīja namo'stu te .. 6 ..
1.27.d:
यज्ञयोने जगद्योने सर्वसत्त्वाभयप्रद ॥
प्रजापतिपते देव जगद्बीज नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 6 ॥
1.27.m: Source of sacrifice, source of the world, grantor of fearlessness to all beings, / lord of the lords of creatures, O god, seed of the world, praise be to you!

1.27.s:
svayambhuve svayaṃ kartre sarvabhūtāntarātmane ..
sarvabhūtavareṇyāya sarvabhūteśvarāya ca .. 7 ..
1.27.d:
स्वयम्भुवे स्वयं कर्त्रे सर्वभूतान्तरात्मने ॥
सर्वभूतवरेण्याय सर्वभूतेश्वराय च ॥ 7 ॥
1.27.m: [Praise] to the self-born, to the self-maker, to the inner self of all beings, / to the one chosen among all beings, and to the lord of all beings!

1.27.s:
acintyāyā'prameyāya prakāśāya mahātmane ..
tvamasya jagato nāthastvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam .. 8 ..
1.27.d:
अचिन्त्यायाऽप्रमेयाय प्रकाशाय महात्मने ॥
त्वमस्य जगतो नाथस्त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.27.m: [Homage] to the unthinkable, the immeasurable, the light, the Great Self! / You are the lord of this universe; in you everything is established.

1.27.s:
tvayā vinā jagatyasminnānyatkiñcana vidyate ..
indriyāṇīndriyārthāśca tebhyaḥ parataraśca yat .. 9 ..
1.27.d:
त्वया विना जगत्यस्मिन्नान्यत्किञ्चन विद्यते ॥
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थाश्च तेभ्यः परतरश्च यत् ॥ 9 ॥
1.27.m: Without you, nothing else exists in this universe: / the senses and the sense-objects, and that which is higher than them.

1.27.s:
vyaktāvyakto jagannātha tvamevaikaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
tvaṃ tapāṃsi variṣṭhāni kṛcchrāṇi niyamāni ca .. 1.27.10 ..
1.27.d:
व्यक्ताव्यक्तो जगन्नाथ त्वमेवैकः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
त्वं तपांसि वरिष्ठानि कृच्छ्राणि नियमानि च ॥ 1.27.10 ॥
1.27.m: Manifest and unmanifest, O lord of the universe, you alone are proclaimed [to be]. / You are the highest austerities, the arduous penances, and the observances.

1.27.s:
kalāḥ kāṣṭhā muhūrtāśca kālasyāvayavāśca ye ..
kālacakraṃ jagaccakraṃ tvamekaḥ puruṣottamaḥ... 11..
1.27.d:
कलाः काष्ठा मुहूर्ताश्च कालस्यावयवाश्च ये ॥
कालचक्रं जगच्चक्रं त्वमेकः पुरुषोत्तमः॥। 11॥
1.27.m: The kalās, kāṣṭhās, and muhūrtas, and whatever are the divisions of time, / the wheel of time, the wheel of the universe: you alone are the Puruṣottama.

1.27.s:
tvameva varado dātā devaḥ śubhacaturmukhaḥ ..
tvattaḥ prasūtau loke'smindharmarudrau jagatpate .. 12 ..
1.27.d:
त्वमेव वरदो दाता देवः शुभचतुर्मुखः ॥
त्वत्तः प्रसूतौ लोकेऽस्मिन्धर्मरुद्रौ जगत्पते ॥ 12 ॥
1.27.m: You alone are the giver of boons, the bestower, the auspicious four-faced god. / From you, O lord of the universe, Dharma and Rudra were born in this world.

1.27.s:
bhṛgvaṃgirā marīcistu pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ ..
atriścaiva vaśiṣṭhaśca tvayā sṛṣṭā jagatpate .. 13 ..
1.27.d:
भृग्वंगिरा मरीचिस्तु पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः ॥
अत्रिश्चैव वशिष्ठश्च त्वया सृष्टा जगत्पते ॥ 13 ॥
1.27.m: Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Marīci, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, / Atri, and Vasiṣṭha were created by you, O lord of the universe.

1.27.s:
sanatkumāro bhagavānsanakaśca sanandanaḥ ..
ākṛtiśca ruciḥ śraddhā tvayā deva vinirmitā .. 14 ..
1.27.d:
सनत्कुमारो भगवान्सनकश्च सनन्दनः ॥
आकृतिश्च रुचिः श्रद्धा त्वया देव विनिर्मिता ॥ 14 ॥
1.27.m: Lord Sanatkumāra, Sanaka, and Sanandana, / Ākṛti, Ruci, and Śraddhā were fashioned by you, O god.

1.27.s:
pūrvātte vadanājjātamṛgvedamamṛtaprabham ..
dakṣiṇādvadanājjātaṃ yajurvedaṃ tathaiva ca .. 15 ..
1.27.d:
पूर्वात्ते वदनाज्जातमृग्वेदममृतप्रभम् ॥
दक्षिणाद्वदनाज्जातं यजुर्वेदं तथैव च ॥ 15 ॥
1.27.m: From your eastern face was born the Ṛgveda, shining with nectar; / and from your southern face was born the Yajurveda in the same way;

1.27.s:
paścimādvadanājjātaṃ sāmavedaṃ tathā tava ..
uttarādvadanājjātamatharvāgirasaṃ śubham .. 16 ..
1.27.d:
पश्चिमाद्वदनाज्जातं सामवेदं तथा तव ॥
उत्तराद्वदनाज्जातमथर्वागिरसं शुभम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.27.m: and from your western face was born your Sāmaveda; / from your northern face was born the auspicious Atharvāngirasa.

1.27.s:
brāhmaṇāste mukhājjātā bāhubhyāṃ kṣattriyāstathā ..
ūrudvayāttathā vaiśyāḥ padbhyāṃ śūdrāstathaiva ca .. 17 ..
1.27.d:
ब्राह्मणास्ते मुखाज्जाता बाहुभ्यां क्षत्त्रियास्तथा ॥
ऊरुद्वयात्तथा वैश्याः पद्भ्यां शूद्रास्तथैव च ॥ 17 ॥
1.27.m: The brahmins were born from your mouth, and likewise the kṣatriyas from your two arms; / similarly, the vaiśyas from your two thighs, and the śūdras likewise from your feet.

1.27.s:
vidyuto'śanimeghāśca rohitendradhanūṃṣi ca ..
tvattaḥ prabho prasūtāni praviśanti tathā tvayi .. 18 ..
1.27.d:
विद्युतोऽशनिमेघाश्च रोहितेन्द्रधनूंषि च ॥
त्वत्तः प्रभो प्रसूतानि प्रविशन्ति तथा त्वयि ॥ 18 ॥
1.27.m: Lightnings, thunderbolts, clouds, red rainbows, and rainbows, / having been produced from you, O lord, enter likewise into you.

1.27.s:
svayambhūrbhagavānviṣṇurdevadevaḥ sanātanaḥ ..
nāmamātravibhedena mohayasyakhilaṃ jagat .. 19 ..
1.27.d:
स्वयम्भूर्भगवान्विष्णुर्देवदेवः सनातनः ॥
नाममात्रविभेदेन मोहयस्यखिलं जगत् ॥ 19 ॥
1.27.m: [As] the self-born, the lord, Viṣṇu, the god of gods, the eternal one, / by a mere distinction of names you delude the entire universe.

1.27.s:
tvattejasā mayā daityā ye yuddhe vinipātitāḥ ..
